the **platform binding**: which key arrives as an App Service application setting, which arrives as a
Key Vault reference, and which are marked slot-scoped so a swap does not repoint an environment
([06 §7.5](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)). 06 refers to these settings **by the key names below**;
it does not restate their types, and this document does not restate its slot scoping.

**Configuration admission is stated per process, because there are three processes and they do not admit
the same names.** An earlier form of this section published a single five-name table and called it "the
closed set of channels — five, and no sixth". **That claim was false, and it was falsified by this
document's own text**: the operator console admits `MIGRATE_SOURCE_CONNECTION`,
`MIGRATE_TARGET_CONNECTION`, `MUSICSTORE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `EXPECTED_ENVIRONMENT`, `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT`,
`ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` and a switch grammar; the test host admits the whole `Tests__*` tree plus
`TESTS_ENGINE_IMAGE` and `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD`; and the web application admits `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` and
eleven configuration sections. A table of five names could not be closed over that, so a reader who
believed it would treat every legitimate name outside it as a defect.

**The admission set is therefore published as a per-process matrix, and *that* is what is closed.** One
row per process. Each row names **every** key the process admits, the **binding** each key arrives as, the
**channel** it arrives through, and the **precedence** of that channel within the process. A key absent
from a process's row is **not admitted by that process** — the process does not read it, and a section
that appears to need it is describing either a key already in the row under another name, or a key
belonging to a different process, or a defect. The two tables that follow are one contract: the first
enumerates the **cross-boundary value channels** — the names by which a value is handed from an operator, a
release pipeline or a test fixture into a running process, which is the subset that carries secrets and
connections — and the second is the per-process admission matrix over the whole key space.

| # | Channel | Form the operator sets | Supplied by | Read by | Secret |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection` | `appsettings.json` key, or the environment override `ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection` | The platform binding of [06 §8.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) for the web application; the invoking shell or pipeline step for the operator tool | The web application's two `DbContext` registrations (section [4.5](#45-two-contexts-two-migration-sets-two-history-tables)), the distributed cache (section [6.3](#63-session-and-cart-identity)), the key repository (section [4.9](#49-the-data-protection-key-store--applicationdbcontext-owns-it)), and the operator tool's `admin` verb (section [10.2](#102-the-target-toolsprovision-admin-and-five-required-properties)) | No — the value carries no password under the managed-identity connection mode the same section validates |
| 2 | `MIGRATE_SOURCE_CONNECTION` | Environment variable only, scoped to the single invocation | The release pipeline step or operator session that runs a data verb | The operator tool's source-reading verbs (section [5.6](#56-the-data-migration-executor)) | No |
| 3 | `MIGRATE_TARGET_CONNECTION` | Environment variable only, scoped to the single invocation | The same | The operator tool's target-writing verbs, including the cache-table and key-table provisioning steps of section [5.3](#53-who-applies-ddl-and-in-what-order) | No |
| 4 | `MUSICSTORE_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | Environment variable scoped to the single invocation, **or** an echo-disabled terminal prompt when the variable is absent and a terminal is attached | The operator, at the moment of the invocation | The operator tool's `admin` verb, and nothing else (section [10.2](#102-the-target-toolsprovision-admin-and-five-required-properties)) | **Yes** — and it is the only secret in the set. It is never an argument, never a file, and never logged |
| 5 | `Seeding:Enabled` and `Seeding:AllowedDatabaseNamePattern` | `appsettings.json` keys, or the environment overrides `Seeding__Enabled` and `Seeding__AllowedDatabaseNamePattern` | The non-production environment's own configuration, never a production one | The seeding guard's checks 2 and 3 (section [5.4](#54-seeding--the-guard-fails-closed-on-three-checks)) | No |

Two properties follow from the table and are stated here so no later section re-derives them. **No
secret is ever a command-line argument** — channel 4 is the only secret in this table and it has no
argument form, so the prohibition is a property of the contract rather than a rule anybody has to
remember. And **when the acceptance matrix of section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) invokes the published
operator bytes, the connection and secret values it supplies are these five names and no others**; a
matrix row supplying a connection or a secret under any other name is a defect in the row. The matrix
additionally sets the operator console's non-secret environment names and the test host's own `Tests__*`
keys, which are **not** channels in this table's sense and are enumerated in the per-process matrix below.

**The per-process admission matrix. Three processes, and every key each one admits.**

| Process | Keys it admits, in full | Binding | Channel | Precedence within the process |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **The web application** (`src/MvcMusicStore`) | `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`; `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection`; and **every member row of the twenty-three options sections enumerated in the sections table below** — `Identity`, `Authentication:Cookie`, `Session`, `Antiforgery`, `DataProtection`, `SqlIdentity`, `Expected`, `Telemetry`, `Site`, `Diagnostics`, `HealthProbe`, `Logging`, `Data`, `Cart`, `Checkout`, `Paging`, `Caching`, `Display`, `Hsts`, `Ingress`, `RateLimiting`, `Security`, `Localization`. **The enumeration is that table, member by member — each row naming the site that enumerates its members — and the admitted set is exactly those members plus the two names above** — a section prefix is not an admission, so a key under one of these prefixes that no member-enumerating site names is *not* admitted and fails validation as an unknown member. The framework's `Kestrel` schema is admitted in Development only. **It does not admit** `Seeding:Enabled`, `Seeding:AllowedDatabaseNamePattern`, `Seeding:CommandTimeoutSeconds`, `Load:BatchSize`, `Load:CommandTimeoutSeconds`, `ProvisionAdmin:Username`, `ProvisionAdmin:Role`, `MIGRATE_SOURCE_CONNECTION`, `MIGRATE_TARGET_CONNECTION`, `MUSICSTORE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `EXPECTED_ENVIRONMENT`, `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT`, `TESTS_ALIAS_KEY`, `TESTS_ENGINE_IMAGE`, `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD` or any `Tests__*` key — each named individually, because "does not admit `Seeding:*`" is a pattern and a pattern cannot close a set. **Two names that look like keys and are not**, listed here because a reader hunting for them in the sections table would otherwise conclude the set is short: `Configuration:HostRole`, which is the *name the aggregate failure message uses* for the host-role signal and is resolved as a registered service through `GetService<IHostRoleSignal>()` rather than read from configuration at all, and `AllowedHosts`, the framework's own host-filtering key, which this application leaves unset in every file and every environment so that `Site:Hosts` is the single declaration of the host set | `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` binds to `HostApplicationBuilderSettings.EnvironmentName` and is **not** a configuration key; every other name binds to an options type in the sections table below, validated at startup, **except** the five sections that table marks as read once in the composition root; `Kestrel` and `Logging` bind to framework schemas. **Two further environment variables are read by name and are not configuration keys either**: `WEBSITE_INSTANCE_ID` and `CONTAINER_APP_REPLICA_NAME`, the platform instance identifiers the diagnostic endpoint of section [2.5.1](#251-the-instance-verification-route-and-why-it-is-not-a-fourth-health-endpoint) reads through `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable` in that order. They are the platform's to set and the application's to read; neither is ever defaulted or computed | `appsettings.json`, `appsettings.{Environment}.json`, user secrets in Development only, environment variables. **No command-line provider at all** — the builder is `WebApplication.CreateBuilder()` with no `args`, per the host table below | Four sources, later wins: 1 `appsettings.json`, 2 `appsettings.{Environment}.json`, 3 user secrets (Development only), 4 environment variables — which is the platform's injection layer and therefore the highest, so a Key Vault reference outranks every committed file |
| **The operator console** (`tools/provision-admin`) | `MIGRATE_SOURCE_CONNECTION`; `MIGRATE_TARGET_CONNECTION`; `MUSICSTORE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; `ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection`; `Seeding__Enabled`; `Seeding__AllowedDatabaseNamePattern`; `EXPECTED_ENVIRONMENT`; `EXPECTED_SQL_SERVER`, `EXPECTED_SQL_DATABASE` and `EXPECTED_DISCRIMINATOR`, which carry the same three expected values the web application's `Expected` section carries but are **read directly by name into typed fields and bound to no options section at all** — which is why the `Expected` section itself stays in this row's exclusion list rather than being admitted under an alias; `MUSICSTORE_AUDIT_ACTOR`, the invocation-scoped actor channel section [10.2](#102-the-target-toolsprovision-admin-and-five-required-properties)'s actor rule requires, named here because an unnamed channel cannot be set by a pipeline; `TESTS_ALIAS_KEY`, admitted **only** so that a suite-launched invocation resolves the same alias key the test host uses (section [12.9](#129-sensitive-test-data-diagnostics-and-redaction)) and absent from every deployed invocation; An earlier form of this row listed only nine, omitting `--model-overrides` and `--authorized-by` — which would have made `diff-schema --model-overrides` and `accept-run --authorized-by` unadmitted tokens on the two verbs whose closed sets require them. **It admits, in addition, every member of every options type the shared registration surface binds** — the twenty-three sections the web row names, member by member exactly as the sections table below enumerates them, each in its `<Section>__<Member>` environment form. That is not a widening for its own sake: step 2 of section [10.2](#102-the-target-toolsprovision-admin-and-five-required-properties) calls `Program.AddMusicStoreServices`, which binds **and validates** all of them in this process too, so property 2b's requirement that the invocation supply every unconditionally required member of every one of them is only satisfiable if those members are admissible here. An earlier form of this row **excluded** twenty-two of those sections by name, which made the tool unstartable rather than tightly scoped — `Validate()` would fail on the first required member no channel could set — and that exclusion is withdrawn. **It does not admit** any `Tests__*` key, the framework's `Kestrel` schema — this process binds no server, so the schema has no consumer here — or any name neither listed in this row nor enumerated as a member by the sections table below | **Every listed name has exactly one binding, and they are given individually rather than as groups.** Read **directly by name** into typed fields on the parsed invocation, and deliberately **not** configuration keys — which is why no prefix-scanning environment source exists: `MIGRATE_SOURCE_CONNECTION`, `MIGRATE_TARGET_CONNECTION`, `MUSICSTORE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `MUSICSTORE_AUDIT_ACTOR`, `TESTS_ALIAS_KEY`, `EXPECTED_SQL_SERVER`, `EXPECTED_SQL_DATABASE`, `EXPECTED_DISCRIMINATOR`, `EXPECTED_ENVIRONMENT`, `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` and `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT` — the last three by the pre-parse, which requires the two environment names to be present and equal and passes the agreed value to `HostApplicationBuilderSettings.EnvironmentName`, and compares it against `EXPECTED_ENVIRONMENT`. Bound to the framework's own schema: `Logging`. Arriving as **configuration**, through an **explicit in-memory collection built from the admitted names above and no scan**: `ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection` → `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection`, `Seeding__Enabled` → `Seeding:Enabled`, `Seeding__AllowedDatabaseNamePattern` → `Seeding:AllowedDatabaseNamePattern`, `Load__CommandTimeoutSeconds` → `Load:CommandTimeoutSeconds`, `Seeding__CommandTimeoutSeconds` → `Seeding:CommandTimeoutSeconds`, every `<Section>__<Member>` name of the sections table's members, and `Load:BatchSize` — which is written in colon form because the `--batch` switch is its only producer and it never arrives as an environment variable at all. **The collection's name list is the closed union of this row's own names and that table's member enumeration**, read one name at a time from `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable`, which is what keeps "no scan" true while still admitting every member the shared surface validates: a name absent from both lists is never looked up, so it cannot reach configuration however it is spelled. **Exactly four of the eleven switches arrive as configuration** through `AddCommandLine` over **the pre-parse's normalized pairs**, never over the raw `args` — `--username`, `--role`, `--report-dir` and `--batch`, the four rule 2's table gives a binding target. **The other seven reach no provider at all**: `--rotate-credential`, `--begin-run` and `--resume` are stripped as valueless flags, and `--store`, `--run-id`, `--model-overrides` and `--authorized-by` are recorded as invocation intent on the tool's own parsed-invocation record, which is what keeps this row's key set closed while the switch set is larger than it | Environment variables read by name; That is why no value in this row is ever described as arriving from one, and why row 83 `83b` of section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) exists as the executable proof rather than the claim being left to inspection: it plants the file beside the published assembly, where the content root points, and requires the run's behaviour to be identical |
| **The test host** (`src/MvcMusicStore.Tests`) | `Tests__Run__Id`; `Tests__Run__ArtifactPath`; `Tests__Baseline__LegacyBuildOutput`; `Tests__Baseline__DeployRoot`; `Tests__Baseline__LocalDbInstance`; `Tests__Baseline__IisExpressPath`; `Tests__Baseline__RecordPath`; `Tests__Target__ProvisionAdminPath`; `Tests__Target__EngineContainerId`; `Tests__Target__EngineConnectionString`; `Tests__Deployed__BaseAddress`; `TESTS_ENGINE_IMAGE`; `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD`; **`TESTS_ALIAS_KEY`** — the alias key of section [12.9](#129-sensitive-test-data-diagnostics-and-redaction), named there rather than described; plus `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` for the host it builds. **It does not admit** `MUSICSTORE_ADMIN_PASSWORD` or any `MIGRATE_*` variable **as its own configuration** — it *sets* those in the environment of the operator-console child processes it launches, which is a different thing and is what the first table's "supplied by" column means by a test fixture | The `Tests__*` tree binds to the fixture options types of section [12.6](#126-the-test-project-the-system-under-test-and-the-host-wiring). `TESTS_ENGINE_IMAGE` and `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD` are read directly by the engine-acquisition script and are never configuration keys of the system under test. `TESTS_ALIAS_KEY` is read directly by name from the environment the platform secret store injects it into, never from configuration, and the suite passes the **same** variable through to every operator-console child process it launches so that a report and a test failure concerning one account carry the same alias | Environment variables, and — for the system under test only — an **in-memory collection the fixture supplies to `WebApplicationFactory`** | For the fixture: environment variables only. For the system under test it hosts: the web application's four sources, **plus** the fixture's in-memory collection added **last** and therefore highest, which is how a test points the system under test at its own acquired engine |

**Why the matrix is closed and the five-name table was not.** The five names are a **kind** — a connection
or a secret crossing a process boundary — and a kind cannot be closed over a key space that also contains
environment names, switch operands, fixture paths and options sections. The matrix closes the key space
itself, per process, which is the only unit over which "admitted" is decidable: a process either reads a
name or it does not.

**The sections, and the type bound to each.** Every options type is bound once, in stage 1 item 1 of
section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order), and resolved by constructor injection thereafter.
No component reads `IConfiguration` directly — that is the
habit `ConfigurationManager.AppSettings` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.App.cs:23-24]
represents and the whole reason section
[3.1](#31-configuration-webconfig-becomes-appsettingsjson-read-through-iconfiguration) requires the
options pattern.

| Configuration section | Options type | Consumed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ConnectionStrings` | `ConnectionStringOptions` — one string member, bound from `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection` so the value is validated once rather than at each of its three consumers | Both `DbContext` registrations (section [4.5](#45-two-contexts-two-migration-sets-two-history-tables)), the distributed cache (section [6.3](#63-session-and-cart-identity)) and the key repository (section [4.9](#49-the-data-protection-key-store--applicationdbcontext-owns-it)) |
| `Identity` | `IdentityPolicyOptions` | The Identity registration, whose values are section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled)'s |
| `Authentication:Cookie` | `AuthenticationCookieOptions` | The cookie handler (section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled)) |
| `Session` | `SessionPolicyOptions` | `AddSession` (section [6.3](#63-session-and-cart-identity)) |
| `Antiforgery` | `AntiforgeryPolicyOptions` | `AntiforgeryOptions` (section [7.4](#74-problem-three--cart-removal-posts-without-a-form)) |

**Twenty-seven rows, counted one way so the count is checkable, and in three binding kinds rather than
two.** **Twenty** name a section whose *whole* binding is an options type this document defines;
**five** — `Hsts`, `Ingress`, `RateLimiting`, `Security` and `Localization` — are read **once in the
composition root** and pushed into a framework options type, which is not a violation of the
no-direct-`IConfiguration` rule below because that rule governs *components*, and `Program` is the
composition root rather than a component; and **two** are bound by a framework schema — `Logging`, over
which this document adds only a validation view, and `Kestrel`, which has no custom type at all.
20 + 5 + 2 = 27. `Diagnostics`, `HealthProbe` and `Security:EventLog` are the newest of the twenty and the
only three another deliverable asked for: [06 §8.3.1.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires the
first, its entire content is one optional boolean, and it changes no validation this section already
performs;
[06 §9.3.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md#readiness-checks)'s timeout hierarchy owns every value the
second carries, which is precisely why the second exists as a section rather than as ten constants this
document would have had to restate to compile; and
[09 §6.8.1](09-security-assessment.md) owns the third's single member, with
[06 §9.3](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owning its delivery.

**Twelve of these rows were added to close the admission set rather than to add configuration**, and
saying so is the point: `Data`, `Cart`, `Checkout`, `Paging`, `Caching`, `Display`, `Hsts`, `Ingress`,
`RateLimiting`, `Security`, `Localization` and `HealthProbe` each carry keys **this document already
specified at their owning sites** — the timeout table of section
[4.12](#412-resiliency-timeouts-cancellation-and-async-data-access), the list endpoints of section
[4.11](#411-result-set-bounds-and-per-request-query-cost), the cache of section
[8.2](#82-child-actions--three-view-components) among them, and the probe budgets section
[2.5](#25-the-health-endpoints--the-application-half-of-the-readiness-contract) requires as
`IOptions<HealthProbeOptions>` the twelfth — while the matrix below admitted only eleven
sections. A key the application requires and the matrix does not admit is not a closed set; it is a
start-up failure waiting for the first deployment that sets it. The defaults and the owners stay where
they are, because one fact has one owner: these rows name the **section, its binding and its
member-enumerating site**, and restate no value.

**`Security:EventLog` is a thirteenth admission-closing row, and it is worth separating from the twelve
because its provenance is the opposite of theirs.** The twelve carry keys this document had already
specified somewhere and merely failed to admit. This one carries a key **this document never specified at
all**: `SubjectPseudonymKey` is [09 §6.8.1](09-security-assessment.md)'s, delivered by
[06 §9.3](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md), and read at run time by the writer of the reserved
security-event category `MvcMusicStore.Security.Events` — the category whose spelling is
[06 §9.6.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) entry 3's and whose level the logging table below pins
explicitly at `Information`. A key another deliverable owns is the
easiest kind for a closed set to miss, because nothing in this document's own prose would have prompted a
reader to look for it — which is why it is named here rather than left to the matrix to reject on the
first deployment that sets it.

**`ConnectionStrings` — one key, and only one.**

| Key | CLR type | Required | Default when absent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection` | `string` | **Yes** | **None. An absent value fails the start** |

**The key's name is `DefaultConnection` because that is the name the source already uses, and the
target story is therefore "same key, new provider" rather than a rename nobody asked for.**
`ApplicationDbContext` passes `base("DefaultConnection")` explicitly
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/IdentityModels.cs:10-15], so the literal is grounded in the migration
source rather than invented here — which is why every consumer in this document, every operator verb of
section [10.2](#102-the-target-toolsprovision-admin-and-five-required-properties), the test host of
section [12.6](#126-the-test-project-the-system-under-test-and-the-host-wiring) and the hosting
settings [06 §6.1.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) supplies all name **this one key** and no
other. It is stated once, here, and no other passage in this document offers a second spelling.

Both contexts read this **same** key, because both target one database (section
[4.5](#45-two-contexts-two-migration-sets-two-history-tables)); the second EF 6 connection name
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Web.config:13] is **not** reproduced, so there is no second key for a
deployment to get half-right. The string's **content** — host, database, authentication mode and the
absence of any credential in it — is [06 §6.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s and is not
restated here. **The committed `appsettings.json` carries no `ConnectionStrings` entry at all**; see the
precedence rules below.

**The string is validated at start, on five properties, and the validation never echoes it.** "Required"
on a connection string means only that some text arrived; the five checks below are what make the arrival
meaningful, and each has a failure this application would otherwise discover later and less clearly. They
run in an `IValidateOptions<ConnectionStringOptions>` — the one-member type that carries the value — under
`ValidateOnStart`, so all five are decided before the first request. Because section
[2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order)'s shared half registers this same validated type, they are
also decided inside `tools/provision-admin` before it opens a connection — by way of the **explicit**
`IStartupValidator.Validate()` call that section
[10.2](#102-the-target-toolsprovision-admin-and-five-required-properties) assertion 2 requires, since a
console command that only builds a host has not validated anything. That is why the accepted modes below
are enumerated **per invocation** and not only per environment.

| Check | Rule | Why it is a start-time check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Present** | Non-null and non-whitespace | Without it the failure is the first database touch, which on a warmed deployment may be a real user's request |
| **Parseable** | It constructs a `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.SqlConnectionStringBuilder` without throwing | A malformed keyword is a typo, and a typo caught at start is a failed deployment rather than a failed checkout. The builder is strict about this: an unrecognised keyword throws `ArgumentException: Keyword not supported`, so the check is real rather than nominal |
| **Authenticates in a mode this invocation may use** | **The row is selected first and the string is checked against that row alone.** The selector is the non-forgeable host-role signal below together with the resolved environment and the presence of the test signal; it yields **exactly one** row of the accepted-mode table, and the parsed builder's `Authentication`, `UserID`, `Password`, `IntegratedSecurity`, `Encrypt` and `TrustServerCertificate` must then satisfy **that** row. Failing it fails the start; there is no fall-through to another row | The dangerous failure here is not a malformed string but a **well-formed one from another path** — a SQL credential this design does not manage, or a mode that authenticates as something other than this environment's identity. Both would work, against the wrong principal, so the refusal has to precede the first use. **Select-then-check rather than search-for-a-match** is what makes that true even when two rows' shapes overlap, which `M1` and `M3` provably do |
| **Names the expected server and database** | The parsed `DataSource` and `InitialCatalog` equal `Expected:SqlServer` and `Expected:SqlDatabase` — compared as **parsed fields**, ordinal case-insensitively, with a leading `tcp:` and a trailing `,1433` normalized away first. **Deployed environments only**: both expected members are absent under `Development` and under the test fixture (below), where the check does not run because there is nothing environment-defined to compare against | A deployment pointed at a neighbouring environment's database is the failure that produces no error at all — it reads and writes successfully, in the wrong place. [06 §9.3.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s pre-traffic gate catches it at swap warm-up; this catches it at start, including on the invocations no swap covers |
| **Carries no unresolved secret reference** | The raw value does not begin with `@Microsoft.KeyVault(` | [06 §8.4.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) records the platform mechanic: an unresolvable Key Vault reference is **passed through as that literal string** rather than failing the platform. The check is this document's half of that contract |

**The accepted modes, enumerated — because "the string carries no credential" is not a rule this design
can hold.** The deployed connection **does** carry a `User Id`: it is how a *specific* user-assigned
identity is selected, and [06 §6.1.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) fixes the exact keyword form.
Development reaches a local instance by integrated security (the `appsettings.Development.json` scoping
table below), and the test fixture reaches a disposable instance of its own. A validator written as
"`UserID` empty, `Password` empty, `IntegratedSecurity` false" would therefore reject the two
configurations that must pass and leave the third undefined. The rule is an explicitly closed set of
four modes instead — **one of which is selected before the string is examined**, by the function stated
immediately after the table — and a string that does not satisfy **the selected one** fails the start,
with no fall-through to any other row:

| Mode | Where it is the accepted mode | `Authentication` | `UserID` | `Password` | `IntegratedSecurity` | Transport |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **M1 — deployed managed identity** | The web host in **every** environment that is not `Development`, on both slots | `ActiveDirectoryManagedIdentity` **or** `ActiveDirectoryMSI` — nothing else | **Required**, and equal to `SqlIdentity:ClientId` after both are parsed as `Guid`s | **Must be empty** | **Must be false** | `Encrypt` true and `TrustServerCertificate` false |
| **M2 — local development** | The web host under `Development` only | `NotSpecified` or `ActiveDirectoryDefault` | Empty | **Must be empty** | **Permitted true** — this is the mode M1 forbids, and the only place it is legal | `Encrypt` true, and `TrustServerCertificate` true **only** under the single certificate-validation exception stated below this table — this row invokes that exception and defines none of its own, so its boundary is that paragraph's local-instance boundary and against any other host the M1 transport rule applies |
| **M3 — the operator and release invocations** | `tools/provision-admin` and the data-load steps of the procedure of section [5.1.2](#512-how-the-load-actually-runs--the-executable-contract), in any environment | **`ActiveDirectoryManagedIdentity` or `ActiveDirectoryMSI`**, with **`ActiveDirectoryWorkloadIdentity`** as the single permitted fallback — the one flow [06 §6.1.1.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) selects for the deployment principal. **`ActiveDirectoryDefault` is rejected here**, because that document prohibits it on the release path: it resolves whichever credential the host happens to offer, which is the opposite of naming a principal | **Required**, and parseable as a `Guid` — it is the **deployment** identity's client ID, not the site's, so it is not compared against `SqlIdentity:ClientId` and is instead confirmed at the database by the `USER_NAME()` assertion of section [5.1.2](#512-how-the-load-actually-runs--the-executable-contract) | **Must be empty** | **Must be false** | As M1 |
| **M4 — the test fixture** | The in-process test host of section [12.3](#123-three-problems-that-must-be-handled-explicitly), and nowhere else | `NotSpecified` for the local container, `ActiveDirectoryDefault` for the throwaway managed database — permitted **here only**, because a fixture provisioning its own disposable database is not the release path [06 §6.1.1.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) prohibits it on, and it has no declared principal to name | Permitted for the container | **Permitted for the container only**, and only a credential the fixture generated for that run | Must be false | `Encrypt` true, and `TrustServerCertificate` true for the container's self-signed certificate **under the single certificate-validation exception stated below this table**, which this row invokes rather than restates; the throwaway managed database is not a local instance and is therefore outside it, taking the M1 transport rule |

**`M1` and `M3` are not distinguishable by the string, and that is a defect in an earlier formulation of
this section rather than a subtlety of it.** Read the two rows: both accept
`ActiveDirectoryManagedIdentity`, both require a `UserID` that parses as a `Guid`, both require an empty
`Password`, both require `IntegratedSecurity` false and both require the same transport. `M1` additionally
requires that the `UserID` equal `SqlIdentity:ClientId`; the `M3` row above says of the same member "it is
the **deployment** identity's client ID, not the site's, so it is **not** compared against
`SqlIdentity:ClientId`". So a string carrying a managed-identity authentication, a `Guid` `UserID`, no
password, `Encrypt` true and `TrustServerCertificate` false, alongside a present-and-equal
`SqlIdentity:ClientId`, **satisfies both rows at once**. Under a
validator that searched the table for a matching row, that string had two answers and the table's own
"exactly one row" rule was unsatisfiable — and the consequences run in both directions. The **web** host
could be handed a release-shaped string and admit it under `M3`'s laxer identity rule, so a site would
start authenticating as the **deployment** principal, which holds DDL rights the runtime identity is
deliberately denied. And the **operator** invocation could be admitted under `M1`, whose rule compares the
deployment identity's client ID against `SqlIdentity:ClientId` — a member that names the *site's* identity
— so a correct release either fails for the wrong reason or passes while comparing two unrelated values.

**What the earlier formulation was missing is not a rule but a *fact*: nothing told the validator which
host it was running in.** "Selected by … which host is running" named a discriminator that did not exist.
`IHostEnvironment` supplies the environment and nothing supplies the role, so the validator had only the
string, and the string cannot say. The fix is the same shape as `M4`'s below and is introduced for the same
reason: a **composition-provided signal that no configuration provider can produce.**

| Element | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| The signal | `IHostRoleSignal`, an interface **declared** in the application at `Services/IHostRoleSignal.cs` — **the same folder `ITestConnectionModeSignal` is declared in**, and both are named by their own enumerated rows in [04 §12.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s closed map, so **no new folder is added** and the map's row fixes the path while this row fixes the member. It exposes one member, `HostRole Role { get; }`, over a closed two-value enum: `HostRole.Web` and `HostRole.Operator`. There is no third value and no `Unknown` — an unset role is an absent registration, which is handled below rather than represented |
| Who registers it | **Each composition root, explicitly, and never the shared half.** `Program.cs` registers `HostRole.Web`; `tools/provision-admin/Program.cs` registers `HostRole.Operator`, immediately after its `AddMusicStoreServices` call. It is **deliberately absent from `AddMusicStoreServices`** (section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order)) — a shared registration would have to pick one value, and picking one is exactly the mistake: the shared half is shared precisely because it does not know which host it is composing |
| Why it cannot be forged | It is a **service descriptor**. The configuration system produces keys and values; it cannot add a descriptor to an `IServiceCollection`. A platform application setting, an environment variable, a Key Vault reference, a release-step override and a command-line argument are all equally powerless against it. That is the same argument `M4`'s gate rests on, and it is the only argument available here — **configuration cannot be allowed to select the mode, because configuration is the thing being validated.** A mode selected by a configuration key would let the value under scrutiny nominate the rules it is scrutinised by |
| How the validator reads it | `GetService<IHostRoleSignal>()` on the `IServiceProvider` the one `IValidateOptions<ConnectionStringOptions>` already takes — the same accessor and the same reason as `ITestConnectionModeSignal` below. **Null is a failure, not a default**, and this is where it differs from that signal: a missing test signal is the ordinary deployed case, whereas a missing host-role signal is a **composition defect** in a root this document specifies. It fails the start as `Configuration:HostRole` "no host role was registered by the composition root", named in the aggregated `OptionsValidationException` like every other member. `GetRequiredService` is not used, so the failure arrives as a validation failure the operator can read rather than as a container resolution throw during `Build()` |
| What a **successful** selection leaves behind | One `Information` record, written **once per process start** by the validator under the event name `startupValidation` with `outcome` = `succeeded`, carrying the six named log-state properties the row below enumerates and nothing besides, so the rule that the connection string never reaches a log (below) is untouched. It exists for three reasons: an operator reading a start-up log can see which contract was applied without inferring it; the two tests below that assert *which row ran* have something to assert on; and [06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s pre-traffic release gate reads it. A validation that succeeds silently is indistinguishable from one that selected the wrong row and happened to pass |
| **The start-up validation record, in full — one event name, two outcomes, and the fields on each** | **This row exists because an earlier form of this table specified the success record as carrying `hostRole` and `connectionMode` "and nothing else", and named no producer for the failure at all.** Both were wrong in a way another deliverable could see: [06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s release gate check 5 requires the application to report **a boolean per property of the resolved connection string** from this very validation and states that "the gate reads four booleans and never the string" — four fields the field list forbade — while the failure had no event name, no level and no place in the producer table of section [3.3](#33-the-target-configuration-contract)'s record-shape mapping. The record is therefore specified here once, for both outcomes. **Event name**: the single literal **`startupValidation`**. **Outcome**: the closed two-literal set **`succeeded`** and **`failed`** — no third value, and no `partial`, because the validation either admitted the configuration or refused the start. **Cardinality: exactly one record per process start**, on either outcome and never both, because the validator runs once and its result is not re-evaluated; a second record of this event name in one process is a defect. **Level**: `Information` on `succeeded`, **`Warning`** on `failed` — and `Warning` rather than `Error` because [06 §9.6.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s `R8` closes the level to those two and reserves `Error` for `R2`, whose producer is the request-path `IExceptionHandler` of section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) and never runs here: a refused start never reaches the request pipeline, so the fault has no R2 emission and this record is the only readable account of it. **Fields on `succeeded` — six**: `hostRole` (`Web` or `Operator`); `connectionMode` (`M1`, `M2`, `M3` or `M4`); and the **four booleans check 5 reads**, one per property of the resolved `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection` — `authenticationIsManagedIdentity`, true when the parsed `Authentication` is either managed-identity member; `encryptIsTrue`; `trustServerCertificateIsFalse`; and `integratedSecurityIsAbsent`. **Fields on `failed` — four**: `hostRole`, or the literal `unregistered` where the composition supplied no signal, since the failure the row above describes is precisely the one with no role to name; `connectionMode`, the row the selection function chose, or `none` where the failure was the role's absence and no row could be selected; **`failedMembers`**, the configuration **key paths** that failed, ordered and joined by `"; "` into one string field for the transport reason [06 §9.6.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s `R2` row gives — the JSON console formatter renders a collection-valued state property as the literal `System.String[]`; and **`failedRules`**, the rule identifiers those members failed, in the same form and the same order, so a reader can pair the two positionally. **Neither outcome carries a configuration value.** No connection string and no fragment of one, no password in any spelling, no client identifier, no server or database name, no environment-conditional member's value, and no exception object — the four booleans exist *instead of* the string, which is what makes the gate readable without making the log a disclosure, and `failedMembers` carries key paths rather than the values at them for the same reason. **Nothing in this record is an exception argument**, so the formatter has no `ToString()` expansion to perform |

**The selection function, total and single-valued — which is what "exactly one row" now means.** The
triple of role, resolved environment and test-signal presence selects the row; the string is never
consulted in selecting it:

| Host role | Resolved environment | `ITestConnectionModeSignal` | Selected row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Web` | Anything other than `Development` | Absent | **M1**, and only M1 |
| `Web` | `Development` | Absent | **M2**, and only M2 |
| `Web` | Neither `Production` nor `Staging` | **Present** | **M4**, and only M4 — the fixture's host is a web host, and its own four conditions below still all have to hold |
| `Web` | `Production` or `Staging` | **Present** | **Failure.** The signal has no legitimate presence in either environment, and this is a stronger statement than "M4 is unavailable there": the registration itself is the defect and the start fails naming it |
| `Operator` | Any | Absent | **M3**, and only M3 |
| `Operator` | Any | **Present** | **Failure.** The operator tool is never the fixture's host, so both signals together are a composition defect rather than a combination to resolve |
| Absent | Any | Any | **Failure** — the missing-registration case in the table above |

Two properties follow, and both are the point of doing it this way. **`M1` and `M3` can no longer be
confused**, because a validator that consults one row cannot pick the wrong one from an overlap — the
overlap is still there in the shapes and is now harmless. And **every failure names a row**: "does not
satisfy M3" is a message that tells an operator which contract was applied, where "matches no accepted
mode" told them only that the search failed.

**M4 is bounded by the fixture's own composition rather than by anything the configuration can carry, and
that distinction is the whole of its safety.** An earlier formulation gated the mode on "a marker the
fixture sets on the configuration". That does not hold: a configuration key is exactly what a platform
setting, an environment variable or a release step **can** supply, so a deployed host would have been one
application setting away from selecting the test mode — and the mode that permits an inline password. The
gate is therefore a **service registration, which no configuration provider can produce**:

| Element | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| The signal | `ITestConnectionModeSignal`, an interface **declared** in the application (`Services/ITestConnectionModeSignal.cs`, which [04 §12.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s map carries as its own row) and **implemented nowhere in it**. It exposes one member: the closed set of `(DataSource, InitialCatalog)` pairs the fixture provisioned **for this run** |
| Who implements it | The test project alone. `src/MvcMusicStore.Tests` holds the only implementation, and the `ProjectReference` edge runs **test → application** ([04 §12.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)), so the application cannot name the type even accidentally: the direction of the reference makes it invisible from the side that gets published |
| How it is supplied | The fixture registers it into the service collection through the test host's own configuration hook, **before** the startup validator runs. It is a `services.AddSingleton<ITestConnectionModeSignal>(…)` call in test code — the one channel that is code rather than data. **It is the fourth line of the exhaustive `ConfigureTestServices` allow-list of section [12.6](#126-the-test-project-the-system-under-test-and-the-host-wiring)**, which fixes the hook, the implementing type and the singleton lifetime; an earlier form of that list ran to three lines and omitted this one, so the list forbade the registration this row requires |
| The validator rule | The one `IValidateOptions<ConnectionStringOptions>` takes `IServiceProvider` and reads the signal with **`GetService<ITestConnectionModeSignal>()`**, which "returns `null` if there is no service of type `T`" (`ServiceProviderServiceExtensions.GetService`, .NET 8) — deliberately not `GetRequiredService`, whose throw would turn the ordinary deployed case into a startup crash, and deliberately not an unannotated constructor parameter, which the container would require to be registered. **Null — the deployed and developer case — makes M4 unavailable outright**, whatever the string looks like: because the selection function above never reaches M4 without the signal, an M4-shaped string is then checked against the row that *was* selected and fails naming **that** row — `M1` for a deployed web host, `M2` under `Development`, `M3` under the operator role. Non-null admits M4 **only** when all four hold: the parsed `DataSource` **and** `InitialCatalog` appear together in one of the signal's pairs; the `DataSource` is a loopback form (`(localdb)\…`, `.`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) or the throwaway managed database the signal names; any `Password` present is the per-run credential the fixture generated, held in memory and written to no file; and the resolved environment is neither `Production` nor `Staging` |
| The target allow-list | The signal's pairs **are** the allow-list, generated at provision time and different every run, so it cannot be pre-declared, checked into a file or reused. A fixture that provisions a database and forgets to name it in the signal fails the start rather than falling through to M2 — the modes are mutually exclusive rows, not a cascade |

**How it is proven that a normal or deployed builder cannot select M4**, rather than asserted: coverage row
**O10** of section [12.4.1](#1241-the-published-operator-bytes) enumerates
the published application's service descriptors and asserts **no descriptor for
`ITestConnectionModeSignal` exists**, then builds a host the ordinary way — no fixture involvement — hands
it an M4-shaped connection string, and asserts the start **fails**, naming the row the selection function
chose for that host rather than M4. The
first half catches a future registration added inside the application; the second catches a validator
edit that made the signal optional. Neither can be satisfied by editing configuration, which is the
property the previous marker lacked.

**One validation test per mode, because a closed set of four rows is only closed if each row is exercised
from both sides.** These run against the validator alone — a built host, no database — so they are cheap
enough to be exhaustive, and each names the failure it would otherwise take a deployment to find.
**These rows are validator tests belonging to this table, not numbered rows of section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage)'s index**, so adding one — as the composition row at the foot of this table
does — changes none of that section's published row, case or execution totals. The one operator-side
assertion that *is* indexed says so in its own row and is cross-referenced from here: **O10** of section
[12.4.1](#1241-the-published-operator-bytes).

| Test | Given | Asserted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **M1 accepted** | `IHostRoleSignal` registered as `Web`, a non-`Development` environment, `ActiveDirectoryManagedIdentity`, `User Id` equal to `SqlIdentity:ClientId`, no password, `Encrypt=True`, `TrustServerCertificate=False`, and all four environment-conditional members present | The start succeeds. Repeated with the `ActiveDirectoryMSI` alias, which parses to a different enum member and must also pass |
| **M1 rejected** | The same, with `SqlIdentity:ClientId` **absent**; and again with it present but **unequal** to the parsed `User Id`; and again with a `Pwd=` keyword added | Each fails the start, naming the member and the rule — **and the message contains neither the connection string nor any password-keyword value** |
| **M2 accepted** | `Development`, `Integrated Security=True`, a local `DataSource`, and **none** of the four environment-conditional members supplied | The start succeeds. This is the test the previous unconditional `[Required]` would have failed, and it is the reason the annotations moved into the validator |
| **M2 rejected** | `Development` with `Integrated Security=True` against a **non-local** `DataSource` and `TrustServerCertificate=True`; and again with `SqlIdentity:ClientId` supplied | Each fails the start — the first on the transport rule, the second because M2 presents no identity of its own |
| **M3 accepted** | Any environment, a generic host built by the operator tool with `IHostRoleSignal` registered as `Operator`, `ActiveDirectoryManagedIdentity` with a `Guid` `User Id`, no password, and no `SqlIdentity:ClientId` | The start succeeds and the member's absence is **not** a failure |
| **M3 rejected** | `ActiveDirectoryDefault`; and again with `User Id` absent; and again with a password present — all three under the `Operator` role | Each fails the start. The first is the [06 §6.1.1.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) prohibition, asserted rather than described |
| **M4 accepted** | The fixture's own host, `IHostRoleSignal` registered as `Web`, and `ITestConnectionModeSignal` registered and naming the provisioned pair | The start succeeds, including with the per-run credential present |
| **M4 rejected** | The same string with the test signal **absent**; with it present but naming a **different** pair; and with the resolved environment set to `Production` | Each fails the start. The first two fail against the row the selection function chose instead of M4, naming that row; the third fails on M4's own environment condition. The first is row **O10** above |
| **One string, one row — the overlap is resolved rather than merely acknowledged** | **A single connection string constructed to satisfy `M1` and `M3` simultaneously**: `ActiveDirectoryManagedIdentity`, a `Guid` `User Id`, no password, `Integrated Security=False`, `Encrypt=True`, `TrustServerCertificate=False`, with `SqlIdentity:ClientId` present and **equal** to that `User Id`. Presented **twice** — once to a host with `IHostRoleSignal` registered as `Web`, once to a host with it registered as `Operator`, everything else held identical | **Both starts succeed, and each succeeds under exactly one row**: the `Web` host validates it against `M1` and the `Operator` host against `M3`. Asserted on the validator's own record of the row it applied, not on the outcome alone — two passes prove nothing about which rule ran. This is the row that fails if a future edit reintroduces "search the table for a matching row", because a search would have two candidates and no defined answer |
| **An operator-shaped string is refused by the web host** | `IHostRoleSignal` registered as `Web`, a non-`Development` environment, and an otherwise valid M3 string: `ActiveDirectoryManagedIdentity`, a `Guid` `User Id` that is **the deployment identity's**, no password, correct transport — and `SqlIdentity:ClientId` present and naming the **site's** identity, so the two `Guid`s differ | The start **fails**, naming `M1` and the unequal-identity rule. This is the finding this table exists to close: without the role signal the string would have been admitted under `M3`, and the site would have opened its connections as the **deployment** principal, which holds the DDL rights section [5.3](#53-who-applies-ddl-and-in-what-order) keeps away from the runtime identity. Repeated in the other direction — a `Web`-shaped string with `SqlIdentity:ClientId` absent, presented to the `Operator` host — and asserted to pass under `M3`, since M3 does not require that member |
| **No host role registered** | A host built with **neither** signal registered — the composition defect, not a configuration state — and any otherwise valid string | The start fails, naming `Configuration:HostRole` in the aggregated `OptionsValidationException`. Asserted on the message rather than on the exception type, because a `GetRequiredService` throw during `Build()` would also fail the start and would **not** be readable: this row is what distinguishes the two |
| **The registration itself, per root — three composition cases** | **(i) present and correct**: each root is composed as specified and its `IServiceProvider` is asked for `IHostRoleSignal`; **(ii) absent**: the root's single `AddSingleton` line is removed and nothing else changes; **(iii) wrong role**: the line is present but carries the *other* root's value — the web root registering `HostRole.Operator`, and the operator root registering `HostRole.Web` — with an otherwise valid string for the root's own contract | **(i)** the resolved service is **non-null**, is of type `HostRoleSignal`, its descriptor's lifetime is **`Singleton`**, and its `Role` equals **`Web`** from `Program.cs` and **`Operator`** from `tools/provision-admin/Program.cs`; two resolutions return the **same instance**. **(ii)** the start **fails** with the message the row above fixes — this is that row, exercised per root rather than once. **(iii)** the start **fails** naming the row the wrong value selected: the web root's string is checked against **M3** and refused on M3's rules, and the operator root's against **M1** and refused on the identity comparison, so a swapped registration cannot pass quietly. **Without case (i) the type is unproven at the only place it is constructed**, and without (iii) the two registration lines are interchangeable — which is the defect the `M1`/`M3` overlap made dangerous in the first place |

**Why the parsed builder rather than a scan of the string, stated because the two are not equivalent.**
Every rule above is expressed over **individual parsed fields**, and that is what makes "no password in
any spelling" enforceable: the builder normalizes the keyword aliases, so `Pwd` surfaces as `Password`,
`Uid` as `UserID`, and both `Trusted_Connection=True` and `Integrated Security=SSPI` as
`IntegratedSecurity = true` — verified against the provider. A substring scan for `Password=` misses all
four. The `Authentication` comparison is against the parsed enum for the same reason, and it accepts
**both** managed-identity members because the documented alias parses to a *different* member
(`ActiveDirectoryMSI`) than the primary spelling (`ActiveDirectoryManagedIdentity`), so a validator
comparing against one alone would reject a form [06 §6.1.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) permits.
This is the application-side counterpart of [06 §9.3.3](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s keyword
scan, and where the two could disagree the parsed form governs, because it is the stricter of the two.

**The connection string is never logged, and never appears in an exception message (CWE-532).** The
failure record names the key, the check that failed and — where the check is a comparison — the **field**
whose values differed, together with the expected and actual values of that field only: a server name, a
database name and a client-ID GUID are not credentials ([06 §6.1.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)
says so of the GUID, and [06 §9.3.3](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) already emits the same pair for
its own check, so the two records agree). **What never appears anywhere is the string itself, any
password-keyword value, and any interpolation of the string into a message, an exception, a stack trace or
a diagnostic page** — the validator therefore constructs its messages from named fields and never from the
bound value, and the provider's own exceptions are logged by their type and message rather than by
re-emitting the configuration that produced them.

**What is rejected in every environment, including the two permissive ones.** No mode permits: a
`Password` in any spelling on M1, M2 or M3; a `UserID` holding anything other than the expected client-ID
GUID on M1; a value beginning `@Microsoft.KeyVault(`, which means a reference the platform failed to
resolve ([06 §8.4.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)); an absent or empty `DataSource` or
`InitialCatalog`, which is a string that would connect to whatever the provider's defaults resolve to;
and `TrustServerCertificate=True` against any host that is not the local or containerized instance its
own row names.

**Certificate validation is disabled in exactly one circumstance, and that circumstance is stated here
rather than in the two rows that rely on it.** `TrustServerCertificate=True` suppresses the check that the
certificate presented by a SQL endpoint is the one a trusted authority issued for that host, which is the
control that makes an interposed endpoint detectable. It is therefore **one** exception with **one**
boundary, not a per-row convenience:

- **The boundary.** The engine must be an instance the invoking process itself owns and reaches without
  leaving the machine — `(localdb)\…`, `.`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, or a container published on
  loopback — and its certificate must be the self-signed one such an engine generates for itself. Rows
  **M2** and **M4** of the table above are the only rows that may invoke it, and each does so **by
  reference to this paragraph**; neither carries an allowance of its own.
- **What it may never be.** Prohibited on **M1** and **M3** in every environment, on any `DataSource`
  that resolves off the machine, on the CI path's allow-listed managed database, in any published
  example, in any runbook step other than the one named below, and in any value a platform or an operator
  supplies. A string that pairs it with a non-local `DataSource` fails the start rather than connecting —
  the `M2 rejected` row of the assertion table below is that assertion, and it exists so the boundary is
  enforced by the validator rather than by this prose.
- **Why the alternative is not taken.** A trusted ephemeral certificate would mean minting one per
  container run and installing it in the trust store of every developer machine and every agent that runs
  the suite — a machine-level mutation, with its own removal problem, for an engine that is destroyed at
  the end of the run. Against a container the run created, **published on loopback by the explicit
  `-p 127.0.0.1:0:1433` bind of stage B3e and confirmed by stage B3a's readback, which fails the stage on
  any published address that is not loopback** (section
  [12.10](#1210-the-execution-runbook-and-the-two-platform-split)), on a port the run owns,
  there is no network position from which an endpoint could be interposed, so the bypass removes a control
  that has nothing to protect there and the trust-store change would be the larger exposure.
- **The corpus assertion, which is checkable rather than asserted.** Exactly **two** places in this
  document put `TrustServerCertificate=True` **into a connection string**: stage **B3a** of section
  [12.10](#1210-the-execution-runbook-and-the-two-platform-split), which builds the disposable
  container's `Tests__Target__EngineConnectionString`, and the `M2 rejected` row of the assertion table
  below, which constructs one **in order to prove it is refused**. Every other connection string this
  document publishes states `TrustServerCertificate=False` explicitly alongside `Encrypt=True` — the
  deployed string, the operator and release string, and both migration connections of section
  [5.1](#51-domain-data-migration-starts-with-schema-extraction). The remaining occurrences of the
  keyword in this document are **prose about the setting** — this paragraph, the rejection list above it,
  and the two mode rows that invoke this exception — and none of them is a string a process would
  connect with. A third *string* carrying it is a defect in this document, and the check is a search for
  the literal followed by reading each hit for whether it sits inside a connection string.

**The unresolved-reference check is not specific to this key, and stating it once is what makes it
enforceable.** Any value this section defines can arrive as a Key Vault reference, and the platform's
pass-through behaviour is the same for all of them, so the rule is a **standing obligation on every
validator in this section**: each `IValidateOptions<T>` rejects any bound `string` member whose value
begins with `@Microsoft.KeyVault(`, with the same message shape and the same value suppression as above.
It is one line per validator rather than a separate mechanism, and it is stated here so no later table has
to repeat it — where a table below says a member is validated, this check is part of what that means.

**How every required member below is *declared*, because the obvious declaration cannot detect a missing
key.** This is a mechanism decision and it precedes the values, because getting it wrong makes every
value below unenforceable.

`[Required]` is the reflex answer and it does not work for a value type. The attribute's implementation
rejects **only** `null` and — unless `AllowEmptyStrings` is set — an empty or whitespace string:
`if (value is null) return false; return AllowEmptyStrings || value is not string stringValue ||
!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(stringValue);` (`RequiredAttribute.IsValid`, `System.ComponentModel.Annotations`,
.NET 8). Configuration binding leaves an unsupplied member at its CLR default, and a CLR default is not
null. So a `bool` declared `public bool PasswordRequireDigit { get; set; }` binds to `false` when the key
is absent, `[Required]` passes, and the application starts with digits **not** required — the exact
failure section [6](#6-authentication-policy-is-decided-not-inherited) exists to forbid, arriving through
the validation that was supposed to prevent it. The same holds for `int` (`0`), `TimeSpan`
(`TimeSpan.Zero`) and every enum (its zero member — which for `SameSiteMode` is `Unspecified`).

**The rule, applied to every table below:**

| Member's logical type | Declared as | Presence detected by | Range or value constraint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `string?` | `[Required]` — correct here, because an absent key really does leave `null` | `[Required]`, plus a per-member rule in `IValidateOptions<T>` where one applies |
| `bool` | **`bool?`** | `[Required]` on the nullable member: an absent key leaves `null`, which the attribute rejects | none — both values are legal, which is precisely why absence must be distinguishable from `false` |
| `int` | **`int?`** | `[Required]` on the nullable member | `[Range]` on the nullable member, which validates the contained value when one is present |
| `TimeSpan` | **`TimeSpan?`** | `[Required]` on the nullable member | A per-member bound in `IValidateOptions<T>`, because `[Range]` has no `TimeSpan` form |
| enum | **`SameSiteMode?`** and equivalents | `[Required]` on the nullable member | An explicit allowed-set check in `IValidateOptions<T>`, because binding an unrecognised name is a bind failure but binding a *legal but unwanted* member is not |

**Nullable declaration is the mechanism; a non-nullable property exposed to the rest of the application is
the outcome.** Each options type exposes the validated value through a non-nullable accessor that the
validator has already guaranteed — so no consumer writes `?? throw`, and no consumer can observe the
nullable form. That is the whole reason the nullability is stated here rather than left to a reader to
infer from "required": it is a property of the options type, not of the key.

**And one member class needs the opposite treatment, because an attribute cannot express a condition and
attaching one anyway makes the condition unreachable.** Some members below are required **only in some
environments or under some connection modes** — the five the safe-default block at the end of this section
names, four conditional on the environment and one on the connection mode. For those, `[Required]` is
**not** declared, and the reason is mechanical rather than stylistic:
`ValidateDataAnnotations()` registers a `DataAnnotationValidateOptions<TOptions>` as one
`IValidateOptions<TOptions>` among the others, and the options factory runs **every** registered validator
and **aggregates** their failures into a single `OptionsValidationException` rather than stopping at the
first (`OptionsFactory<TOptions>.Create`, `Microsoft.Extensions.Options`, .NET 8). So an unconditional
`[Required]` on a conditionally required member fails the start in exactly the environments the condition
was written to permit, and no amount of logic in the environment-aware validator can withdraw a failure
another validator has already reported.

| Member class | Declared as | Where presence is enforced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unconditionally required | The nullable form above, **with** `[Required]` | The data-annotations half. Correct here because the answer does not depend on the environment |
| **Conditionally required** | The same nullable form, **without** `[Required]` and without `[Range]` | **The type's one `IValidateOptions<T>`**, which reads `IHostEnvironment`, the selected connection mode and the sibling members, and reports the failure only when the condition holds. Range and format rules for those members move into the same validator, for the same reason |

**The consequence is a rule with no exceptions: each options type has exactly one `IValidateOptions<T>`,
and for a conditionally required member that validator is the *only* place presence is decided.** A second
validator for the same type would reintroduce the aggregation problem in a form that is harder to see,
because both halves would then be this document's own code.

**`Identity` — `IdentityPolicyOptions`. Every member is required and none has a default; the value each
member carries is section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled)'s.**

| Member | Declared as | Value | Framework default | Label |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PasswordMinimumLength` | `int?`, `[Range(8, 128)]` | **12** | `6` (`PasswordOptions.RequiredLength`) | **Deliberate hardening** |
| `PasswordRequireDigit` | `bool?` | **`true`** | `true` | **Deliberate hardening** relative to the source, which assigns no password validator at all; equal to the target default |
| `PasswordRequireLowercase` | `bool?` | **`true`** | `true` | **Deliberate hardening**, as above |
| `PasswordRequireUppercase` | `bool?` | **`true`** | `true` | **Deliberate hardening**, as above |
| `PasswordRequireNonAlphanumeric` | `bool?` | **`true`** | `true` | **Deliberate hardening**, as above |
| `PasswordRequiredUniqueChars` | `int?`, `[Range(1, 16)]` | **4** | `1` | **Deliberate hardening** |
| `LockoutEnabled` | `bool?` | **`true`** | `true` (`LockoutOptions.AllowedForNewUsers`) | **Deliberate hardening** — the source has no lockout of any kind |
| `LockoutMaxFailedAccessAttempts` | `int?`, `[Range(3, 20)]` | **5** | `5` | **Preserved** against the target default; hardening against the source, which counts nothing |
| `LockoutDefaultDuration` | `TimeSpan?`, bounded to 1 minute – 24 hours | **`00:15:00`** | `00:05:00` | **Deliberate hardening** |
| `SignInRequireConfirmedAccount` | `bool?` | **`false`** | `false` | **Preserved**, deliberately — section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled) records why the hardening is the wrong call here |
| `UserRequireUniqueEmail` | `bool?` | **`false`** | `false` | **Preserved** |
| `UserAllowedUserNameCharacters` | `string?`, `[Required]` | **`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-._@+`** | the same string | **Preserved** against the target default — the value *is* the framework default, which is why the column beside this one repeats it — and a **deliberate widening** against the source, whose effective policy is alphanumeric-only. Both frames are stated for the same reason `LockoutMaxFailedAccessAttempts` above states both, and this cell points at section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled)'s verdict, which is the widening. A one-word "**Preserved**" here pointed at the opposite word and is deleted |

**Why the values live here and the labels live in section
[6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled).** A security value and its justification are two different
review objects. The **value** belongs where a reviewer can see it beside its key, its type and its
presence rule — that is this table, and it is the only place any of these numbers appears. The **label and
the reason** belong where the policy is argued, which is section 6.1; that table cites this one for the
number rather than carrying a second copy. The label column above is a one-word pointer at 6.1's
verdict, not a second decision.

**`UserAllowedUserNameCharacters` is load-bearing for the migration, not decoration.** Identity's user
manager validates a username against the set section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled)
fixes on every write, and that set does not contain a space. The migrated usernames are the source's
own, so section [5.5](#55-the-identity-transition--a-schema-decision-plus-a-data-migration) validates
every extracted username against that exact string **before** the load and stops on a violation — a name
that loads but can never be updated afterwards is a defect the load should not create.

**No member has a default, because a default here is precisely the framework-inherited value section
[6](#6-authentication-policy-is-decided-not-inherited) exists to forbid.** The two rows section 6.1
deliberately declines to harden — `SignInRequireConfirmedAccount` and `UserRequireUniqueEmail` — are
**still required keys**: an explicit value is a stated decision, an absent key is an
inherited one, and only the first can be reviewed. That distinction is only expressible because both are
declared `bool?`.

**`Authentication:Cookie` — `AuthenticationCookieOptions`. This section configures the *application*
cookie — the framework's `IdentityConstants.ApplicationScheme`. The other cookies the application issues
are inventoried below it, because "the cookie policy" is not one cookie.**

| Member | Declared as | Value | Framework default | Label |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Name` | `string?`, `[Required]` | **`.MvcMusicStore.Auth`** | `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application`, *generated* rather than set: the post-configuration step assigns `".AspNetCore." + Uri.EscapeDataString(schemeName)` when no name is supplied, and the scheme is `Identity.Application` | **Deliberate change**, and the label section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled) carries for the same key. **This corrects an earlier form of this row**, which named `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` and called it preserved: that put two different literals on one `Cookie.Name` assignment — this one and 6.1's — and only one string can be written. `.MvcMusicStore.Auth` is the one, for the reason 6.1 gives: a name distinct from the legacy `.AspNet.ApplicationCookie` means the cutover cannot leave a browser presenting an undecryptable ticket under a name the new key ring accepts. Setting the literal at all — rather than inheriting the generated one — means renaming a scheme cannot silently rename a live cookie and sign everyone out |
| `ExpireTimeSpan` | `TimeSpan?`, bounded to 1 hour – 30 days | **`14.00:00:00`** | `TimeSpan.FromDays(14)` | **Preserved** — it equals both the target default and the source middleware's own default, so the ticket lifetime does not change at cutover |
| `SlidingExpiration` | `bool?` | **`true`** | `true` | **Preserved**, stated |
| `PersistentExpireTimeSpan` | `TimeSpan?`, bounded to 1 hour – 30 days | **`14.00:00:00`** | no such option exists — see the wiring below | **Preserved**: the source honours the "remember me" flag [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:63] and its middleware's persistent cookie expires on the same 14-day ticket window |
| `SameSite` | **`SameSiteMode?`**, restricted to `Lax` or `Strict` | **`Lax`** | `Lax` | **Deliberate hardening** — the source middleware has no such option at all (section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled)). `Unspecified` and `None` are rejected by the validator rather than merely undocumented |
| `LoginPath` | `string?`, `[Required]`, must begin `/` | **`/Account/Login`** | `/Account/Login` | **Preserved** [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:17] |
| `LogoutPath` | `string?`, `[Required]`, must begin `/` | **`/Account/LogOff`** | `/Account/Logout` | **Preserved** — the source's sign-out action is `LogOff` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:300-306], so the framework default would name a route this application does not have |
| `AccessDeniedPath` | `string?`, `[Required]`, must begin `/` | **`/Home/Error/403`** — the status-code error action of section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types), which **sets 403 on the response**. **This corrects an earlier form of this row**, which named `/Account/AccessDenied`: that was a second value for one key, and no action of that name exists anywhere in this document, so a denied request would have redirected to a route that returns 404. **The member is set and the redirect it configures never fires**: the global `OnRedirectToAccessDenied` of section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) writes 403 instead, and `UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute` re-executes this very path to render the view. The value is therefore the *rendered* path rather than a redirect target, and it is set rather than left null so that the two mechanisms name one string | `/Account/AccessDenied` | **Deliberate hardening**, minor: the source redirects a denied authenticated user to the login form (section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled)). The **action** is net-new; it renders the **generic error view** of section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) with a 403 rather than a view of its own, so no view file is added and section [8.4](#84-the-view-disposition-by-semantic-role) is unchanged |

**`PersistentExpireTimeSpan` is wired to a real mechanism, and the mechanism is named because the
framework has no option of that name.** There is no separate persistent-cookie lifetime in
`CookieAuthenticationOptions`. The sign-in handler sets `Properties.ExpiresUtc` to
`IssuedUtc + Options.ExpireTimeSpan` **only when the caller left it unset**, and then, `if
(Properties.IsPersistent)`, copies that value into the response cookie's `Expires` attribute
(`CookieAuthenticationHandler.HandleSignInAsync`, .NET 8). So the value binds to exactly one call site:
the sign-in path passes `new AuthenticationProperties { IsPersistent = <the "remember me" flag>, ExpiresUtc
= TimeProvider.GetUtcNow() + PersistentExpireTimeSpan }`. Two consequences are worth stating: the member
controls the **browser-persistence** window and `ExpireTimeSpan` controls the **ticket** window, so
setting the first longer than the second would produce a cookie the browser keeps and the handler
rejects — which is why the validator requires `PersistentExpireTimeSpan <= ExpireTimeSpan`; and a
non-persistent sign-in passes `IsPersistent = false` and no `ExpiresUtc`, leaving a session cookie whose
ticket window is `ExpireTimeSpan`, exactly as today.

**Every cookie the application can issue, with the one place each is configured.** The list is closed: a
cookie not in it is not issued at all. **Four cookies carry a name this application chooses**, and the
first three of those are the names [06 §7.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s protected-payload
table depends on — that document defers the closed inventory here, so the names are stated once, in this
table, and cited rather than restated there. Three further rows are cookies the framework *would* name but
this application never writes, and each says so with the evidence rather than by assertion — they are
listed because an unconfigured cookie that a later change starts writing inherits framework defaults, and
two of those defaults are `SecurePolicy = None`. The Katana cookie `.AspNet.ApplicationCookie` is
deliberately **not** in this inventory: the target never issues it, and the only component that names it
is the deletion stage of section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) item 3.

| Cookie | Name | Where its attributes are set | `Secure` / `HttpOnly` / `SameSite` / essential |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Application (sign-in) | **`.MvcMusicStore.Auth`** — the one name, set explicitly; there is no second name for this cookie anywhere in this document | `Authentication:Cookie` above | Always / on / `Lax` / essential |
| External sign-in | **`Identity.External`** — the framework sets this one's `Cookie.Name` to the scheme string itself, without the `.AspNetCore.` prefix | **The cookie is a removed surface** (section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) decision item 3): nothing in the target issues or reads it, so it appears in this inventory as a **scheme entry `AddIdentity` creates and no flow uses**, not as a cookie the application writes. Its attributes are nonetheless set **in code**, on the framework's `IdentityConstants.ExternalScheme` options, for the one reason this table's preamble gives — an unconfigured cookie that a later change starts writing inherits `SecurePolicy = None`. **No configuration key**, because a key would invite tuning a removed surface. Its `ExpireTimeSpan` stays at the framework's `00:05:00` | Always / on / `Lax` / essential |
| Two-factor | `Identity.TwoFactorUserId` and `Identity.TwoFactorRememberMe`, by the same scheme-name rule | Code, in the same call as the external cookie's. **Never written**: no two-factor flow exists in the source, none is added, `Identity:*` has no two-factor member and section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled) adds no row. Configured anyway, so a future flow starts from these attributes rather than the framework's | Always / on / `Lax` / essential |

| Cart recovery | `.MvcMusicStore.CartRecovery` | Code, on the cart-migration failure branch of section [4.3](#43-the-cross-store-consistency-model); **no configuration key**, because its payload, its seven-day fixed lifetime and its attempt counter are that branch's contract rather than a deployment choice | Always / on / `Lax` / essential, host-only, `Path=/` |
| Temp-data | `.AspNetCore.Mvc.CookieTempDataProvider` | Code, on `CookieTempDataProviderOptions`; **no configuration key**. The provider **is** registered — MVC's default view services call `TryAddSingleton<ITempDataProvider, CookieTempDataProvider>()`, so the registration is not ours to decline — but **nothing writes `TempData`**, verified by `git grep -n TempData -- 'src/**/*.cs' 'src/**/*.cshtml'` returning nothing, so no cookie is ever written. It is configured regardless because this cookie's framework defaults are the weakest of the set: `SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.None` and `IsEssential = false` | Always / on / `Lax` / essential |
| Consent / policy | none | **Not added.** No cookie-policy consent gate is registered, so no consent cookie exists. Every cookie above is marked essential, which is a factual claim about this application rather than an exemption — the session cookie *is* the cart identity [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/ShoppingCart.cs:19] | n/a |

**Five cookie attributes are deliberately *not* configuration-backed on any cookie: `Secure`, `HttpOnly`,
`IsEssential`, `Path` and `Domain`.** All five are set in code and have **no key**, because a configurable
