**The handler's gate order, because a route handler carries no attributes to do this for it and the order
is what makes [06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s statuses reachable.** Every value below is
06's and is cited rather than re-derived; what this table fixes is **which check runs first**, since a
size bound evaluated after the body has been read is not a bound. **The whole of the previous
attribute-by-attribute generation — `[HttpPost]`, `[AllowAnonymous]`, `[IgnoreAntiforgeryToken]`,
`[Consumes]`, `[EnableRateLimiting]` and `[RequestSizeLimit(65536)]` — is deleted with the action it
decorated**, along with the two caps it expressed (an 8 KiB and a 64 KiB ceiling varying by media type)
and the `IHttpMaxRequestBodySizeFeature` assignment that varied them.

| Gate | Where it comes from, and what it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Route and verb** | The registration itself: `MapPost("/csp-report", …)`, section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) stage 2 item 13. The path is absolute by construction — a route handler has no controller prefix to inherit, so the `/Home/csp-report` hazard the attribute form had to guard against cannot arise — and mapping `POST` alone means any other verb on the path is the framework's own **`405`**, which is 06's route-and-verb row satisfied with no code here at all |
| **Authorization** | `.AllowAnonymous()` on the registration, **and the handler reads no `User`**. Both are required and 06's authorization row says why: `.AllowAnonymous()` removes the requirement but does not stop a principal existing, since `UseAuthentication()` (stage 2 item 10) runs ahead of the endpoint, so a report from a signed-in visitor's browser arrives authenticated and must be treated identically to an anonymous one |
| **Anti-forgery** | `.DisableAntiforgery()` on the registration — section [7.1](#71-the-policy)'s second opt-out, and the metadata its enumeration asserts |
| **Media type — first in the handler, before a byte is read** | The `Content-Type` is parsed with `MediaTypeHeaderValue.TryParse` and its media type compared against **exactly** the two 06 accepts, parameters such as `charset` tolerated and ignored. Anything else — `application/json` included — is 06's **`415`** with the body unread. There is no `[Consumes]` to lean on, so this is the handler's first statement, and putting it first is what keeps "body unread" true |
| **Declared length — second** | `Request.ContentLength` present and greater than **16,384** is 06's **`413`**, returned without touching the stream. An **absent** length is *accepted* and falls through to the gate below — 06's payload-bound row is explicit that a request declaring no length is treated exactly as one declaring a length within the bound |
| **Bounded read — third** | The body is read in chunks with a running total into a buffer that never exceeds the budget, and the read **stops at the first byte past it — byte 16,385 —** answering `413` and discarding what it holds. This is the one gate the earlier generation got structurally wrong: it rejected an absent length outright and relied on the server-wide limit to catch a lying one, which meant the bound was enforced by a `BadHttpRequestException` it then had to catch. Because this handler never reads past the budget, Kestrel's own `MaxRequestBodySize` is left at its configured value, nothing on this path raises that exception, and no request-length decision depends on catching one |
| **Parse — fourth** | `System.Text.Json` with 06's parser settings, into whichever of the two DTO shapes the accepted media type selected. A body that does not parse, one missing the member its shape requires, and a `reports+json` array above **20** elements are each 06's **`400`**, and the batch is rejected whole |
| **Rate limit — ahead of all of the above** | `.RequireRateLimiting("csp-report")` on the registration, evaluated by the middleware at stage 2 item 11 and therefore **before the handler runs at all**. A refused request executes none of these gates. The limits are section 2.4 stage 1 item 14's and the rejection is that item's options-level **`429` with `Retry-After`**, which is what 06 requires this endpoint to inherit |

**The status set is 06's and is not restated as a table here** — the previous generation's five-row
response table is deleted, and with it the two statuses that disagreed with 06: a `413` for a request
that declared no length, and a `204` for a rate-limited request. **What this section does own is the
handler's failure discipline, because it is the difference between a bounded body and an alert storm.**
Every gate above returns its status directly, and the whole body is wrapped so that **no exception
escapes the handler**: an unexpected failure increments the drop counter and answers `204`, never `500`
and never a redirect. An escaping exception would travel the pipeline into stage 2 item 4's handler and
write one `Error`-level record **per report**, which is precisely the amplifier
[06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s rejection row forbids by requiring that no rejected
request produce a per-report record. No response on any path carries a body or a cookie.

**It touches no session and no database, and the one cost the previous generation had to admit is gone
rather than reduced.** The handler reads no session entry, and `UseSession()` at stage 2 item 9 of section
[2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) loads and stores nothing for a request that never touches
`ISession`, so no session is created and no row is written to the distributed cache — otherwise every
report from every browser would mint one. It executes no query either, which is what
[06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s "no read of the database" requires. **And because the
endpoint is a route handler, its only injected dependencies are the sink singleton and the options it
reads, so no `DbContext` is constructed on a report request at all.** The action form could not say that:
`HomeController`'s constructor takes `MusicStoreEntities` (section
[4.1](#41-the-ten-manual-instantiation-sites-constructor-injection-replaces)), so a scoped context was
constructed and disposed on every report — a few allocations rather than a connection, but a cost that
existed only to keep the two opt-outs in one file, and section [7.1](#71-the-policy)'s two-surface
enumeration removes the reason to pay it.

**What Stage 1 registers, and where the middleware goes.** Both are entered in section
[2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order), which stays the authoritative composition; they are named
here so the endpoint's contract is readable in one place.

| Registration | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `AddRateLimiter` | `AddPolicy<string, CspReportRateLimitPolicy>("csp-report")` — registered **alongside** the chained global limiter of stage 1 item 14, not instead of it. The limits, the partition and the rejection behaviour are that item's |
| `AddSingleton<CspReportSink>()` | The handler body, the normalizer, the two hourly budgets and the emission |
| `UseRateLimiter()` | **Stage 2 item 11** — after `UseAuthentication()` (item 10) and before `UseAuthorization()` (item 12), which is where section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) places it and where it states both halves of the reason. The documented constraint this endpoint depends on is the routing one: "`UseRateLimiter` must be called after `UseRouting` when rate limiting endpoint specific APIs are used. For example, if the `[EnableRateLimiting]` attribute is used, `UseRateLimiter` must be called after `UseRouting`" (*Rate limiting middleware in ASP.NET Core*, .NET 8) — before routing, the endpoint's policy metadata has not been selected and the named policy silently does not apply. **The earlier form of this row said it sits "inside stage 8's group, immediately after `UseRouting()`" and "above stages 9 to 12", so that a rejected report "reaches neither authentication, nor session, nor the endpoint". Both claims are deleted**: the limiter is item 11, which is **below** session at item 9 and **below** authentication at item 10, so a refused report does traverse both — at the cost of one cookie-decrypt attempt, which is the concession item 11 states, and nothing more, because session loads nothing for a request that never touches it and the handler never runs. What the position genuinely buys is that a refused report evaluates **no authorization policy and never reaches the endpoint** |

**The partition key is the address the ingress observed, and a caller cannot inflate it.**
[06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires partitioning on the client address "as
reconstructed by `UseForwardedHeaders`" and never on the `UserId`, and the mechanism is **stage 2 item
1**: that middleware rewrites `HttpContext.Connection.RemoteIpAddress`, so the policy reads that property
and gets the resolved value. `ForwardLimit = 1` — the option, set in stage 1 — is what makes it
trustworthy: only
the entry the platform ingress appended is consumed, so a caller-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` value sits to
its left and is never read. Two consequences: the limiter's own partition table is bounded by **real**
client addresses rather than by strings a caller chooses, and a request arriving with no resolvable
forwarded address — which on either platform means it did not come through ingress — partitions under a
single fixed `unknown` key rather than creating one partition per caller.

**The window and the rejection are both stated once, in section
[2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) stage 1 item 14, and this paragraph exists to record what an
earlier form of it said instead.** The window is a **fixed window of 20 permits per minute per
partition** with `QueueLimit = 0`, so a rejected request is refused immediately and never queued — the
figure [06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s rate-limiting row states *per partition per
instance* and stage 1 item 14 carries verbatim. **The earlier form read "a fixed window of 20 permits per
5 minutes" and had the policy's own `OnRejected` answer `204` "so that a rejection is indistinguishable
from an acceptance", set on the policy rather than on the options object "so that no future rate-limited
endpoint inherits a 204". All three are deleted.** The window figure was simply a different number from
the one its own cited owner publishes. The `204` contradicted 06's rate-limiting row, which requires this
endpoint to inherit **05's `429`-with-`Retry-After`** behaviour, and it also defeated the promotion gate:
06's limiter test asserts a `429` on the twenty-first request, and an endpoint answering `204` to a
refusal cannot be shown to be limited at all. So `OnRejected` is left **null** on the policy, the
options-level `RejectionStatusCode` of `429` and its `Retry-After` callback govern, and the documented
default this endpoint would otherwise fall to — `RateLimiterOptions.RejectionStatusCode` "defaults to
`Status503ServiceUnavailable`" (API reference, ASP.NET Core 8) — is the reason stage 1 item 14 sets it
explicitly for every limiter rather than per policy.

**The acceptance set is 06's, and no numbered parity row in this document names this endpoint.** Every
branch of the response set above is asserted by [06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s
numbered promotion-gate tests, on the ownership sub-section
[7.5.2](#752-cardinality-overflow-collapses-to-a-fixed-marker-because-a-hash-preserves-the-cardinality-the-cap-bounds)
states in full — the closed field set, the per-field allow-lists and the truncation rules being
[06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s, and the shape each field survives in being section
[3.3](#33-the-target-configuration-contract)'s. None of them asserts anything a browser would have to do:
that half discharges through [06 §10.2.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s browser-evidence gate,
never here.

#### 7.5.1 Every limit is enforced per replica, so a "global" cap on an in-process limiter is not global

**The mechanical fact is this document's; every figure derived from it is 06's, and an earlier form of
this subsection had that the wrong way round.** The framework's rate limiter holds its window state in the
**worker process**, and the sink of section
[7.5](#75-the-second-opt-out-mapped--the-report-collectors-application-half) holds its two hourly budgets
and its distinct-value set in that same process — no shared store, no coordination between instances, no
distributed counter. Every cap attached to either is therefore enforced **per replica**, and a cap phrased
"across all clients" but implemented in one process is multiplied by the instance count. Affinity is not a
way out ([06 §8.3](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)): it is being retired, and a browser's report is
sent by the reporting machinery rather than by the page, so nothing binds a report to the replica that
served the page it came from.

**06 now publishes its caps in that form itself, so this subsection cites them rather than converting
them.** [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) states the accepted-report budget and the
distinct-value cardinality **per replica** with the fleet-wide figure each one holds;
the same sub-section carries the arithmetic to the autoscale ceiling and to
the floor, and states why the per-client limiter is the one left undivided; and
[06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s rate-limiting row publishes the per-client window *per
partition per instance* with a scale note that reaches the same conclusion.

**What is deleted is this subsection's own copy of that arithmetic**: a three-row table headed "06
§10.2.2's figure", converting each into a per-replica budget and a fleet-wide worst case, plus the two
paragraphs that justified and costed the division. It had already drifted from the source it named, in
three places — it gave the per-client window as **20 requests per 5 minutes** where 06 states 20 per
minute, and it described the endpoint as answering **`204`** under an **8 KiB** cap where 06's contract
answers `429` on a refusal and bounds the body at 16 KiB. Two documents converting one set of figures is
how copies drift; one owner and a citation cannot.

**What this subsection keeps is the part 06 cannot state on this document's behalf: the cost of the
division is borne here, and it is visible.** Because the budgets bind per replica, they engage well before
a reader extrapolating from a fleet figure would expect. That is deliberate — a cap on diagnostic exhaust
should fail toward suppressing early rather than toward an unbounded bill — and it is observable rather
than silent, because suppression **writes its own record** (sub-section
[7.5.2](#752-cardinality-overflow-collapses-to-a-fixed-marker-because-a-hash-preserves-the-cardinality-the-cap-bounds))
carrying the budget and the counts, so a reader who sees a thin stream can tell whether it was quiet or
clipped. The divisor is 06's on both hosting targets, and under the secondary Container Apps option the
budgets are recomputed from that revision's `maxReplicas` — an arithmetic dependency, not a second design.

**Why the two fleet caps are not backed by the SQL distributed cache the application already has.** It is
the obvious alternative — section [6.3](#63-session-and-cart-identity) already puts a distributed cache
in the application's own database — and each of these four reasons defeats it on its own:

- [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires this endpoint to perform **no read of the
  database** and to write **nothing** to the application database. The cache table is in that database, so
  a shared counter would break the requirement the caps exist to serve.
- It would put a database round trip on a **public, unauthenticated** path — handing an anonymous caller a
  lever on the very resource the endpoint is kept away from.
- `IDistributedCache` offers get, set, refresh and remove and **no atomic increment**, so a shared counter
  is a read-modify-write race. The result would be an approximation *with* a database dependency, where
  the division above is an approximation without one.
- It would place diagnostic exhaust inside the backup and restore position
  [06 §6.7](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) deliberately keeps it out of.

#### 7.5.2 Cardinality overflow collapses to a fixed marker, because a hash preserves the cardinality the cap bounds

An earlier formulation of this contract — and of
[06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s half of it, which
that section has since withdrawn on the same reasoning — replaced a
`blocked-uri` beyond the hourly budget with a **SHA-256 prefix** of itself, recorded under a fixed
`blocked-uri-overflow` marker so that the *count* survived. The intent was right and the mechanism defeated
it: **a digest is injective.**
Distinct attacker-chosen inputs produce distinct prefixes, so retaining one retains exactly the
cardinality the cap was written to bound — 100 000 fabricated values become 100 000 distinct property
values in a 90-day table ([06 §9.5](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)) — and truncating the prefix only
moves the bound to the prefix's own collision space rather than to the budget. What this application
records instead:

| | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Beyond the budget** | The property value is the **fixed literal `blocked-uri-overflow`** — no digest, no prefix, no per-value component of any kind. Every suppressed report carries the identical value, so the property's cardinality beyond the budget is exactly **one** |
| **What is kept** | One **`CspReportSuppressed`** record per replica per hour, carrying an **`outcome`** of the single literal **`budgetExceeded`** — the member [06 §9.6.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s `R8` row requires and an earlier form of this cell omitted, with one literal for the whole domain because passing the budget is the only condition that produces the record — together with the budget, the count of suppressed reports, the count of distinct values dropped and the top `effective-directive` values — a field already reduced to the directive names in [06 §10.2.1](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s policy, so the summary cannot itself be inflated. It is the summary record [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires, named here so a query can find it; it is **not** a sixth mandatory event in the sense of [06 §9.2.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) and nothing alerts on its absence |
| **What is lost, said plainly** | *Which* URI was blocked beyond that hour's budget. No decision hangs on it: the promotion criteria of [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) resolve a report to a defect or to an approved policy amendment from the **directive** and the values already recorded, and an unbounded tail of attacker-chosen strings informs neither |
| **The second property it buys** | The sink's own memory is bounded too. The distinct-value set never holds more than the budget's entries — 33 strings of at most the 256 characters [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) truncates to — where a digest design needs an unbounded set to know whether it has seen a value before |

**The sink's state, stated because a per-replica hourly budget is mutable shared state reached from a
public path.** One singleton holds a UTC hour stamp, two counters and the bounded set, mutated under a
single lock, with `Interlocked` where a counter is the only thing changing; the window advances by
comparing the stored hour when a report arrives, so there is no timer, no background service and no
registration beyond the singleton. Concurrency is a property of the design rather than an afterthought:
every replica serves reports on many threads at once, and an unsynchronized counter would make the
budget's own numbers wrong in the direction of admitting more.

**What lands in the sink.** `CspViolationReported` at `Warning`, under the reserved category
[06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) names for this record class — the category is what lets
the promotion gate query these records alone, so the event name and the category are stated together
rather than one of them being left to inference — with the field set, the per-field
allow-lists and the truncation rules of [06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md), normalized
from both wire shapes into that subsection's one hyphenated record. The *shape* the fields survive in is
section [3.3](#33-the-target-configuration-contract)'s: each is a **named log-state property**, never
interpolated into the message — which is also what that subsection's CWE-117 rule requires, since a value
concatenated into a message text can forge a field boundary in the sink.

**Coverage:** [06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s numbered promotion-gate tests — the ones
asserting the record cardinality per request, the closed field set and the rejection paths — which section
[2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) stage 2 item 13 places in this document's suite and counts
there rather than as parity rows, together with
[06 §10.2.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s own requirement of one summary record per replica per
hour. **An earlier form of this line read "rows 40 and 41 of section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage)"; both citations are deleted rather than renumbered**, because row 40
asserts album input integrity on the administration writes and row 41 the administration delete of an
absent row — neither has ever named this endpoint, and no numbered parity row does.

## 8. Views, static assets and the wire contracts

### 8.1 Bundling and static assets — no bundler

Five bundles are registered [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:11], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:14], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:19],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:22], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:26], and two token forms in them are the real obstacle rather than the bundling: a
**`{version}` token** — `"~/Scripts/jquery-{version}.js"` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:12] — and **glob tokens** —
`"~/Scripts/jquery.validate*"` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:15] and `"~/Scripts/modernizr-*"` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:20]. No successor supports either
form ([12 F-12-02](12-migration-blockers.md)).

**Resolution: no bundler at all.**

- **The web root becomes `wwwroot`, served by static-file middleware** (section
  [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order)). **What moves into it is not the whole source inventory**,
  and this bullet deliberately states no count of its own: the 27 files under `Content/`, `Scripts/`,
  `Images/` and `fonts/`
  (`git ls-files 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/*' 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Scripts/*' 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Images/*' 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/fonts/*' | wc -l` → `27`)
  each take **one** of three outcomes — relocate, replace or remove — and section
  [8.1.1](#811-the-per-file-disposition-of-the-27-source-assets) is the single owner of that
  disposition, file by file, with its arithmetic closing on 27 and its target payload closing on **13
  served files**. Only **six** of the 27 are the application's own and relocate; the web-root
  `favicon.ico`, which is not one of the 27, relocates as a seventh. Relocating all 27 would serve two
  versions of jQuery and two of Bootstrap from one web root, which is why that subsection exists.
- Cache busting uses the framework's **version-appending tag helper** on `<script>` and `<link>`
  elements, which appends a content hash. That replaces the `{version}` token's purpose — the token
  resolved a *filename* version, the tag helper appends a *content* version, which is strictly better
  for cache correctness and needs no filename convention.
- **The reason a bundler is not reintroduced:** minification and concatenation would require a
  JavaScript toolchain — a package manifest, a lock file, a build step and a CI dependency — for
  **27 asset files** on an application that has no build automation of any kind today
  ([08 §7.2](08-technical-debt-register.md)). That is a permanent build dependency bought for a
  one-time size saving on a catalog application. It is not justified, and if it ever becomes justified
  it is an additive decision taken then.
- **All 11 helper call sites are rewritten**, because both helpers cease to exist along with the five
  bundle virtual paths they name: **10** `@Scripts.Render` and **1** `@Styles.Render`
  (`git grep -o '@Scripts.Render' -- 'src/MVC5/*.cshtml' | wc -l` → `10`; the same for
  `@Styles.Render` → `1`). **Four are in the shared layout** — `@Styles.Render("~/Content/css")`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:7], `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/modernizr")`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:8], `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/jquery")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:41] and `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/bootstrap")`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:42] — **and the remaining seven** sit in the Account, Checkout and StoreManager views, each inside a
  `@section Scripts` block and each naming the same `~/bundles/jqueryval` path:
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml:35],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Login.cshtml:57],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:28],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Register.cshtml:40],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Checkout/AddressAndPayment.cshtml:8],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/StoreManager/Create.cshtml:71] and
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/StoreManager/Edit.cshtml:72]. `4 + 7 = 11`. Each becomes a direct
  `<script>` or `<link>` element with the tag helper — **except the first of the seven**, whose view the
  external-login split deletes (section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types)), so **10 of the
  11 source sites are rewritten and one disappears with its file**. The 11 is a source census and stays
  11; what it does not tell a reader is how many rewrites land, which is why the difference is stated.
- **Two bundle members do not come across at all**, because the libraries they name are removed rather
  than updated: `respond.js` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:24] and the modernizr
  bundle [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:19-20]. Both exist for browsers the target does not support. [04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)
  owns their removal and [06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) states the browser matrix; section
  [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas) lists the narrowed matrix as an approved delta.
- **The casing is corrected in the move.** The style bundle registers `"~/Content/site.css"`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:28] while the tracked file is
  `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css` — verified: the directory holds `Site.css`,
  `bootstrap.css` and `bootstrap.min.css`, and the registration's lowercase `s` matches none of them.
  IIS resolves this; a case-sensitive filesystem does not, and the stylesheet 404s with no error
  anywhere. Every asset reference is therefore emitted against the **actual** filename after the move.
  [11 §3.7](11-cloud-readiness-assessment.md) owns the finding and
  [06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns the audit that gates its hosting recommendation.

Client-side library pins and the acquisition mechanism, including `libman.json`, are
[04 §9](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s. This document names no version.

#### 8.1.1 The per-file disposition of the 27 source assets

**"Relocate the 27 assets" is not a migration plan, and taken literally it produces a broken
application.** Twenty-one of the 27 are the client libraries and their development companions that
[04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) replaces or removes — Bootstrap 3 stylesheets, jQuery
1.10.2, a source map for a file being deleted, two IntelliSense stubs, a vsdoc file, Respond, Modernizr
and the Bootstrap 3 Glyphicon fonts. Copying them into `wwwroot` alongside the pinned successors would
serve two versions of jQuery and two of Bootstrap from one web root. **Only six of the 27 are the
application's own**, and only those relocate.

**How the reference counts below are measured, because the obvious command gets them wrong.** A
repository-wide `git grep` for an asset's file name matches
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/MvcMusicStore.csproj`, whose 61 `<Content Include=…>` items
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/MvcMusicStore.csproj:192-266] name **every** asset by construction — a build
manifest entry is not a reference — and it also matches the two SVG files' own Inkscape export metadata
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Images/logo.svg:18]. Every count in this section is therefore measured over the
surfaces that can actually reference an asset at runtime:

```bash
git grep -n '<pattern>' -- 'src/MVC5/*.cshtml' 'src/MVC5/*.cs' \
                           'src/MVC5/*.css'    'src/MVC5/*.config'
```

Every file has exactly one outcome, and the arithmetic closes:

| Source path | Outcome | Target path, or the reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Content/Site.css` | **Relocate and adapt** | `wwwroot/css/site.css`. The lowercase target name is deliberate: it settles the mismatch between the registration `"~/Content/site.css"` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:28] and the tracked `Content/Site.css` by standardising on one lowercase convention, and it is where section [8.5.5](#855-contentsitecss--the-named-change-list)'s rule-by-rule rewrite lands |
| `Images/home-showcase.png` | **Relocate** | `wwwroot/images/`. Referenced at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:7] |
| `Images/placeholder.png` | **Relocate** | `wwwroot/images/`. Referenced from the seed constant [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:13], which is why it is also the subject of [06 §3.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s data-supplied casing gate |
| `Images/logo.png` | **Relocate — but unreferenced** | `wwwroot/images/`. See the note below |
| `Images/logo.svg` | **Relocate — but unreferenced** | `wwwroot/images/` |
| `Images/placeholder.svg` | **Relocate — but unreferenced** | `wwwroot/images/` |
| `Content/bootstrap.css`, `Content/bootstrap.min.css` | **Remove — superseded** | The pinned Bootstrap successor ([04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)) replaces both, and section [8.5](#85-the-bootstrap-upgrade-is-markup-work-not-a-version-bump) is the markup work that makes the replacement safe |
| `Scripts/jquery-1.10.2.js`, `Scripts/jquery-1.10.2.min.js`, `Scripts/jquery-1.10.2.min.map` | **Remove — superseded** | The pinned jQuery successor. The `.min.map` is a source map **for a file being deleted**, so it has nothing left to map |
| `Scripts/jquery.validate.js`, `Scripts/jquery.validate.min.js` | **Remove — superseded** | The pinned `jquery-validation` successor |
| `Scripts/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.js`, `Scripts/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.min.js` | **Remove — superseded** | The pinned `jquery-validation-unobtrusive` successor, which is a **replacement** rather than an update ([04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)) |
| `Scripts/bootstrap.js`, `Scripts/bootstrap.min.js` | **Remove — superseded** | Replaced by the Bootstrap **bundle** file, for the Popper reason [04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) gives |
| `Scripts/_references.js` | **Remove — development-only** | A Visual Studio IntelliSense reference file. It is served to no browser, and the reference probe above for `_references\.js` returns **no match** — nothing in any view, class, stylesheet or configuration file names it |
| `Scripts/jquery-1.10.2.intellisense.js` | **Remove — development-only** | An IntelliSense companion, not a runtime file |
| `Scripts/jquery.validate-vsdoc.js` | **Remove — development-only** | A vsdoc companion, not a runtime file |
| `Scripts/respond.js`, `Scripts/respond.min.js` | **Remove — no successor** | A media-query polyfill for Internet Explorer 8. Removal is part of the narrowed browser matrix, an approved delta (section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas)); its bundle membership [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:24] is the rewrite that does not happen (section [8.1.3](#813-the-rendered-tags-and-every-bundle-path-they-replace)) |
| `Scripts/modernizr-2.6.2.js` | **Remove — no successor** | Feature detection for the same era. Its layout call [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:8] is deleted rather than rewritten |
| `fonts/glyphicons-halflings-regular.eot`, `.svg`, `.ttf`, `.woff` | **Remove — unused after the icon decision** | All four exist solely to render the Glyphicons that section [8.5.4](#854-glyphicons-are-removed-rather-than-replaced) removes. No icon library replaces them, so no font files replace them |
| `favicon.ico` (web root, **outside** the 27) | **Relocate** | `wwwroot/`. Worth one note: **no view references it** — the reference probe above for `favicon` returns no match, so there is no `<link rel="icon">` anywhere and the only mention of the file is its build-manifest item [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/MvcMusicStore.csproj:194]. It is served purely by the browser's root-path convention, which the target's static-file middleware satisfies from the same location |

**`1 + 5 + 11 + 3 + 3 + 4 = 27`** — one relocated-and-adapted, five relocated images, eleven superseded,
three development-only, three with no successor, four Glyphicon fonts — plus the favicon, which is
relocated and is not one of the 27.

**Three images are unreferenced, and they are relocated anyway.** `logo.png`, `logo.svg` and
`placeholder.svg` are referenced by nothing: the reference probe above returns **no match** for any of
the three, against exactly one match each for `home-showcase.png`
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:7] and `placeholder.png`
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:13]. **Deleting brand
assets is a product decision, not a technical-assessment one**, so they move with the rest and are
**flagged for a product decision** rather than dropped on the assessment's own authority. The cost of
carrying them is three files; the cost of being wrong about them is a logo nobody can find.

**The target payload, stated separately from the source inventory, because they are different sets and
different sizes:**

| Group | Count | Contents |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Relocated, application-owned | 7 | `wwwroot/css/site.css`, five files under `wwwroot/images/`, and `wwwroot/favicon.ico` |
| New, application-owned | 1 | `wwwroot/js/shopping-cart.js` (section [8.1.2](#812-the-externalized-cart-script)) |
| Acquired and committed under `wwwroot/lib/` | 13 | Exactly the files [04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s manifest selects, listed there and not re-selected here: `jquery/jquery.js`, `jquery/jquery.min.js`, `jquery/jquery.min.map`; `jquery-validation/jquery.validate.js`, `jquery-validation/jquery.validate.min.js`, `jquery-validation/additional-methods.js`, `jquery-validation/additional-methods.min.js`; `jquery-validation-unobtrusive/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.js`, `jquery-validation-unobtrusive/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.min.js`; `bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css`, `bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css.map`, `bootstrap/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js`, `bootstrap/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js.map` |
| **Served total** | **21** | `7 + 1 + 13` |

**Thirteen acquired files from four libraries, and the gap between those two numbers is what this row is
easiest to get wrong on.** The manifest has **four** `libraries` entries and not one of them selects a
single file: jQuery selects three, jQuery Validation four, the unobtrusive adapter two and Bootstrap
four, so the file count is `3 + 4 + 2 + 4 = 13` rather than 4. The selection is deliberately **not
uniform across the four**, and the three reasons are all
[04 §9.5](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s: both the minified and the unminified build of each
jQuery-family file, because the unminified one is what a Development-time reference requests (section
[8.1.3](#813-the-rendered-tags-and-every-bundle-path-they-replace)); only the compiled Bootstrap builds,
because nothing references its sources; and a source map only where the file it maps is itself acquired,
which is three of the thirteen. [04 §9.3](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) states the three counts that
get conflated here — six source package dispositions, four acquired libraries, thirteen acquired files —
and this row uses the third, whose owner is [04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s manifest.

**Two glyphs the target renders are inside one of those files rather than beside them, and that changes a
header rather than this count.** The acquired stylesheet carries its icon-like assets as
`data:image/svg+xml` background images — among them the navbar toggler's glyph consumed by
`.navbar-toggler-icon` and the checked mark of `.form-check-input`, both adopted by section
[8.5.3](#853-non-class-markup-that-changes-with-the-library) and the token matrix of section
[8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens). **No file is added and this table does not
move**: the served total stays **21** and [04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s manifest stays at
four entries and thirteen files. What they require is an image content-security-policy that admits the
`data:` scheme, which [06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns and decides — and the same
section requires both controls to be **seen rendering** under the enforced policy, because a blocked
embedded image produces an empty button and an unticked checkbox with no server-side signal at all.

So the port **serves 21 static files where the source directory holds 28**, and the two sets barely
overlap: **21 of the 28 do not come across at all** — the eleven superseded vendored-library files, the
three development-only companions, the three files of the two removed polyfill libraries and the four
Glyphicon fonts, `11 + 3 + 3 + 4` from the disposition table — and the **7** that do are joined by
**1** new application file and the **13** acquired ones. Wherever the figure 27 appears in this document
set it is the **assessed source inventory**; the served payload is the table above.

#### 8.1.2 The externalized cart script

**The application has exactly one inline `<script>` block, and it has to leave the page.**
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:7-35] is the whole of the application's
JavaScript — 29 lines inside a `@section Scripts` block [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:6], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:36] — and
[06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires it externalized so the content-security policy
can be `script-src 'self'` with **no `unsafe-inline` and no nonce machinery**. That document owns the
policy; this section owns the artifact, because the target inventory is this document's.

**The artifact:** **`src/MvcMusicStore/wwwroot/js/shopping-cart.js`**, mapped from
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:7-35]. It is **page-specific, not
layout-wide** — it binds a handler that exists only on the cart page — so it is emitted from that page's
scripts section rather than from `_Layout.cshtml`, with `asp-append-version="true"` like every other
asset (section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler)).

**Its path on disk and its URL are different strings, and only one of them is assertable in a response.**
The file sits at `src/MvcMusicStore/wwwroot/js/shopping-cart.js`; the view writes `src="~/js/shopping-cart.js"`;
and the browser receives **`/js/shopping-cart.js`** with a version query string appended. `wwwroot` is the
web root, so it is a prefix the URL never carries — which is why section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage) the coverage assertion requires the **public URL** and would fail a correct implementation if
it asserted the disk path.

**Load position and order, which is a correctness requirement and not a preference.** The script calls
`$(function () { … })` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:8] at parse time, so **jQuery must already be loaded when it runs**. The order
is therefore jQuery, then this file, and on the form pages the validation chain must load in its own
fixed order — jQuery, `jquery-validation` with its `additional-methods` companion,
`jquery-validation-unobtrusive` — because each depends on the ones before it.
[04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) fixes the manifest and
[04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)
[04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) the resulting order; this
document renders the tags in it (section
[8.1.3](#813-the-rendered-tags-and-every-bundle-path-they-replace)), and section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage) **row 101** asserts the rendered order — every element's position in the
parsed document — rather than trusting it.

**Required behaviour, itemized against the source so nothing is silently dropped.** Every current
behaviour is preserved; five are added, and each addition is a requirement stated elsewhere rather than
an invention here.

| Behaviour | Source | Target requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bind to the removal controls on ready | `$(".RemoveLink").click(…)` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:10] | Unchanged selector — `RemoveLink` is retained as a class hook (section [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens)) — but it now binds to a `<button type="button">` rather than an anchor (section [8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements) item **a6**), which is what makes the control keyboard-operable |
| Read the record id and the post URL from the control | `$(this).attr("data-id")`, `$(this).attr("data-url")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:12-13], guarded by `!= ''` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:14] | Unchanged, guard included. The URL stays server-rendered onto the control rather than constructed in script |
| Post the removal | `$.post(PostToUrl, { "id": recordToDelete }, …)` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:17] | Unchanged **transport**: the body stays **form-urlencoded** with the single field `id`, because that is jQuery's default serialization and no `contentType` is set. **Added:** the `RequestVerificationToken` **header**, read from the page-rendered token — the contract is section [7.4](#74-problem-three--cart-removal-posts-without-a-form)'s and is not restated here |
| Fade out an emptied row | `if (data.ItemCount == 0) { $('#row-' + data.DeleteId).fadeOut('slow') }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:21-22] | Unchanged, **plus** suppression under `prefers-reduced-motion` (section [8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements) item **c5**) and the focus move of item **c4**, because the faded row contains the control that currently holds focus |
| Update a reduced row's count | `$('#item-count-' + data.DeleteId).text(data.ItemCount)` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:24] | Unchanged |
| Update the cart total | `$('#cart-total').text(data.CartTotal)` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:27] | Unchanged |
| Update the message | `$('#update-message').text(data.Message)` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:28] | Unchanged target — the element exists [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:44-45] — **plus** the `role="status" aria-live="polite"` attributes on that container (item **c1**), which is what makes the update audible |
| Update the cart badge | `$('#cart-status').text('Cart (' + data.CartCount + ')')` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:29] | **Dropped, and nothing is invented to receive it.** `#cart-status` addresses an id **no view in the application emits**, so this write already lands nowhere and the badge is server-rendered only. The ported script performs the four writes above and **not** this one; section [8.2.1](#821-the-cartsummary-component-dom-contract) fixes that as the contract, retires the identifier, and makes the cart page's own `#update-message` region the removal's status surface |

**Two properties of the writes, stated because they are easy to lose in a rewrite.**

- **Every DOM write stays text-only.** The source uses `.text(…)` at all four update sites [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:24], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:27],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:28], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:29] and never `.html(…)`. That is preserved as a **requirement**, not an accident: `Message`
  is composed from the album title [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:75-76],
  and an album title is administrator-supplied free text, so an `.html(…)` rewrite would turn a catalog
  field into a script-injection vector. [09](09-security-assessment.md) owns the exposure; this is the
  line of code that keeps it closed.
- **The payload reads keep their PascalCase names** — **seven reads over five distinct properties**, the
  two extra being on line [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:24], which selects by `data.DeleteId` and writes `data.ItemCount` in one
  statement. Section [8.7](#87-the-json-contract--annotate-one-model-not-the-policy) owns the decision and
  [12 F-12-16](12-migration-blockers.md) states the same five and seven. Moving the code into a file
  changes nothing about either count.

**Three behaviours are added because the source has none of them**, and they are the reason this is a
specified artifact rather than a copy-paste:

- **A pending state.** The control is disabled and carries `aria-busy="true"` from the moment the post
  is issued until it settles, then re-enabled — success **or** failure (item **c2**). Today a
  double-click posts twice.
- **A failure path.** The source handler has a success callback and nothing else [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:17-30]: no `.fail`,
  no `error` callback, no status inspection. A rejected removal — including one rejected by the
  anti-forgery validation this port adds — is **completely silent**, and the user believes the item was
  removed. The target handles the failure, leaves the row untouched, and writes a visible message into
  the announced status region (item **c3**).
- **Focus management** across the row removal (item **c4**).

**One consequence for the enforced policy.** With this file in place, the cart page emits **no inline
script at all**, so `script-src 'self'` holds with nothing excepted.
[06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) requires cart removal to be exercised under the
**enforced** policy — not merely the report-only phase — before that phase ends, because a blocked
script produces a page that renders perfectly and silently does nothing.

#### 8.1.3 The rendered tags, and every bundle path they replace

[04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) fixes the manifest, the file selection and the versions, and
[04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) fixes the resulting order and the reason for each ordering
constraint. **This document renders them**, and names no version.

**The elements, with their placement.** Every one carries `asp-append-version="true"`, which is what
replaces the `{version}` token's purpose (section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler)).
The table gives the **deployed** form; the blocks after it state the Development variant and the one
library file whose reference site [04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) assigns to this section.

**The `~/` in these attributes is view source, not what the browser sees.** Each element below is written
as it appears in the `.cshtml` file; the tag helper resolves `~/` against the application root and appends
the version, so the rendered `href` and `src` are `/lib/…`, `/css/site.css` and `/js/shopping-cart.js`
with a query string — **never `wwwroot/…`**, which is the web root and appears in no URL. Section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage) the coverage assertion requires the rendered form for that reason.

| Where | Element |
| --- | --- |
| `_Layout.cshtml`, in `<head>`, at the position of today's `@Styles.Render` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:7] | `<link rel="stylesheet" href="~/lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css" asp-append-version="true" />` |
| `_Layout.cshtml`, in `<head>`, immediately after it | `<link rel="stylesheet" href="~/css/site.css" asp-append-version="true" />` |
| `_Layout.cshtml`, end of `<body>`, at the position of today's `@Scripts.Render("~/bundles/jquery")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:41] | `<script src="~/lib/jquery/jquery.min.js" asp-append-version="true"></script>` |
| `_Layout.cshtml`, immediately after it, at the position of [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:42] | `<script src="~/lib/bootstrap/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js" asp-append-version="true"></script>` |
| Then, unchanged | `@RenderSection("scripts", required: false)` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:43] |

**The Development variant, which is why the manifest acquires two builds of each jQuery-family file.**
[04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) selects both the minified and the unminified build of
`jquery`, `jquery.validate`, `additional-methods` and `jquery.validate.unobtrusive` — four pairs — and
[04 §9.5](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) assigns the elements that choose between them to this
section. The choice is made with the framework's `<environment>` tag helper, registered along with the
rest of the tag-helper set in `Views/_ViewImports.cshtml` (section
[8.6](#86-view-serving-and-_viewimports)): the **four** script elements above that name those files — the
layout's jQuery element and the form pages' three — are each written **twice**,
once inside `<environment include="Development">` naming the unminified file, once inside
`<environment exclude="Development">` naming the minified one — in the same position and the same order
either way, so the load order of section [8.1.2](#812-the-externalized-cart-script) holds in both
environments. **Two elements have no variant and are deliberately not wrapped**: the Bootstrap
stylesheet and the Bootstrap bundle, because only their compiled builds are acquired
([04 §9.5](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)), so a wrapper around them would offer a choice between one
file and itself. `wwwroot/css/site.css` and `wwwroot/js/shopping-cart.js` have a single build each and
are not wrapped either.

**That preserves a behaviour the source already has rather than adding one.** `@Scripts.Render` emits a
bundle's members as individual **unminified** files while `<compilation debug="true">` is in force
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Web.config:33], and the single minified bundle once the Release transform has
removed that attribute [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Web.Release.config:18]. The target has no bundler and
minifies nothing, so that debug-versus-release distinction survives **only** as a choice between two
already-acquired files — which is what the manifest's four pairs are for, and why omitting the wrapper
would leave four committed, published files referenced by nothing.

**Which pages reference `additional-methods` — the one question
[04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) leaves to this section.** **All six form pages**, in the row
above, between the core plugin and the unobtrusive adapter. It is absent from
[04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s table because that table fixes the order of the **four
libraries** and this file travels inside one of them beside its own core file; its reference site is this
section's statement, made here so that no acquired file is committed, published and referenced by
nothing. Three properties of the decision:

- **It must load after `jquery.validate`**, which defines the validator it extends. It may load before or
  after the adapter, which reads its rules at document ready; the position above is the stricter of the
  two and is the one the elements render.
- **It changes no rendered field's validation.** Unobtrusive validation runs only the rules the server
  emitted as `data-val-*` attributes, and the application's annotations emit a **closed set of five** —
  `required`, `length`, `range`, `equalto` and `regex`, from `[Required]`, `[StringLength]`, `[Range]`,
  `[Compare]` and `[RegularExpression]` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Order.cs:20-58],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Album.cs:16-27],
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/AccountViewModels.cs:7-60]; the `[DataType]` and `[Display]`
  annotations alongside them emit no rule at all. An element that registers further validator methods
  therefore adds no rule to any field this application renders, which is why this is **not** an approved
  delta (section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas)) even though the source's `Scripts/` folder
  contains no such file.
- **What it buys is the failure it removes.** The pinned plugin's distribution is two files at this
  version, and referencing only the first is exactly the silent-non-running rule
  [04 §9.5](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) names: a future annotation whose client rule lives in the
  second file would validate on the server and silently not in the browser, which surfaces as a
  validation message that appears only after a round trip.

The seven source form-page sites are
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml:35],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Login.cshtml:57],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:28],

[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/StoreManager/Edit.cshtml:72] — verified with
`git grep -n 'Scripts.Render' -- 'src/MVC5/*.cshtml'`, which returns 10 lines of which these seven name
the validation bundle. **7 + 3 layout script calls = 10 `@Scripts.Render`**, and the layout's single
`@Styles.Render` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:7] completes the 11 of section
[8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler).

**Six of those seven become a `<script>` element; the seventh does not exist in the target.**
`Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml` is deleted by the external-login split (sections
[8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types), [8.4](#84-the-view-disposition-by-semantic-role)), so
the table row above applies to **six** form pages — `Account/Login`, `Account/Manage`,
`Account/Register`, `Checkout/AddressAndPayment`, `StoreManager/Create` and `StoreManager/Edit`.
**Six of those seven form pages take the rewrite, and the seventh is gone.**
`Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml` is one of the four views removed with the external-login

source counts above are source counts and stand as measured; the **ported** figures are **6** validation

**Two bundle members therefore have no target element at all** — `modernizr-*` and `respond.js` — which
is the same fact section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler) states as a consequence of the
browser matrix, expressed here as the two rewrites that do not happen. A port that mechanically rewrote
every `@Scripts.Render` into a `<script>` would emit two elements pointing at files that no longer exist,
and static-file middleware would answer both with 404 while the page rendered normally.

**jQuery is retained only because the unobtrusive validation adapter requires it**, which is
[04 §9.6](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)'s statement and is not re-argued here.

#### 8.1.4 The four `@Url.Content` call sites, mapped

**`@Url.Content` survives the port, and saying only that is not a mapping.** `IUrlHelper.Content` exists
in ASP.NET Core and resolves a leading `~/` against the application's path base, so every one of the four
source call sites is source-compatible and none is rewritten into a different helper. What differs site by
site is *what the helper is asked to resolve*: three of the four resolve a value that comes out of the
**database**, and the fourth resolves a path that names an **action**. Both are seams, so each site is
mapped here with its target expression, its emitted URL and the assertion that pins it.

| Site | Source expression | Target expression | Emitted URL, and what pins it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:15] | `@Url.Content( @album.AlbumArtUrl)` — the stray inner `@` and the space after the parenthesis are source noise the port drops | `@Url.Content(album.AlbumArtUrl)`, inside the absent-value guard section [8.10](#810-absent-album-art--the-rendering-rule) adds | Whatever the stored value resolves to, which is the subject of the two paragraphs below. Section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) row 23 `23a` collects this `img[src]` from the rendered page and requires it to answer **200** at the **exact rendered casing** |
| [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Browse.cshtml:17] | `@Url.Content(@album.AlbumArtUrl)` | `@Url.Content(album.AlbumArtUrl)`, and the source's `String.IsNullOrEmpty` guard [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Browse.cshtml:15] becomes section [8.10](#810-absent-album-art--the-rendering-rule)'s whitespace-aware one | As the row above |
| [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Details.cshtml:10] | `@Url.Content(@Model.AlbumArtUrl)` | `@Url.Content(Model.AlbumArtUrl)`, inside the same guard | As the row above |
| [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml:75] | `@Url.Content("~/ShoppingCart/RemoveFromCart")`, on the removal control's `data-url` attribute | Unchanged | `/ShoppingCart/RemoveFromCart`. It is a **string-built action path rather than a route-generated one**, and it is deliberately kept that way: under the single conventional route of section [2.2](#22-the-five-application_start-registrations-do-not-share-one-fate) the emitted value is identical either way, and the attribute is what the externalized script reads (section [8.1.2](#812-the-externalized-cart-script)). What makes the string safe is the assertion rather than the helper — row 28 requires the attribute to be **exactly** `/ShoppingCart/RemoveFromCart`, so a route change that invalidated it fails a test instead of a visitor's removal |

**The three album-art sites resolve data, and the committed data does not survive the asset relocation
untouched.** Every album in the committed catalog carries one stored value — `~/Images/placeholder.png`,
from the seed constant [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:13] — while section
[8.1.1](#811-the-per-file-disposition-of-the-27-source-assets) relocates that asset to
**`wwwroot/images/placeholder.png`**, lowercase. `Url.Content` resolves the tilde and changes nothing
else, so a value carried across verbatim renders `/Images/placeholder.png`: served by the source's
case-insensitive host, and **404 on Linux**. That is not a hypothetical — it is exactly what row 23 `23a`
measures, so an implementation that carried the value across would fail its own coverage rather than fail
quietly in production. Two things follow, and they are the whole of the fix:

- **The migrated value is transformed, and the transform is declared where the migration's projection is
  declared** rather than here. `Album.AlbumArtUrl` moves out of section
  [5.6](#56-the-data-migration-executor)'s *carried unchanged* bucket into its *transformed* bucket for
  the values that name a relocated repository asset: the asset's path segment is lowercased to the target
  name section 8.1.1 fixes, so `~/Images/placeholder.png` becomes `~/images/placeholder.png`. Any other
  value — an administrator-entered absolute URL, for instance — is carried unchanged, because nothing in
  the served inventory corresponds to it. **That is this document's decision for a non-matching value and
  it is stated once, here: carried unchanged, with no placeholder substituted at migration time.** The
  distinction the two rules turn on is *absence*, not *resolvability* — section
  [8.10](#810-absent-album-art--the-rendering-rule)'s render-time placeholder applies where
  `String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace` holds, so a value that is present but resolves to nothing renders as it does
  today and the migration does not rewrite it either. Substituting a placeholder for a non-matching value
  would rewrite stored data on a guess about what the administrator meant and would discard the only
  record of what was entered, which is the opposite of what a data migration is for.
  **[03](03-modernization-roadmap.md) W5 states the same rule, and an earlier form of this bullet recorded
  it as a contradiction.** That earlier form read that 03 *"requires a placeholder on this branch"* and
  that the requirement contradicted this decision, leaving it to 03 to align; the two are now converged
  and the withdrawal is recorded rather than the disagreement. 03 W5's step 4 leaves a value with **no
  match at any casing exactly as it is** and logs the row for review — substituting nothing, at
  migration time or at render time — and its step 5 gate is what **refuses** such a value rather than
  repairing it. So this bullet and that step are one rule stated from two ends: this document owns the
  application's render rule and the migration's projection, 03 W5 owns the audit and the gate, and neither
  rewrites stored data on a guess. The residual case — a stored
  value the transform did not cover that then fails to serve on Linux — is caught by the data-supplied
  casing gate [06 §3.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns, which **reports** it rather than
  rewriting it.
- **The ported seed writes the target path directly.** The seeding command of section
  [5.4](#54-seeding--the-guard-fails-closed-on-three-checks) carries `~/images/placeholder.png` as its
  constant, so a freshly seeded non-production database needs no transform and the two paths — migrated
  and seeded — agree on one string.

[06 §3.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns the data-supplied casing gate that catches a stored
value the transform did not cover, and the repository-wide casing audit and the Linux serving gate are
that document's as well. This subsection owns only the four call sites, the target expressions and the
one transform the relocation makes necessary.

### 8.2 Child actions — three view components

Child actions do not exist in the target — [12 F-12-23](12-migration-blockers.md#f-12-23--mvc-child-actions)
is the blocker of record, and this section is its resolution for the migration source. MVC 5 declares
`[ChildActionOnly]` on **three** actions, and **each becomes a view component with its call site**, so
the target contains **three** view components: one class and one `Default.cshtml` per source action, and
no source child action left without a successor. The count matters in both directions — a plan promising
fewer components silently drops a rendered surface, and a plan promising more schedules work with no
source behind it.

| Source action | Renders | Target component | Call site to rewrite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `StoreController.GenreMenu` — `[ChildActionOnly]` at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreController.cs:43], the action body at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreController.cs:43-55] | The genre navigation in the shared layout | Class **`src/MvcMusicStore/ViewComponents/GenreMenuViewComponent.cs`**, view **`src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Components/GenreMenu/Default.cshtml`** | `@Html.Action("GenreMenu", "Store")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:25] |
| `ShoppingCartController.CartSummary` — `[ChildActionOnly]` at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:86], the action body at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:86-99] | The cart count in the same layout | Class **`src/MvcMusicStore/ViewComponents/CartSummaryViewComponent.cs`**, view **`src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Components/CartSummary/Default.cshtml`** | `@Html.Action("CartSummary", "ShoppingCart")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:26] |
| `AccountController.RemoveAccountList` — `[ChildActionOnly]` at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:316], the action body at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:316-322] | The external-login removal list — the **retained** management surface of section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) — on the account-management page | Class **`src/MvcMusicStore/ViewComponents/RemoveAccountListViewComponent.cs`**, view **`src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Components/RemoveAccountList/Default.cshtml`** | `@Html.Action("RemoveAccountList")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:22] |

**The exact target call sites, written once here so no other section restates them.** Each source
`@Html.Action` line becomes one awaited invocation, in the same position in the same file, with the
component named by string:

| Target file and position | Exact target line |
| --- | --- |
| `src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml`, replacing the source line at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:25] | `@await Component.InvokeAsync("GenreMenu")` |
| `src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml`, replacing the source line at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:26] | `@await Component.InvokeAsync("CartSummary")` |
| `src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml`, replacing the source line at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:22], inside the retained `<section id="externalLogins">` block | `@await Component.InvokeAsync("RemoveAccountList")` |

**Why this invocation form and not the tag-helper form.** `<vc:genre-menu />` is equivalent in effect,
but it resolves only in a view whose `_ViewImports.cshtml` carries an `@addTagHelper` directive naming
**this assembly** — a registration line with no source counterpart, whose omission fails by rendering the
literal element text rather than by erroring. `Component.InvokeAsync` needs no registration at all, so the
three call sites above are the complete change and there is no fourth file to keep in step. **No
`@addTagHelper` directive for this application assembly is added anywhere, and the tag-helper form of
these three invocations is deliberately not used.** The name passed is the component class name with the
`ViewComponent` suffix removed, which is the framework's own convention and is why `"GenreMenu"` resolves
`GenreMenuViewComponent`; each component's single `Default.cshtml` is found by the conventional
`Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml` path the table above gives, so no view path is passed at a
call site either. Each invocation is `await`ed because `InvokeAsync` is the asynchronous entry point all
three components declare — the two layout components query the database and the third awaits
`UserManager.GetLoginsAsync`.

**Every URL a view component generates names its controller as well as its action, and that is a
correctness rule here rather than a style preference.** A view component renders **inside the parent's
request**, so the ambient route values a controller-omitting overload falls back on are the *request's* —
not those of the controller the child action used to live on. `@Url.Action("Index")` inside
`GenreMenuViewComponent` would resolve against `HomeController` on `/`, against `StoreController` on
`/Store/Details/1` and against `ShoppingCartController` on `/ShoppingCart`: one expression, a different
URL on every page, and no compile error anywhere. The source already names the controller at four of the
five URL-generating expressions in these three views; the fifth is the defect this rule fixes.

| URL generated inside a component | Source expression | Target expression | Emitted URL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GenreMenu` — the dropdown toggle | `@Url.Action("Store")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/GenreMenu.cshtml:4] | `@Url.Action("Index", "Store")` | **`/Store`** — the catalog index. The source's single argument is read as an *action* named `Store` on the ambient controller, and `StoreController` declares only `Index`, `Browse`, `Details` and `GenreMenu` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreController.cs:16,27,36,44], so it emits `/Store/Store` and answers `404`. This is a **defect correction rather than an approved delta** — the toggle's label, position and surrounding chrome are unchanged and the path it named served nothing — so it carries no register row and is named with the other two link corrections in section [12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual). It is asserted by section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) row 9 |
| `GenreMenu` — each genre link | `@Html.ActionLink(genre.Name, "Browse", "Store", new { Genre = genre.Name }, null)` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/GenreMenu.cshtml:9-11] | The same generation, controller named as it is today; the anchor gains `dropdown-item` (section [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens)) | `/Store/Browse?Genre={name}`, URL-encoded |
| `GenreMenu` — the `More...` link | `@Html.ActionLink("More...", "Index", "Store")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/GenreMenu.cshtml:16] | Unchanged in form | `/Store` — the same path the toggle now reaches, which is why row 9 asserts both |
| `CartSummary` — the badge anchor | `@Url.Action("Index", "ShoppingCart")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:4] | Unchanged in form (section [8.2.1](#821-the-cartsummary-component-dom-contract)) | `/ShoppingCart` |
| `RemoveAccountList` — the removal form's action | `Html.BeginForm("Disassociate", "Account")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:16] | The form tag helper's `asp-controller="Account"` and `asp-action="Disassociate"`, which is the same pair named explicitly | `/Account/Disassociate` |

**So exactly one emitted URL changes**, and it changes from a path no action serves to the catalog index.
No other generated URL in the three components is affected by the conversion, because none of the other
four ever relied on the ambient controller.

Four specifics:

- **All three components get a typed view model, and the reason is contract safety rather than a missing
  API.** A view component **does** expose `ViewData`, `ViewBag` and `TempData` — `ViewComponent.ViewData`
  returns `ViewComponentContext.ViewData` and `ViewBag` is a dynamic wrapper over it — so the source's
  pattern (`ViewBag.CartCount` and `ViewBag.CartSummary`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs:95-96], read by the partial at
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:1], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:4], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:6]) would **compile and
  render** if carried across verbatim. What the target changes is the *direction* data flows: the
  component's `ViewData` is a **defensive copy** of the calling view's, so values the parent set are
  visible inside the component while **values the component sets are not visible to the parent** — the
  one pattern that fails silently. The reason for a typed model is therefore stated correctly:
  `ViewBag.CartCoount` is a runtime nothing in either framework and a compile error against a typed
  model, and a two-property class is a contract two files can be checked against. **Do not justify it
  by claiming view components lack `ViewData` — they do not, and a reviewer who checks that claim will
  discard the recommendation with it.**
- **The two layout components execute in the same request and the same scope, and one reachable case must
  be tested.** A
  child action ran as a nested action invocation; a view component executes inline during the parent's
  render, inside the same request scope and therefore against the **same** scoped `DbContext` as the
  parent's controller (section
  [4.2](#42-what-scoped-registration-actually-changes--and-what-it-does-not)) — including any entities
  that controller has added or modified **without saving**. Two consequences:
  - **No view component ever calls `SaveChangesAsync`.** Stated as a rule, because a component that did
    would commit whatever the parent action had left pending in the tracker.
  - **One target request genuinely reaches that state, and it is the test to write.** Of the three
    actions that write, `AddToCart` and a successful checkout both **redirect** — so the page that
    renders the components is a *different* request with a *different* scope and proves nothing — and
    `RemoveFromCart` returns JSON, which renders no layout and therefore no components at all. The one
    that does not is the **checkout failure path**: it returns `View(input)` after the write attempt
    (section [8.12](#812-the-checkout-write-path--one-ordered-contract)), so the layout — and with it
    both layout components — renders in a request whose context still tracks the added-but-uncommitted
    order and order-detail entities. The coverage assertion requires that both layout components render
    correctly there **and that nothing is persisted by that render**, which is the assertion the
    redirect-crossing test it replaces could never have made.
- **`RemoveAccountListViewComponent` is the third, and its model is where the adaptation work sits.** The
  source action reads the signed-in user's linked logins and passes them to a partial whose model is
  `ICollection<Microsoft.AspNet.Identity.UserLoginInfo>`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:1], with the remove button gated on
  `ViewBag.ShowRemoveButton` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:13] set from `HasPassword() || linkedAccounts.Count > 1`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:319-321]. Three things change and nothing
  else:
  - **The type name survives, the namespace and the producing API do not.** `UserLoginInfo` keeps its
    name under `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity`, but its shape differs — it carries
    `ProviderDisplayName` in addition to `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` — and it is obtained from
    `UserManager.GetLoginsAsync(user)` returning `IList<UserLoginInfo>` rather than from
    `UserManager.GetLogins(userId)`. So this is a namespace update **plus** an adaptation of how the
    collection is obtained and what the view reads from each element, not a rename.
  - **`ViewBag.ShowRemoveButton` becomes a model property**, for the reason the first specific gives: a
    value the *component* sets is not visible to the parent, and a value the parent sets is not the one
    the component computes. The component's model carries `IReadOnlyList<UserLoginInfo> Logins` and
    `bool ShowRemoveButton`, computed inside `InvokeAsync` from the same two conditions as the source —
    `await UserManager.HasPasswordAsync(user) || logins.Count > 1`. **This is the one surviving consumer
    of the source's `HasPassword()` helper** [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:364];
    its other two call sites, both feeding `ViewBag.HasLocalPassword` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:139], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:151], go with the removed
    set-password branch (section
    [6.4](#64-the-account-surface--authorization-map-redirect-safety-and-error-paths)), so the predicate
    moves here rather than disappearing. The expression is **preserved rather than folded**, even though
    the load halt of section
    [5.8](#58-roles-role-assignments-claims-and-external-logins--the-other-four-tables) means its first
    operand is true for every migrated account: simplifying it to `true` would encode that halt into
    rendering code, where a later decision to admit password-less accounts would silently change what the
    button does.
  - **The removal form's contract is preserved exactly.** The `Default.cshtml` posts `loginProvider` and
    `providerKey` to `Disassociate`
    [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:19-20], which is the action kept
    authorized in section [6.4](#64-the-account-surface--authorization-map-redirect-safety-and-error-paths);
    the anti-forgery token [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:17] is emitted by the form tag helper instead of the explicit call, and
    validated by the global filter of section [7.1](#71-the-policy).

  The `@Html.Action` call at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:22] becomes a component
  invocation and the `<section id="externalLogins">` block that contains it [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:21-24] is **kept**.

  **The one behavioural difference this conversion introduces, stated precisely because the loose version
  overstates it.** `/Account/RemoveAccountList` is not usable today either: the conventional route matches
  it, and `[ChildActionOnly]`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:316] then rejects the direct request by
  throwing, which the global `HandleErrorAttribute`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:10] turns into an error page. In the target **no route
  matches at all**, because a view component is not addressable, so the same request answers **404**
  instead. The capability is unchanged and the status code is not — which is why it is recorded as
  `D-33` rather than as a preserved contract, and asserted by the coverage assertion.
- **The two layout components query the database on every page render today, and the target treats them
  differently from each other — one is cached in the application's own SQL-backed cache, one is not cached
  at all.** This is the fourth specific and the only one that is a performance decision rather than a
  portability one. **This sub-section owns the caching mechanism entire — the store, the key, the lifetime
  and the invalidation — and [06 §6.4](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns only the hosting sizing
  that follows from it.** That division is not chosen here: the committed
  [11 §2](11-cloud-readiness-assessment.md) assigns it in its ownership table and repeats it in its two
  index rows, recording that 11 itself names no cache and no placement.

  **An earlier revision of this bullet handed the *store* decision to 06 and took a per-instance
  in-process, per-instance cache from it. Both halves are withdrawn, and the second is withdrawn for a
  defect rather than a preference.** The deployment is **not** single-instance: [06 §5](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)
  fixes a steady state of two instances and an autoscale ceiling of six. A per-instance cache can only be
  evicted by the instance that handles the write, so an administration write served by one replica leaves
  **every other replica** serving the superseded menu until its own entry expires — and the application
  cannot state a bound for that, because the number of replicas holding a stale copy is a platform fact
  and each copy expires on its own clock. "Cross-replica convergence is the expiry" is a description of
  that gap rather than a control over it. **The three administration writes exist precisely to make the
  menu correct sooner than the expiry**, so a store that cannot deliver their effect to the replica the
  next request lands on defeats the only reason invalidation is specified at all.

  **The store is therefore the application's SQL-backed `IDistributedCache`** — `dbo.SessionCache`, the
