**The 404 this sub-section previously specified is withdrawn, explicitly, and its argument is answered
rather than dropped.** An earlier form of this passage read *"Resolution: the branch returns
`NotFound()`, and the status is 404 rather than 403"*, on the ground that a 200 means "a request for an
order that is not yours succeeds, as far as any client can tell". Four things are wrong with shipping
that, and the first is decisive on its own:

- **It is an unapproved change to a user-visible response.** The set of approved deltas in section
  [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas) contains none for this surface and is not widened to
  create one, so a target answering 404 here would be a regression rather than a delta — which is
  precisely what coverage row 14's `14b` case exists to catch, and why that row states in its own text
  that the `200` "is **not** an approved delta".
- **The disclosure it was meant to close does not exist.** The argument against a 403 is sound — a 403
  would assert *this order exists and is not yours*, turning the action into an existence oracle for
  other customers' order ids, the same disclosure the cart-scoped lookup at census site `S3` closes
  (section [4.15](#415-query-failure-contracts--the-complete-branch-census)). But the source already
  merges the two cases: `Any(...)` is false for a nonexistent id **and** for another user's order, and
  both reach [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/CheckoutController.cs:81] with the identical response. A 404 would merge them too. So the 404 buys **no**
  reduction in disclosure over the preserved 200 — the merge, not the status, is what closes the oracle,
  and the merge is preserved either way.
- **The crawler and monitor concerns are answered by the authorization attribute, not by the status.**
  The class-level `[Authorize]` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/CheckoutController.cs:8] means an
  unauthenticated caller — every crawler, and every uncredentialed probe — receives the **302** to
  `/Account/Login` that coverage row 14's `14c` case asserts, and never sees the 200 at all. The only
  caller that reaches this response is an authenticated client asking for an order it does not own. A
  response no anonymous agent can obtain cannot be indexed as content or recorded as success by an
  external monitor.
- **The page carries no order data**, so even a stored copy of it discloses nothing: `14b`'s oracle
  asserts the absence of the order key and of all nine personal-data field values, and the dedicated
  view above contains two static headings and no model.

**What a future 404 would cost, recorded so the question is decided rather than reopened.** It would need
an approved delta of its own in section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas) with a named
approval owner; coverage row 14's `14b` oracle and its explanatory clause would both have to be rewritten,
and the three consumers that cite that row for the preserved response would have to move with it; the
status-code page would begin serving a 404 on a path reachable only by an authenticated caller, which the
`/Home/Error/404` action would then answer layout-free and with a trace identifier — so the change is a
change to the *rendered page* as well as to the status line; and the merged-case property would have to be
re-asserted from scratch, because it is currently inherited from the source rather than designed. None of
that is expensive, and none of it is this document's to decide unilaterally, which is the whole reason the
preserved behaviour is the specification and the alternative is a costed note.

The class-level `[Authorize]` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/CheckoutController.cs:8] still sends an
anonymous caller to the login page, unchanged, and **no separate coverage row is added for the
nonexistent-order input**: it is not a second behaviour to assert but the same single predicate failing,
so `14b`'s case establishes both branches by construction.

**One wording correction that belongs with this, because the capability is routinely overstated.**
`Complete` is the **only** order-reading surface in the application: it shows **one order, to its owner,
by id**. There is no order list, no order index and no order-history page anywhere in the migration
source — `git ls-files 'src/MVC5/*/Views/Checkout/*'` returns exactly two files,
`AddressAndPayment.cshtml` and `Complete.cshtml`, and the `View("Error")` at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/CheckoutController.cs:81] resolves to the
*shared* view above rather than to one of its own. Statements about preserving "the user's own orders"
mean exactly this one owner-scoped confirmation page, and the port owes nothing more.

**Do not attribute MVC 4's exception disclosure to this view.** MVC 4's disclosure is in its
*controller* — `ModelState.AddModelError("", e)` passing the exception object rather than a string
[src/MVC4/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:211-213], which
[09 §4.9](09-security-assessment.md) owns — and MVC 5's error view discloses nothing at all. This view
is rewritten for exactly one reason: its model type is gone.

**(2) `Views/Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml` — two separate problems in one file.**

- `Request.IsAuthenticated` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml:2] does not exist
  on the target's request type. **Resolution:** an explicit, null-handled identity check —
  `User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true` — because both `User` and `Identity` are reference-typed in
  the target and an unauthenticated request can present a non-null principal with a null name.
- `User.Identity.GetUserName()` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml:10] is an extension method from the Identity 1.0 namespace imported
  at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml:1]. **Resolution:** the namespace import is updated and the call becomes a direct read of the
  identity name, which is what the extension returned. The rendered text — `"Hello " + name + "!"` —
  is preserved exactly.

**Both signed-in and signed-out rendering need tests**, because the file's **entire structure** is a
conditional on the first of those two problems [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml:2-22]: the signed-in branch renders the sign-out form
and the manage link [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml:4-14], the signed-out branch renders register and log-in links [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml:18-21]. A
null-handling mistake does not error — it silently renders the wrong branch, and a suite that only
exercises one of them cannot tell.

**(3) `Views/Account/Manage.cshtml` — namespace import plus a rewritten call site.**
`@using Microsoft.AspNet.Identity;` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:2] becomes the
target's Identity namespace. Its `@Html.Action("RemoveAccountList")` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:22] becomes a **view-component
invocation** per section [8.2](#82-child-actions--three-view-components), and the surrounding
`<section id="externalLogins">` block [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:21-24] is **kept**, because the external-login **management**
surface is retained per the decision below. Two of its own invocations go with the **challenge** surface
that decision removes: the provider-list partial at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:23], and the `_SetPasswordPartial` arm of the
`ViewBag.HasLocalPassword` conditional at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:18], leaving [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:12-19] as an unconditional render of the
change-password partial [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:14]. Its `@Scripts.Render` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:28] is rewritten per section
[8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler).

**(4) `Views/Account/_ChangePasswordPartial.cshtml` — namespace import plus an identity read.**
`@using Microsoft.AspNet.Identity` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_ChangePasswordPartial.cshtml:1]
becomes the target's Identity namespace, and `@User.Identity.GetUserName()` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_ChangePasswordPartial.cshtml:4] becomes a direct
identity-name read, as in (2). Its `@Html.AntiForgeryToken()` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_ChangePasswordPartial.cshtml:8] disappears into automatic emission
(section [7.1](#71-the-policy)).

**(5) `Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml` — and `UserLoginInfo` is *not* renamed.**
`@model ICollection<Microsoft.AspNet.Identity.UserLoginInfo>`
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:1]. **The type name survives** — the
target's Identity keeps `UserLoginInfo` under its own namespace — so this looks like a one-word
namespace edit and is not: **the type's shape and the API that produces it both differ**, so the change
is a namespace update **plus** adaptation of how the collection is obtained (today
`UserManager.GetLogins(User.Identity.GetUserId())`
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:319], in the target
`UserManager.GetLoginsAsync(user)` returning `IList<UserLoginInfo>`) and of what the view reads from each
element (`account.LoginProvider` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:11], `account.ProviderKey` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:20]).

**The view is not deleted: it becomes the third view component's `Default.cshtml`**
(`src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Components/RemoveAccountList/Default.cshtml`, section
[8.2](#82-child-actions--three-view-components)), which is also where `ViewBag.ShowRemoveButton` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml:13]
becomes a typed model property. The adaptation above is therefore work this port does, not a hypothetical
it avoids.

**The external-login decision is CLOSED here, and this is the only statement of it in this document.**
[12 §7.3](12-migration-blockers.md) posed it as 05's choice — map `ChallengeResult` onto the framework's
external-challenge flow, or remove the disabled external-login surface entirely. **The choice is now
made, and neither of those two answers is it**, because the construct they treat as one thing is **two
surfaces** with different standing on the authoritative map. **The decision, final and admitting no third
reading, is three statements:**

| # | Half or construct | What it is | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Management** | An account's **existing** linked logins — listing them, and removing one | **RETAINED** |
| 2 | **Challenge** | Signing in with a provider, and linking a **new** one | **REMOVED** |
| 3 | **The external sign-in cookie** | The source's `UseExternalSignInCookie` registration [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:20] and the cookie it issues | **REMOVED, and removed *because* item 2 is** — a cookie exists to carry a handshake between a challenge and its callback, and with no challenge and no callback there is no handshake to carry. It is removed as a **surface**: no registration is written, no `SignInAsync` or `AuthenticateAsync` naming the external scheme appears anywhere in the target, and no cookie of that scheme is ever issued or read. The `AddIdentity` scheme *entry* that survives is stated below, and it is not this cookie |

**No later section re-opens any of the three.** Where another section describes the same constructs it
cites this table; where a source-state description mentions the external cookie it is describing MVC 5
and not the target.

**Why the management half is retained.** The AAP's authoritative file map carries
`src/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Components/RemoveAccountList/` — a `RemoveAccountListViewComponent.cs`
class and a `Default.cshtml` — and [04 §12.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) names both as created
artifacts, sourced from MVC 5's third `[ChildActionOnly]` action. That component exists for exactly one
purpose: rendering an account's registered external logins. Deleting the surface while creating its
component would be a self-contradiction, and deleting both would leave one of MVC 5's three child actions
with no successor — the one outcome [12 F-12-23](12-migration-blockers.md#f-12-23--mvc-child-actions)
does not permit. The half is also **not vestigial**: `AspNetUserLogins` rows migrate (below), so the list
it renders can be non-empty on the first day, and `Disassociate` is the action that acts on what it shows.

**Why the challenge half is removed.** No provider is registered and none ever was — all four
registrations are commented out with empty credentials
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:23-35], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:24-25], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:28-29], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:32-33] — so **nothing in
this half was reachable in any deployment of the source**. There is no behaviour to preserve, and mapping
it would re-express 27 lines of hand-rolled challenge plumbing
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:394-420] as framework calls that no request can
reach. That is not a neutral cost. The framework's `GetExternalLoginInfoAsync` has an overload that binds
the callback to the challenging principal and an overload that does not; the second compiles, passes
manual testing, and silently drops the check, so a victim who followed a link-completion URL prepared
under an attacker's challenge would acquire the attacker's external identity as a permanent alternative
sign-in path into their own account. Mapping would require that hazard to be got right, reviewed and
regression-tested in code no request can execute. Removing the half removes the hazard with it.

**What removal covers, itemized, so that nothing is left half-removed.**

| Source construct | Disposition in the target |
| --- | --- |
| `private class ChallengeResult : HttpUnauthorizedResult` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:394-420] and its `ExecuteResult(ControllerContext)` override [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:411] | **Removed with no replacement.** No custom action-result type is written, and no `ConfigureExternalAuthenticationProperties` or `Challenge(properties, provider)` call appears anywhere in the target |
| `IAuthenticationManager` property [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:338-344] | **Removed.** `SignInManager<ApplicationUser>` and `UserManager<ApplicationUser>` are constructor-injected (section [4.1](#41-the-ten-manual-instantiation-sites-constructor-injection-replaces)) and carry the account surface that remains |
| `XsrfKey` constant [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:336] and the user id the source threads through it | **Removed.** Nothing challenges, so there is no callback to correlate |
| `ExternalLogin` POST [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:200] | **Removed.** The route does not exist |
| `ExternalLoginCallback` GET [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:208-209] | **Removed.** The route does not exist |
| `ExternalLoginConfirmation` POST [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:262-265] and the `ExternalLoginConfirmationViewModel` it binds | **Removed**, that model class included — nothing else binds it |
| `ExternalLoginFailure` GET [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:311] | **Removed.** Its only callers were the two flows above |
| `LinkLogin` POST [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:237] | **Removed** |
| `LinkLoginCallback` GET [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:245] and the principal binding it performs, `GetExternalLoginInfoAsync(XsrfKey, User.Identity.GetUserId())` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:247] | **Removed.** This is the row mapping made dangerous and removal settles: the source's binding is correct, its framework equivalent is one omitted argument away from being wrong, and no surviving code has to reproduce it |
| The **set-password branch** of `Manage` POST [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:168-189], its `AddPasswordAsync` call [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:179], and the `SetPasswordSuccess` arm of the `Manage` GET status message [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:135] | **Removed.** The branch exists only for an account with no local password, and such an account is reachable only through a provider; with none registered it is a password-setting form with no authenticated route to it |
| `Views/Account/_ExternalLoginsListPartial.cshtml`, `Views/Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml`, `Views/Account/ExternalLoginFailure.cshtml`, `Views/Account/_SetPasswordPartial.cshtml` | **Removed** — the four views of the arithmetic below |
| The four commented-out provider registrations [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:23-35] | **Not re-created.** No `AddGoogle`, `AddFacebook`, `AddMicrosoftAccount` or `AddTwitter` call appears in `Program.cs`, and no provider package is pinned ([04 §7.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)) |
| External sign-in cookie registration [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:20] | **Removed** — item 3 of the decision table above. No equivalent registration is written, and no code path in the target issues, reads or expires a cookie of the external scheme. **What survives is a scheme entry, not a cookie**: `AddIdentity` registers `IdentityConstants.ExternalScheme` regardless (section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order)), and suppressing that entry would mean abandoning `AddIdentity` for `AddIdentityCore` and hand-wiring the sign-in manager, the role services and the cookie handler in order to delete a registration that never executes. The entry has **no flow**; the surface is gone |

**What retention covers — two constructs, whose contracts are unchanged.**

| Source construct | Target form |
| --- | --- |
| `Disassociate` POST [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:114] | **Retained.** `UserManager.RemoveLoginAsync(user, loginProvider, providerKey)` replaces the source's `RemoveLoginAsync(userId, new UserLoginInfo(...))` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:117], redirecting with `RemoveLoginSuccess` or `Error` exactly as today [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:116-126] |
| `RemoveAccountList` `[ChildActionOnly]` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:316-322] | **The third view component** of section [8.2](#82-child-actions--three-view-components). Its **route** disappears while its rendering does not, and its collection is obtained through `UserManager.GetLoginsAsync(user)` per item (5) above |

**The one retained action's verb and anti-forgery posture, stated because a disposition table does not
state a request contract and a wrong verb is invisible until a route answers a method it should not.**

| Action | Source verb and attributes | Target verb | Target anti-forgery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Disassociate` | **POST** — `[HttpPost]` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:112], `[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:113], authorized by the class-level `[Authorize]` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:15] | **POST**, `[Authorize]` | **Validated**, by the global `AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute` of section [7.1](#71-the-policy); no per-action attribute is written, and none is needed |

**Six routes are asserted absent rather than left undocumented**, because a removal nobody tests is
indistinguishable from a removal nobody made: `/Account/ExternalLogin`, `/Account/ExternalLoginCallback`,
`/Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation`, `/Account/ExternalLoginFailure`, `/Account/LinkLogin` and
`/Account/LinkLoginCallback` resolve to **no action** and answer **404**, authenticated or not.
`/Account/RemoveAccountList` answers 404 for a different reason — it is a component rather than an action
— and the difference matters only in that both are asserted. Section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage) carries them.

**Two retained views change because each invoked a removed one, and both changes belong to the port.**

- `Views/Account/Manage.cshtml` keeps its `<section id="externalLogins">` block
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:21-24] and the view-component invocation inside it
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:22], and **loses** the provider-list partial at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:23]. Its `ViewBag.HasLocalPassword` conditional
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:12-19] collapses to the change-password partial [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:14] alone, which is exactly the POST branch that
  survives (section
  [6.4](#64-the-account-surface--authorization-map-redirect-safety-and-error-paths)).
- `Views/Account/Login.cshtml` loses the provider-list partial at
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Login.cshtml:52] and the wrapper that exists only to hold it. The
  local sign-in form above it is untouched.

**The account with no local password: the halt stands, and its severity rises rather than falls.** An
account whose `PasswordHash` is null or empty has never had a local password, and in the source only an
external login could create one. Section
[5.8](#58-roles-role-assignments-claims-and-external-logins--the-other-four-tables) **halts the Identity
load** if any such account exists, and this decision makes that halt stricter: with the challenge half
removed there is no external sign-in **and** no set-password branch, so such an account has no route into
the application at all. The count is therefore known before cutover, the halt is not overridable from
this document, and the risk stays **open** in [07](07-effort-risks-sequencing.md)'s register until one of
two named responses is approved — a registered provider under its own scoped decision, or an
operator-driven local password reset for the affected accounts. Neither is assumed or supplied here.

**`AspNetUserLogins` migrates regardless of the removal, and the grants are what make that coherent.**
The table's rows **are** the management half's content, so they are loaded in full by section
[5.8](#58-roles-role-assignments-claims-and-external-logins--the-other-four-tables) and the authoritative
extraction's row count is reported to the data owner. The runtime identity holds **SELECT and DELETE** on
the table and **no INSERT** — SELECT because the component lists rows, DELETE because `Disassociate`
removes one, and no INSERT because no new external login can be created until a provider is approved and
that approval is a separate decision. [06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) publishes the grant
inventory; this section states the requirement the surface decision produces.

**The dead-scaffolding findings move in the right direction, and neither is closed here.** The dormant
challenge surface's standing as deployed attack surface is
[09 §6.11](09-security-assessment.md)'s finding and [08 §9.3](08-technical-debt-register.md)'s dead
scaffolding; removing it is what those findings ask for, and the retained management half is live code
with a real function rather than scaffolding. **Enabling a provider remains a separate decision owned by
Security**, and it is now additive work — a registration call, its pinned package, its secrets, its
actions, its views and its tests — rather than a switch. Section
[6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled) labels the management retention **preserved** and the
challenge removal an approved delta on that basis.

**This is approved delta `D-11`** of section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas) — the
external-login **challenge** surface is removed, and the external sign-in **cookie** is removed with it as
items 2 and 3 of the decision table above. **The delta names those two and nothing else.** The
management surface is preserved behaviour and is not a delta, and no second delta id is allocated for the
cookie, because a cookie whose only purpose is to carry the removed handshake is not a separate change.

**The view arithmetic, stated once and closed.** The migration source has **29** views under
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views` (`git ls-files 'src/MVC5/*/Views/**/*.cshtml' | wc -l` → `29`), and the
target has **25 ported + 4 removed with the challenge surface = 29**. The four removed are
`Account/_ExternalLoginsListPartial.cshtml`, `Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml`,
`Account/ExternalLoginFailure.cshtml` and `Account/_SetPasswordPartial.cshtml`. Section
[8.4](#84-the-view-disposition-by-semantic-role) carries the per-view disposition of all 29 and
reconciles to the same two numbers.

**Route and behaviour tests attach to what remains and to what is gone**: `Disassociate` resolves as an
authorized POST and removes exactly one login row; the `RemoveAccountList` component renders an account's
migrated rows and renders nothing where the account has none; `/Account/RemoveAccountList` and the six
removed routes answer 404; `Manage` renders the change-password branch only; and the sign-in, register,
sign-out and manage flows are otherwise unaffected. The coverage assertion in section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage) carries them.

### 8.4 The view disposition, by semantic role

**Twenty-nine views, twenty-nine dispositions, and the disposition is set by what a view *is* — a routed
page, a component's view, a rendered partial, the layout — not by whether its filename begins with an
underscore.** The distinction is not pedantry: `Store/GenreMenu.cshtml` and
`ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml` carry no underscore and are **not** pages — they are the rendered
bodies of the two `[ChildActionOnly]` actions of section
[8.2](#82-child-actions--three-view-components) — while `Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml` carries one and is
rendered into every page. A filename heuristic gets both wrong in opposite directions, and section
[12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual) depends on getting them right,
because it is the capture set.

Every view has exactly **one primary disposition** and the arithmetic closes:

| Disposition | Count | Views |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| **Ports unchanged** | 1 | `Views/_ViewStart.cshtml` |
| **Becomes a view component's `Default.cshtml`** | 3 | `Store/GenreMenu.cshtml`, `ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml`, `Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml` — section [8.2](#82-child-actions--three-view-components) |
| **Per-line rewrite — names a legacy type** | 4 | `Shared/Error.cshtml`, `Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml`, `Account/Manage.cshtml`, `Account/_ChangePasswordPartial.cshtml` — section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) items (1)-(4) |
| **Per-line rewrite — no successor for a non-type construct** | 1 | `StoreManager/Index.cshtml`, whose `@helper Truncate` declaration has no successor — the `@helper` directive was removed in ASP.NET Core. The target expresses it as a `static` string helper called from the view, and the rendered output is unchanged |
| **Per-line rewrite — the checkout input model** | 1 | `Checkout/AddressAndPayment.cshtml` — sections [8.8](#88-the-checkout-input-model--ten-properties-not-nine) and [8.8.1](#881-the-view-rewrite--why-changing-only-model-renders-promocode-twice), the latter element by element |
| **Ported with the shared mechanical transformations** | 15 | `Account/Login.cshtml`, `Account/Register.cshtml`, `Checkout/Complete.cshtml`, `Home/About.cshtml`, `Home/Contact.cshtml`, `Home/Index.cshtml`, `Shared/_Layout.cshtml`, `ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml`, `Store/Browse.cshtml`, `Store/Details.cshtml`, `Store/Index.cshtml`, `StoreManager/Create.cshtml`, `StoreManager/Delete.cshtml`, `StoreManager/Details.cshtml`, `StoreManager/Edit.cshtml` |
| **Removed with the external-login challenge surface** | 4 | `Account/_ExternalLoginsListPartial.cshtml` (the OWIN provider enumeration and the form that posts to the removed challenge actions), `Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml`, `Account/ExternalLoginFailure.cshtml`, `Account/_SetPasswordPartial.cshtml` — section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types), approved delta `D-11` |
| **Total** | **29** | Ported: 1 + 3 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 15 = **25**. Removed: **4**. 25 + 4 = 29 |

**Two notes the table needs, because both are available to be misread.**

- **The AAP's five legacy-type views are all present and none is double-counted.** Four are rewritten
  **in place** and appear in row three; the fifth, `Account/_RemoveAccountPartial.cshtml`, appears in row
  two because it relocates under its view component — its legacy-type problem is resolved *there*, at its
  new path, and section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) item (5) specifies it. Adding it
  to row three as well would make the total 30.
- **"Mechanical" means no legacy type and no missing successor. It does not mean small.** Several views
  in row six carry substantial per-view work: `Shared/_Layout.cshtml` is the entire navbar migration of
  section [8.5](#85-the-bootstrap-upgrade-is-markup-work-not-a-version-bump) plus the
  script and style tags of section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler); `ShoppingCart/Index.cshtml`
  is the script externalization of section
  [8.1.2](#812-the-externalized-cart-script) and the table semantics of section
  [8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements); `StoreManager/Details.cshtml` restructures
  a removed Bootstrap component; and `StoreManager/Create.cshtml` and `StoreManager/Edit.cshtml` take the
  `@model` change and the two dropdown rewrites of section
  [8.11](#811-the-administration-input-models--the-entity-stops-being-a-binding-target)'s **R4** block.
  Those last two stay in row six rather than moving to row five, and the distinction is the one row five
  is named for: the checkout view's **rendered field set** changes, which is why section
  [8.8.1](#881-the-view-rewrite--why-changing-only-model-renders-promocode-twice) exists, while these two
  render the same fields under the same names and change only the type the expressions resolve against.
  What every view in this row shares is that a **compiler** finds the mistakes, which the
  rows above it cannot rely on.

The four shared mechanical transformations, which every ported view takes. **Each count is given twice —
the source's, and the ported subset — because approved delta `D-11` eliminates call sites of three of
them and a single figure would overstate the work by exactly those sites.** The middle column counts work
that disappears, which is not the same as work that is physically inside a removed file: the three
`@Html.Partial` sites are in **retained** views (`Login.cshtml` and `Manage.cshtml`) and disappear because
what they invoke is removed, whereas the anti-forgery and `BeginForm` sites are inside the removed views
themselves. Either way the site is not ported, which is what the column measures.

| Transformation | Source call sites | Eliminated by `D-11` | Ported call sites |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `@Html.Partial` becomes the `<partial>` tag helper | **5** (`git grep -o '@Html.Partial' -- 'src/MVC5/*.cshtml' \| wc -l` → `5`) | **3** — `Account/Login.cshtml:52` and `Account/Manage.cshtml:23` invoke `_ExternalLoginsListPartial`, `Account/Manage.cshtml:18` invokes `_SetPasswordPartial` | **2** |
| `@Url.Content` remains valid, unchanged | **4** (→ `4`) | 0 | **4** — each mapped to its target expression and emitted URL in section [8.1.4](#814-the-four-urlcontent-call-sites-mapped) |
| `@Html.AntiForgeryToken()` disappears into automatic emission (section [7.1](#71-the-policy)) | **10** | **3** — `ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml`, `_ExternalLoginsListPartial.cshtml`, `_SetPasswordPartial.cshtml`, one each | **7** |
| `Html.BeginForm` becomes a form tag helper | **12** (`git grep -o 'Html.BeginForm' -- 'src/MVC5/*.cshtml' \| wc -l` → `12`) | **3** — the same three views, one form each | **9** |

The bundling helpers are rewritten per section
[8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler). Form and input helpers are source-compatible; tag
helpers are the target convention and are adopted where a form is being touched anyway — which, because
of the anti-forgery change, is every ported form.

**One asymmetry makes this less safe than it sounds, and it cuts in the port's favour.** These 29 source
views — the **26** that reach the target and the 3 the split deletes alike — have **never been
compile-checked**: `MvcBuildViews` is `false`, so no view is compiled at build time
today ([10 §12.3](10-build-and-deployment-requirements.md), [08 §8.1](08-technical-debt-register.md)).
The target compiles Razor views as part of the build. So type errors that are invisible today —
including the removed model type in (1) above — become **build** errors, discovered for free rather
than at first request. The consequence for this plan is that the view port needs no separate
type-checking pass; it needs a build.

#### 8.4.1 The order-confirmation page's `Store` link — the label is preserved and the destination is corrected

**The one control the order-confirmation page offers is labelled for the catalog and navigates to the
home page.** `Checkout/Complete.cshtml` renders `@Html.ActionLink("Store", "Index", "Home")`
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Checkout/Complete.cshtml:12], so the visible label is `Store` while the
generated `href` is `/` — the `Home` controller's `Index`. The view sits in row six of the table above,
which means the port would otherwise carry the helper across mechanically and reproduce the mismatch, so
the disposition is decided here rather than left to whoever types the line.

**Two dispositions were available and only one of them is a correction.**

| Disposition | What it produces | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Keep the label, retarget the link** — `Store`, `href="/Store"` | The control does what its label already says. The label, its position and its surrounding sentence [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Checkout/Complete.cshtml:10-13] are unchanged; only the `href` moves | **Selected.** The label is the promise the page makes to a visitor who has just ordered, and the catalog is the destination that promise names |
| Keep the target, relabel the link — `Home`, `href="/"` | The control becomes truthful by giving up the affordance | **Rejected.** It preserves a destination nobody asked for and removes the one route back into the catalog from the end of the order flow, which is a product regression dressed as a consistency fix |

**It is an absorbed defect correction rather than an approved delta, and the register carries no row for
it deliberately.** The label already says `Store` and the control already presents itself as the way to
the catalog; what changes is that it now goes there. A link whose destination its own label does not name
is a defect rather than behaviour a visitor could rely on, so this correction sits with the other two link
corrections this document makes — the dropdown toggle repointed by section
[8.2](#82-child-actions--three-view-components) and the dead footer anchor removed by section
[8.14](#814-the-two-absolute-external-links--one-decision-each) — none of which is on either approval
register, and all three of which section
[12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual) names together so that a reviewer does
not file one as a regression. It is the same defect and the same correction as the toggle's — a helper
overload resolving to a route the label does not name — reached through `ActionLink` rather than through
`Url.Action`, and the two are recorded separately because they sit on different pages with different
labels and neither implies the other. The link is generated with the controller and action stated
explicitly, `@Html.ActionLink("Store", "Index", "Store")`, on the URL-generation rule of section 8.2:
the single-argument and ambient-controller overloads are exactly what produced the defect.

**Rendered appearance is preserved and only the attribute moves**, so section
[12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual) carries it in that same enumerated
group rather than as a new capture, and it is confirmed on images the capture set already collects: the
label text is unchanged and the emitted `href` is the catalog index.

### 8.5 The Bootstrap upgrade is markup work, not a version bump

[04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) pins the target Bootstrap version. **The markup work is
this document's**, and it is not optional: **upgrading the package without touching the markup changes
the rendered page.**

**Resolution: a visual-preservation port.** Every affected class name is mapped old-to-new, the
collapse mechanism's data attributes are updated to the target library's form, the horizontal-form
grid is re-expressed in the target's grid utilities, and **acceptance is defined as the rendered layout
matching the Bootstrap 3 baseline captured *before* the port.** The baseline capture and the review are
scoped in section [12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual); they are
deliberately **not** claimed by the automated suite.

#### 8.5.1 The breakpoint, and the two viewports

**Target navbar expansion: `navbar-expand-md`.** The source navbar has no expansion class at all,
because Bootstrap 3 hard-codes one collapse boundary: the toggle is hidden at `min-width: 768px`
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:4235-4239], so the navbar is collapsed below 768px and
expanded at 768px and above. The target library makes the boundary explicit and its `md` tier begins at
768px, so **`navbar-expand-md` reproduces the source boundary exactly**. `navbar-expand-lg` — the value
the target's own templates default to — would move the boundary to 992px and leave the navbar collapsed
across a 224-pixel band where it is expanded today. That is a visible regression from a copied default,
and naming the class here is what prevents it.

**Baseline and comparison viewports, by dimension:**

| Viewport | Dimensions | Why this one |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Narrow | **375 x 812** | Below the 768px boundary, so the navbar is **collapsed** and the toggle is rendered. Also below the source's `sm` tier and below the target's `md`, so in **both** scales only the infix-free column widths apply — `col-xs-4` today, `col-4` after the port ([8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens)) |
| Wide | **1280 x 800** | Above every boundary either scale places below 1400px, so in the source `col-sm-*`, `col-md-*` and `col-lg-*` are all active at once and in the target `col-md-*`, `col-lg-*` and `col-xl-*` are, with the narrowest-declared tier winning in each. The expanded navbar, both album grids and the horizontal forms are therefore all exercised in one capture |

Both are stated as exact dimensions because "one wide and one narrow" is not reproducible, and section
[12.5.1](#1251-the-capture-manifest--one-table-one-total) computes its capture total from them.

**Two endpoint viewports are the right basis for comparing appearance and the wrong basis for verifying
tier behaviour, and section
[12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual) therefore carries a second, separate
pass.** 375px and 1280px sit inside the first and last intervals of both scales, so neither can observe
what happens in the intervals between — and the tier remapping of
[8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens) is precisely a set of claims about interval
boundaries. The **breakpoint-boundary verification pass** of section 12.5 brackets every boundary in both
scales; the two viewports above remain the basis for the whole-page appearance comparison and are not
widened to do the boundary pass's job.

**One consequence of the wide viewport that is pinned rather than merely checked.** Bootstrap 3's
`.container` is capped at 750px, 970px and 1170px at its three breakpoints
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:927-930], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1081-1084], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1244-1247]; the target's caps
differ in value and its ladder has **five** steps to the source's three, adding one below 768px and one at
1400px. At 1280px wide the page's outer container would therefore resolve to a **different maximum width**
after the upgrade even with identical markup. Because that is not something a reviewer can be asked to
accept or reject, section
[8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) **group 1a pins all three source
caps at the source's own three boundaries and neutralizes the target's other two**, and the reviewer's job
at the wide viewport is to confirm the pinned 1170px rather than to discover a number. It is
compounded by an application-level oddity: `container` is applied to the album `<li>` elements
themselves [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:13],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Browse.cshtml:13], nested inside a `row`, so each grid cell carries
a capped-width block. The markup is **preserved as-is** — changing it would be a redesign — but both
album grids are checked at both viewports for exactly this reason.

**The two per-view results, written out, because these are the two elements where four column tokens meet
on one `class` attribute:**

```html
<!-- src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:13 and
     src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Browse.cshtml:13, source: -->
<li class="col-lg-2 col-md-2 col-sm-2 col-xs-4 container">
<!-- target: -->
<li class="col-xl-2 col-lg-2 col-md-2 col-4 container">
```

The `container` token stays on the `<li>` — it is the application-level oddity
[8.5.1](#851-the-breakpoint-and-the-two-viewports) records, and removing it would be a redesign.

**The remapping rule, and the arithmetic behind it.** Bootstrap 3 has **four** tiers and the target has
**six**, and **three** boundaries coincide — 768px, 992px and 1200px, as the table's own middle rows show;
`xs` has no boundary to coincide with, and the target's 576px and 1400px are the two the source has no
tier at. **The lead-in read "two", which its own table contradicts**, so it is corrected here rather than
left for a reader to reconcile: 3 shared + 2 target-only = the target's 5 boundaries:

| Source tier | Source boundary, from the committed stylesheet | Target tier at the same boundary | Target's own tiers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `xs` | none — `col-xs-*` widths are declared unconditionally [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:879-925] | the **infix-free** column, which also carries none | — |
| `sm` | `min-width: 768px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:927] | **`md`**, which begins at 768px | `xs` <576, `sm` ≥576 |
| `md` | `min-width: 992px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1081] | **`lg`**, which begins at 992px | `md` ≥768, `lg` ≥992 |
| `lg` | `min-width: 1200px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1244] | **`xl`**, which begins at 1200px | `xl` ≥1200, `xxl` ≥1400 |

So the rule is **`xs` → infix-free, `sm` → `md`, `md` → `lg`, `lg` → `xl`**, and the target's `sm`
(≥576px) and `xxl` (≥1400px) tiers are **not used by this port at all** — there is no source tier at
either boundary, and introducing one would create a reflow the source does not have.

**What carrying a name across unchanged would actually have done**, stated concretely because "the
breakpoints differ" understates it. `col-sm-2` left as `col-sm-2` would begin applying at **576px**
instead of 768px, so the album grid would go from three tiles per row to **six** across the whole
576-767px band — the six-up grid is 2 of 12 columns, and nothing in the source produces it below 768px.
`col-md-2` and `col-md-10` left unchanged in the horizontal forms would begin applying at **768px**
instead of 992px, so every one of the seven forms would break into its two-column label-beside-control
layout **224 pixels early**, in a band where the source still stacks the label above the control. Both are
regressions a class-name diff cannot see, and both are why every column token above carries a target.

**`navbar-expand-md` is already correct and is explicitly exempt from the rule above.** It is **not** a
carried-across source infix — Bootstrap 3 has no expansion class at all, and its collapse boundary is
hard-coded at `min-width: 768px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:4235-4239]. The `md` in
`navbar-expand-md` was chosen directly against the **target's** scale, whose `md` begins at 768px, so it
is already an equal-pixel match ([8.5.1](#851-the-breakpoint-and-the-two-viewports) states the same
reasoning from the other direction). A reader applying the `md` → `lg` rule mechanically to it would
produce `navbar-expand-lg` and reintroduce exactly the 224-pixel collapsed band that section warns about.
**Do not remap it.**

**Forms — 5 tokens.** This is the group where a class rename is not enough, because the target has no
horizontal-form component at all.

| Source token | Target | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `form-horizontal` | **Removed with no replacement class.** The horizontal layout is expressed structurally instead: `row` on the group and `col-form-label` on the label | **7 sites, in two shapes.** Five are an `@class` on the form itself — [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml:8], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Login.cshtml:11], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Register.cshtml:8], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_ChangePasswordPartial.cshtml:6], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_SetPasswordPartial.cshtml:8] — and two are a wrapper `<div>` *inside* a form: [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/StoreManager/Create.cshtml:13], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/StoreManager/Edit.cshtml:13]. **The second shape leaves an empty wrapper `<div>` once the class is removed**, which is retained rather than unwrapped — deleting an element changes the DOM the reviewer is comparing, and it costs nothing to keep |
| `form-group` | **`row form-group`** — the target's `form-group` is gone from the *library*, so `row` restores the two-column layout and the **class name is retained as an application-owned one** carrying the source's `margin-bottom: 15px` ([8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) group 1a), the same pattern `jumbotron` and `dl-horizontal` follow. **`mb-3` is rejected**: it is `1rem`, 16px against the pinned 14px body, and it carries `!important` | 29 sites |
| `control-label` | **`col-form-label`** | 22 sites |
| `form-control` | Unchanged | 11 sites |
| `checkbox` (wrapper `<div>`) | **`form-check`**, with `form-check-input` on the input and `form-check-label` on the label. The wrapper's and the label's metrics are pinned in [8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) **group 12** — including the label's normal weight, which the source sets and the successor does not — while the control's own rendering changes from the platform checkbox to the library's styled box, which is `D-36` | [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Login.cshtml:33-36] |

One misapplication is corrected while the forms are being touched: `control-label` is applied to an
`<h5>` heading in the catalog [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Browse.cshtml:19], where it is a form
class on a non-form element. It is **dropped there** rather than translated, and the heading's size is
held with a type utility per section
[8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements).

**Buttons and text — 7 tokens.** One rename, one **withdrawn** defect correction, **three whose class name
carries across while its rendered value does not** — of which only two survive into the port — and two
genuinely unchanged. The rename carries a **visible** consequence and is therefore a numbered approved
delta rather than a silent substitution: **`D-15`** of section
[11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas). The correction was numbered alongside it and is now
withdrawn, for the reason stated under the table.

| Source token | Target | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `btn` | Unchanged | 11 sites |
| `btn-default` | **`btn-secondary`** — the target has no `btn-default`. **The fill and label colour change; the geometry does not**, because [8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) pins the padding, type scale and radius. **`D-34`** | the same 11 sites |
| `text-danger`, `text-info`, `text-success` | **Class name unchanged; the colour is pinned.** The target replaces these three with utilities that carry **different values** and declare them `!important`, so leaving the name alone silently recolours every site. The source values — `#b94a48` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:440-442] and `#468847` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:444-446] — are preserved by [8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) group 1c, which matches the `!important` so the override wins. **`text-info` needs no pin**: its `#3a87ad` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:448-450] has **no ported site**, so pinning it would define a value nothing reads | **5 source sites, 3 ported**: `text-danger` on [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Error.cshtml:7], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/Error.cshtml:8] and `text-success` on [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/Manage.cshtml:9] port; `text-info` on [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/_SetPasswordPartial.cshtml:3] and [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/ExternalLoginConfirmation.cshtml:15] are **both in removed views** |
| `text-center` | Unchanged, name **and** value — `text-align: center` in both libraries [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:460-462] | 2 sites: [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:6], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:35] |
| `text-error` | **No change is made — the change is withdrawn**, for the reason below | 1 source site, 0 ported: [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/ExternalLoginFailure.cshtml:6], a removed view |

**`text-error` is a Bootstrap *2* class that never existed in Bootstrap 3**, so the heading it is applied
to renders **unstyled today** — the stylesheet the application actually ships defines `.text-danger`
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:440] and has **no** `text-error` rule at all
(`Select-String -Path src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css -Pattern text-error` → 0 matches).
Correcting it to `text-danger` would therefore make that one heading render in the danger colour where
today it renders in the body colour — a **visible change on one page** — which is why an earlier revision
numbered the correction as an approved delta rather than treating it as a silent defect fix.

**The change is withdrawn, and the reason is that the page it would change no longer exists.** The token's
**only** site in the entire source is
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Account/ExternalLoginFailure.cshtml:6], and that view is one of the four
removed with the external-login challenge surface (section
[8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types), approved delta `D-11`). No ported view carries the
token, so there is nothing to rename, nothing to recolour, and nothing for a reviewer to accept: the
class disappears with the file. **The withdrawal is recorded here and outside the approved-delta count** of
section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas) — a change that is not made is not a delta, and
carrying a numbered row for it would put a visible difference on the reviewer's checklist that no page can
show. The two dispositions the earlier revision weighed — correcting the class, or dropping it so the
heading keeps rendering in the body colour — are both moot for the same reason, and neither needs an
owner. **Nothing is pending**: were the challenge surface ever reinstated under its own decision, the
view would return carrying the source's own `text-error` and this paragraph would become live again, which
is why the analysis is kept rather than deleted.

**Components removed in the target — 4 tokens.** These are the two that need real restructuring, plus
the icons.

The hand-written pair at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Checkout/AddressAndPayment.cshtml:23], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Checkout/AddressAndPayment.cshtml:26] mirrors the naming of the framework's built-in object template, which is what `@Html.EditorForModel()` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Checkout/AddressAndPayment.cshtml:17] renders the nine shipping fields through, so the same stacked wrapper shape surrounds **every** field on this page and not only the promo code. This is the **stacked** structure, not the `row` / `col-form-label` pair the horizontal forms get: the checkout form carries neither `form-horizontal` nor `form-group` (`git grep -c form-group -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Checkout/AddressAndPayment.cshtml'` → no match) |

The externalized script of section [8.1.2](#812-the-externalized-cart-script) selects on it |

`14 + 5 + 11 + 5 + 7 + 4 + 5 + 5 = 56`.

#### 8.5.3 Non-class markup that changes with the library

Four changes are not class substitutions and would be missed by a search-and-replace over `class`
attributes:

- **The collapse plugin's data attributes are namespaced.** `data-toggle="collapse"` and
  `data-target=".navbar-collapse"` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:15] become
  `data-bs-toggle="collapse"` and `data-bs-target="#navbarMain"`, and `data-toggle="dropdown"`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/GenreMenu.cshtml:4] becomes `data-bs-toggle="dropdown"`. **A
  missed prefix fails silently**: the markup renders, the button is clickable, and nothing happens.
- **The collapse target becomes an id rather than a class selector, and the id is fixed here as
  `navbarMain`.** The source targets `.navbar-collapse` — a *class* selector that happens to match one
  element — and a class selector cannot supply an accessible name-and-state relationship, because
  `aria-controls` takes an **id reference** and nothing else. So the collapse element gains
  `id="navbarMain"` and the toggler references it three times over: as the plugin's target, as
  `aria-controls`, and implicitly through the `aria-expanded` state the plugin maintains on the toggler.
  The id is stated as a literal rather than left to the implementer because two of those three
  references must agree exactly, and section
  [8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements) item **a1** asserts them in the rendered
  response. **The literal target markup** — this replaces the toggler at
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:15-19] and the collapse wrapper at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:22], and it
  is the markup section [8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements) item **a1** requires
  and section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) **row 28** asserts against — row 28 being the response-level
  assertion that section 8.9's own acceptance table assigns to `a1`, so the id agreement is checked in a
  rendered response rather than reviewed by eye:

  ```html
  <button class="navbar-toggler" type="button"
          data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#navbarMain"
          aria-controls="navbarMain" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Toggle navigation">
    <span class="navbar-toggler-icon"></span>
  </button>
  <div class="collapse navbar-collapse" id="navbarMain">
  ```

  `aria-expanded="false"` is the **initial** value; the plugin flips it on toggle, and that flipping is
  what makes the attribute worth emitting rather than decorative. `aria-label="Toggle navigation"` is
  net-new: the source toggler's only content is three empty `<span class="icon-bar">` elements
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:16-18], so it has **no accessible name at all** today — the label is what gives it one, and it is
  additive markup rather than a visual change.
- **The toggler's three bars become one icon element**, as the token table records and the literal
  markup above shows.
- **The caret element is deleted, not reclassed** — `<b class="caret"></b>`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/GenreMenu.cshtml:4] leaves no element behind, and the empty
  divider `<li>` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/GenreMenu.cshtml:14] is replaced by an `<li>` wrapping an `<hr>`.

#### 8.5.4 Glyphicons are removed rather than replaced

**Glyphicons are removed rather than replaced with an icon library.** They were dropped from Bootstrap
after 3. Use is decorative and confined to **exactly two views** — verified:

```text
src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/ShoppingCart/CartSummary.cshtml:5:  <span class="glyphicon glyphicon glyphicon-shopping-cart"></span>
src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Details.cshtml:27:            <span class="glyphicon glyphicon-shopping-cart"></span>
```

**Neither is the shared layout** — a natural assumption, since the cart badge renders *into* the
layout, but the markup lives in the cart-summary partial rather than in `_Layout.cshtml`. The two spans
are removed; the adjacent text and link in each view are preserved, so both controls keep their label
and their behaviour and lose only the pictogram. (The cart-summary span also carries the `glyphicon`
class twice [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/GenreMenu.cshtml:5], which is worth nothing except as a sign that nobody has looked at this markup in a
long time.)

**Removing them adds no dependency, no acquisition mechanism and no licence question**, which is
precisely the argument for removal over substitution at this scale. It is an **approved visual delta**
(section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas)), not an unnoticed regression. **If a stakeholder
wants icons retained, that is a scoped decision with its own pinned source and its own licence
review — this document does not assume one.**

#### 8.5.5 `Content/Site.css` — the named change list

The application's own stylesheet is **86 lines and eighteen qualified rule blocks**, and three of them are coupled to the
library being replaced. It relocates to `wwwroot/css/site.css` (section
[8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler)), which is also what settles the casing mismatch at
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:28]. Every rule has a stated disposition — "review the
CSS" is not one of them, and neither is "adjust where needed": each row below states **retained
unchanged**, **retained with a rewritten selector**, or **removed**, and where a selector is rewritten
the target selector is written out.

**Eighteen blocks, and the table's twelve rows account for all of them**, because two rows carry more
than one block:

```text
(Get-Content src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css | Select-String -Pattern '\{').Count   # -> 18
```

`body` 1 + `.body-content` 1 + `input, select, textarea` 1 + the six validation blocks 6 +
`ul#album-list li` 1 + the two `img` blocks 2 + the `a` block 1 + the `a:hover` block 1 +
`.navbar-inverse, .navbar-inverse .navbar-brand` 1 + `.navbar-inverse .navbar-text` 1 +
`.navbar-inverse .navbar-nav > li > a` 1 + `.jumbotron` 1 = **18**.

| Rule | Lines | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body { padding-top: 50px; padding-bottom: 20px }` | [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:1-4] | **Re-measured, not copied.** The 50px exists solely to clear the fixed-top navbar, and it matches Bootstrap 3's `.navbar { min-height: 50px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:4025-4028] exactly. The target's navbar has different intrinsic padding and line-height, so **the value is set from a measurement of the rendered target navbar at each viewport** — including the collapsed navbar at 375px, where an expanded menu pushes content further. No replacement number is invented here; the measurement is the acceptance step in [8.5.6](#856-acceptance). `padding-bottom: 20px` clears the fixed-bottom footer and is re-measured on the same basis. **Section [8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) pins the navbar's own constituent metrics** — its minimum height, its vertical padding and the brand's padding and line-height — to the source values, so the measurement is expected to confirm 50px rather than to discover a new number; if it does not, **the offset follows the measurement**, not the other way round |
| `.body-content { padding-left: 15px; padding-right: 15px }` | [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:7-10] | **Retained unchanged**, selector included. Application-owned; the class is preserved per [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens), so nothing about the rule needs to move |
| `input, select, textarea { max-width: 280px }` | [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:13-17] | **Retained, and checked at both viewports.** It is an unqualified element selector that overrides `form-control`'s full-width behaviour on **every** input in the application, including the ones inside the restructured `row form-group` groups. At 375px the column is already narrower than 280px so the cap is inert; at 1280px it is what makes the form fields short rather than column-wide. Preserving that appearance is the point, so the rule stays and the reviewer confirms it still bites |
| The six validation rules — `.field-validation-error`, `.field-validation-valid`, `input.input-validation-error`, `input[type="checkbox"].input-validation-error`, `.validation-summary-errors`, `.validation-summary-valid` | [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:20-42] | **All retained, unchanged and still correct.** The pinned unobtrusive-validation successor ([04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)) emits the same five class names, so these rules keep working. Stated explicitly because they look like framework leftovers and are not: deleting them silently removes every client-side error style in the application. `#b94a48` is the colour being preserved |
| `ul#album-list li { height: 160px }` | [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:47-49] | **Retained unchanged**, selector included. Fixes the album tile height in both grids, and it is the reason the grids do not reflow when the library's own line-height changes |
| `ul#album-list li img:hover { box-shadow … }` and `ul#album-list li img { box-shadow …; border: none; padding: 0 }` | [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:51-53] and [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:55-59] | **Both retained unchanged**, selectors and values included. Two blocks, not one: the `:hover` block [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:51-53] carrying `box-shadow: 1px 1px 7px #777`, and the base block [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:55-59] carrying `box-shadow: 1px 1px 5px #999`, `border: none` and `padding: 0`. Neither selector names a library class, so neither is affected by the upgrade |

The library's global `a:focus { outline: thin dotted #333; outline: 5px auto -webkit-focus-ring-color; outline-offset: -2px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:348-352] still applies to them, and nothing in the application stylesheet cancels it — the album rule below is `:hover` only and declares no `outline` property at all [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:65-70] — so **a focused album link shows the platform focus ring today**.
