This separate rule is therefore deleted as redundant rather than as dead |

#### 8.5.6 Acceptance

**The rendered layout matches the Bootstrap 3 baseline captured before the port, at both stated
viewports, except for the approved deltas of section
[11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas) and the approval-owned additions of section
[11.7](#117-approval-owned-additions)**. **The expected-difference set is enumerated once, in section
[12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual)**, classified by what the reviewer is
asked to do with each entry; it is cited here rather than restated, so the two cannot drift apart. Four of
those entries originate in this section: the **withdrawn** `text-error` entry, `D-34`, `D-35` and `D-36`
are the library-default differences that section
[8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) resolves as approved
changes rather than as preserved appearance — the last two of them partially, since `D-35` preserves the
ring's values and narrows only the selector, and `D-36` changes the checkbox control while the wrapper
and the label around it are pinned. The `text-error` entry is carried **outside** the delta count, for the
reason section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas) states: `D-11` removes its only site.

Ten checks are named individually because they are the ones a class-by-class diff cannot establish:

- The **body offset** clears the target navbar at 375px and at 1280px, with no content hidden behind it
  and no visible gap ([8.5.5](#855-contentsitecss--the-named-change-list), first row).
- The **outer container width** at 1280px, and the album-tile widths in both grids at both viewports
  ([8.5.1](#851-the-breakpoint-and-the-two-viewports)).
- The **navbar collapses below 768px and is expanded at and above it**, matching the source boundary, with
  the toggler operable and the genre dropdown opening in both states.
- The **form field widths** still reflect the 280px cap at 1280px
  ([8.5.5](#855-contentsitecss--the-named-change-list), third row).
- The **navbar's rendered height** at both viewports, against the 50px the source composes from
  `.navbar { min-height: 50px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:4025-4031] and the brand's
  `15px + 20px + 15px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:4194-4199] — the check that decides the body offset above
  ([8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses)).
- The **sampled colours** of the four values a class mapping cannot carry: the dark navbar's background
  against `#222222` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:4503-4506], the table cell border against `#dddddd` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1421-1431], the stripe
  against `#f9f9f9` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1482-1485], and the list-group item border against `#dddddd` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:5255-5262]
  ([8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses)).
- **Which edge carries each rule, not only its colour** — the horizontal rule sits above every table cell
  and above every list-group item boundary with no doubled line, and the rule under the header row is the
  heavier one. Colour sampling passes even when every rule has moved a row, which is why the edge is a
  check of its own ([8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) groups 4 and
  5).
- **Links are undecorated at rest and underlined on hover, and the two controls that became `<button>`
  elements are indistinguishable from the links they replace** — no box, no border, no shifted baseline,
  and the same hover behaviour as their neighbours. The sign-out control specifically matches the `#ddd`
  of the nav links beside it rather than the body link colour
  ([8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) groups 2 and 10).
- **The footer's two lines are stacked and centred, not side by side** — the check that the `navbar` class
  came off that element, since a flex row is what its presence produces
  ([8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) group 13).
- **The genre menu in its open state**: the hovered item is white on the link blue, the open toggle sits
  on the darkened panel, and the menu's top corners are square against the navbar
  ([8.5.7](#857-library-default-differences-that-no-class-mapping-expresses) groups 6 and 11).

The review procedure, the capture set and the sign-off artifact are section
[12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual)'s;
[07](07-effort-risks-sequencing.md) carries it as a task.

#### 8.5.7 Library default differences that no class mapping expresses

Section [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens) maps class *names*. It cannot
express the other half of a major-version upgrade: a difference where the **same** class, or no class at
all, renders differently because the library's own base values changed. Those differences are invisible
to a class-by-class diff, they appear on **every** page rather than on the one being edited, and they are
exactly what a reviewer would otherwise record as an unexplained regression. Each one below is therefore
resolved in one of two ways and never left open:

- **Preserved** — with the `wwwroot/css/site.css` declaration that preserves it **written out** in the
  block below. The value in the declaration is the Bootstrap 3 value measured from the committed
  stylesheet, which is the baseline the review compares against.
- **An approved change** — with its number and its named owner in section
  [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas).

**Why the preservation mechanism is application CSS rather than build variables.** The successor is
acquired as **pre-built CSS** and committed, not compiled from source
([8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler), with the manifest owned by
[04 §9.4](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) and the pins by
[04 §9.2](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md)), so there is no variable layer to set these values in. They
are set as overrides in the application's own stylesheet, which the layout links **after** the library's
([8.1.3](#813-the-rendered-tags-and-every-bundle-path-they-replace), rows one and two of the element
table) — that ordering is what makes the overrides win, and it is why the two `<link>` elements are
stated in a fixed order rather than as a pair.

| Difference | Bootstrap 3 baseline, from the committed stylesheet | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Base typography** — font stack, size, line-height and body colour, which set the metrics of every block of text on every page | `"Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif`, `14px`, `1.428571429`, `#333333` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:313-319] | **Preserved** — the four declarations in group 1 below. The port does **not** rescale the root font size to achieve this: the successor sizes its components in `rem` against the root element, so moving the root would move every library padding, margin and border-radius at once — a far larger change than the one being prevented. The root stays where the successor puts it, `body` is pinned here, and the handful of components that carry their own `rem` type scale are pinned individually in group 3 |
| **The grid gutter and the container's side padding — a 30px gutter against the successor's 24px, on every column of every page.** The source states the three halves of one measurement as three fixed values; the successor derives all three from one custom property, so pinning that property is what preserves them together | `.container { padding-right: 15px; padding-left: 15px; margin-right: auto; margin-left: auto }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:759-764]; `.row { margin-right: -15px; margin-left: -15px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:786-789]; and every column `padding-right: 15px; padding-left: 15px` under the full column selector list [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:811-863] | **Preserved** — group 1a, by setting `--bs-gutter-x: 30px` and writing the container padding explicitly. The successor's default is `1.5rem`, which is **24px**, so leaving it alone narrows every gutter by 6px and every container's side padding by 3px — the album tiles move, the horizontal-form columns move, and the body content shifts 3px inward on all 29 views at once. The custom property is set on **both** `.container` and `.row` rather than on one of them: custom properties inherit, so a `.row` inside a `.container` would pick it up, but the two album grids are **not** the same shape — `<ul class="row list-unstyled">` on the home page [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:10] carries `row` and `<ul id="album-list" class="list-unstyled">` on the browse page [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Browse.cshtml:10] does **not**, so the browse tiles are columns with no row ancestor and inherit the property from the `container` class each `<li>` carries instead |
| **The container's three width caps, against the successor's five-step ladder.** This is the difference section [8.5.1](#851-the-breakpoint-and-the-two-viewports) records at the wide viewport, resolved here rather than left for the reviewer to discover | `max-width: 750px` at `min-width: 768px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:927-930], `970px` at `992px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1081-1084], `1170px` at `1200px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1244-1247] — and **no cap at all below 768px**, where `.container` is fluid | **Preserved** — group 1a, which pins the three source values at the source's own three boundaries and neutralizes the successor's two extra steps: its cap at `min-width: 576px` is cancelled with `max-width: none`, restoring the source's fluid band across 576-767px, and its cap at `min-width: 1400px` is overridden with the same `1170px` so no fourth cap appears where the source has three. Both neutralizing rules are written even though source order alone would win, because a reader must be able to see that the two extra steps were considered rather than missed |
| **`.row` changes layout model — the successor's row is a flex container where the source's is a block with floated columns.** The class name is identical, so a class diff sees nothing, and the consequence differs on each of the three surfaces that carry it | `.row` is a block element with a `:before`/`:after` clearfix [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:786-809] and its columns are floated [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:865-877]; there is no flex property anywhere in the source's grid | **Preserved — one surface needs a declaration, the other two are unaffected, and the reason each is unaffected is stated rather than assumed.** The jumbotron's showcase row is `<div class="row text-center">` wrapping a bare `<img>` with **no column class** [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Index.cshtml:6-8]: `text-align: center` centres an inline image inside a block, but a flex item is placed by `justify-content`, which defaults to `flex-start`, so the home page's first image would move from centred to left-aligned. Group 1a **preserves** it with `justify-content: center` scoped to `.jumbotron .row`. **The home page's album grid needs no declaration**, because the one difference flex could produce there — a wrapped line starting below the tallest tile of the line above rather than below the tile directly above — requires tiles of unequal height, and the application fixes every tile at one height: `ul#album-list li { height: 160px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/Site.css:47-49], retained unchanged ([8.5.5](#855-contentsitecss--the-named-change-list)). Equal-height items wrap identically under both models. The tiles also carry no background and no border, so a stretched flex item and a floated block are indistinguishable. **The browse grid's `<ul>` carries no `row` at all** [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Store/Browse.cshtml:10], so no layout model changes on it |
| **Vertical rhythm between form groups — `15px` in the source, and the successor has no `form-group` class to carry it** | `.form-group { margin-bottom: 15px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1755-1757], plus `.form-horizontal .form-group { margin-right: -15px; margin-left: -15px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1969-1972], which is the row behaviour the target gets from `row` | **Preserved** — group 1a, and the mapping in [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens) is written to make it possible: `form-group` becomes **`row form-group`**, retaining the source class name as an application-owned class, rather than `row mb-3`. `mb-3` is **rejected on measurement**: it is `1rem`, which against the pinned `14px` body is **16px**, one pixel more than the source on each of the **29** groups — and it carries `!important`, so a `.row.mb-3` override would have to carry `!important` too, to restore a value the library never needed to be told. Retaining the class name follows the same pattern as `jumbotron` and `dl-horizontal` in groups 8 and 9: a name the successor has dropped, defined once in the application's own stylesheet |
| **The heading scale and the six `.h1`-`.h6` type utilities.** The base-typography row above pins `body` and nothing else, and headings do not inherit their size from it — every one of the **36** headings in the 29 views takes its size, weight, line-height and margins from the library's own heading rules | Shared: `font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.1` on `h1`-`h6` **and** `.h1`-`.h6` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:464-479]. Margins: `h1, h2, h3 { margin-top: 20px; margin-bottom: 10px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:498-503] and `h4, h5, h6 { margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:505-510]. Sizes: `36px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:512-515], `30px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:517-520], `24px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:522-525], `18px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:527-530], `14px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:532-535], `12px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:537-540] | **Preserved** — group 1b, which pins all three shared properties, both margin pairs and all six sizes, on the elements **and** the utilities. Pinning the utilities is not decoration: item **a4** of section [8.9](#89-accessibility-and-interaction-state-requirements) holds the catalog's rendered sizes with `class="h3"` and `class="h5"` while correcting the heading outline, and that only preserves the rendering **because** these declarations make `.h3` mean `24px` and `.h5` mean `14px` as they do today. The distribution is **h1 × 1, h2 × 16, h3 × 7, h4 × 11, h5 × 1, h6 × 0** across 24 of the 29 views (`git grep -c -o -E '<h[1-6][ >]' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views'`), so `h2` and `h4` carry most of the risk. The source's `h* small` rules [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:481-496], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:542-557] are **not** reproduced, and that is a measurement rather than an omission: the only `<small>` in any view is in the footer paragraph [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:37], not inside a heading, so those rules match nothing today |
| **Block-level text defaults — paragraph, list, rule, `small` and `address` metrics.** These set the vertical rhythm of nearly every page and none of them is expressed by a class, so nothing in [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens) can catch a change in them | `p { margin: 0 0 10px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:403-405]; `ul, ol { margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 10px }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:565-569] with `ul ul, ol ul, ul ol, ol ol { margin-bottom: 0 }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:571-576] and `.list-unstyled { padding-left: 0; list-style: none }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:578-581]; `hr { margin-top: 20px; margin-bottom: 20px; border: 0; border-top: 1px solid #eeeeee }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:385-390]; `small { font-size: 85% }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:420-422]; `address { display: block; margin-bottom: 20px; font-style: normal; line-height: 1.428571429 }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:706-711] | **Preserved** — group 1d, over a **counted** surface rather than an open-ended one: **24** paragraphs across 16 views, **10** `<hr>` elements in 10 views — one of them the rule above the footer on **every** page [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:34] — **7** `<ul>` elements, **2** `<address>` blocks [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Contact.cshtml:7], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Home/Contact.cshtml:14], and the **1** `<small>` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml:37]. The `hr` rule is the one that would be noticed first: its `#eeeeee` hairline is not the successor's default treatment, and it separates the content from the footer on all 29 views |
| **The contextual colour utilities that have a ported site**, which the successor replaces with utilities of its own carrying **different values** and `!important` | `.text-danger { color: #b94a48 }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:440-442] and `.text-success { color: #468847 }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:444-446] are pinned. `.text-info { color: #3a87ad }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:448-450] is **not**: both of its sites are in views removed with the external-login challenge surface (section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types), approved delta `D-11`), so pinning it would define a value no ported page reads | **Preserved** — group 1c, and the declarations carry `!important` to match the successor's own utilities, exactly as the two navbar backgrounds in group 6 do; without it the override loses silently. **3 ported sites of 5 source sites**, listed in [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens), and they are all message text — the error page's two lines and one success notice — so a colour change here reads as a change in severity rather than as a change in style |
| **Form element defaults that the control-geometry row does not cover — `legend` and `label`.** `.form-control` and `.btn` are pinned above, but the elements *around* a control are not, and two of them differ | `legend { display: block; width: 100%; padding: 0; margin-bottom: 20px; font-size: 21px; line-height: inherit; color: #333333; border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #e5e5e5 }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1642-1652]; `label { display: inline-block; margin-bottom: 5px; font-weight: bold }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1654-1658] | **Preserved** — group 1e. The `label` rule reaches the labels that are **not** `col-form-label` — the checkout's own — because group 7 restates padding and margins for the horizontal-form labels but not the weight, so the base weight is pinned here for both. **The placeholder colour is pinned as well**, in the same group: the source declares `color: #999999` through four vendor-prefixed selectors [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1703-1705], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1707-1709], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1711-1713], [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1715-1717], and the successor draws its placeholder from a themed colour variable instead, so the value differs. It is written as one standard `::placeholder` rule rather than four prefixed ones, since every browser in the target matrix ([06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) owns the matrix) honours the unprefixed selector. **The state it governs is not reached by any view today** — there is no `placeholder` attribute anywhere in the 29 views (`git grep -c placeholder -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views'` → no match) and the port adds none — and it is pinned regardless, because this table's job is to close the **library's own defaults** against the source's values rather than to cover only the markup that exists now: with it, all four `.form-control` states in this section (resting and focused geometry, disabled fill, placeholder colour) are pinned, and the first form field that ever carries a placeholder renders the source's grey rather than the successor's. **One neighbouring reset is deliberately not written**, with its reason: the source's `fieldset { padding: 0; margin: 0; border: 0 }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1636-1640] is matched declaration for declaration by the successor's own reset, so a copy of it would change nothing |
| **Link colour**, resting and hover | `#428bca` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:337-340]; `#2a6496` on hover and focus [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:342-346] | **Preserved** — group 2. This is not confined to one page: the catalog genre links, the administration `Edit \| Details \| Delete` links and the checkout's own links all inherit it |
| **Resting link decoration — the single largest visible difference in this table, because it applies to every link on every page.** The source draws links **undecorated** at rest and underlines them on hover and focus; the successor underlines them **at rest** and removes the underline on hover | `a { text-decoration: none }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:337-340] and `a:hover, a:focus { text-decoration: underline }` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:342-346] | **Preserved** — group 2, which sets both halves explicitly rather than only the colour. Both `outline` declarations are kept, in the source's order, because the second is honoured only by engines that recognise the keyword and the first is the fallback for the rest. **One thing about it does change and is owned**: the selector is narrowed so the ring is drawn for keyboard focus and not for a pointer click, which `:focus` alone does not distinguish — **`D-35`** of [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas), owner **Product**. | **Control geometry and type scale** — button and input padding, font size, line-height, height and corner radius | `.btn`: `6px 12px`, `14px`, `1.428571429`, radius `4px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:2000-2013]. `.form-control`: height `34px`, `6px 12px`, `14px`, `1.428571429`, colour `#555555`, border `1px solid #cccccc`, radius `4px` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Content/bootstrap.css:1719-1733] | **Preserved** — group 3, over the 11 button sites and 11 `form-control` sites of [8.5.2](#852-the-token-matrix--all-56-distinct-class-tokens).
