## 9. A namespace substitution table is not a transformation plan

This section exists because writing a `FROM → TO` import table and calling it a migration plan is the
single most likely structural error in this port, and it is a tempting one: nineteen of twenty-seven
source files carry a legacy `using` directive, so a table looks like it covers the work. **It does not.
The imports are a symptom; the file's role in the target is the plan.**

### 9.1 The census, and how to count it

**19 of the 27 `.cs` files** in the migration source carry at least one directive naming a namespace
that does not survive the port.

**A methodology note that changes the answer.** All 27 files carry a **UTF-8 byte-order mark**, so a
naive `^\s*using` match against the file decoded as UTF-8 sees the BOM as a leading character on line 1
and **misses a first-line directive**. That count returns **17**. A BOM-tolerant per-file census
returns **19**. Both commands and both results are in
[Appendix A](#appendix-a--reproducibility) so the difference is checkable rather than asserted.

**One row below states a different number from the frozen plan, and the BOM does not explain that
one**: `using System.Web;` is **11** files measured here and **10** in the plan's own census. **That is
not an open question. The plan's own §0.11.3 supplies the governing rule — "Where a deliverable and the
repository disagree, the repository wins" — so 11 is the authoritative figure**, and the table below and
every use of the count in this document state it. It is reproducible by a
BOM-insensitive command — `git grep -n 'using System.Web;' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs' | grep -v 'System\.Web\.'`
returns **11** lines, one per file — whose full output is printed beside the record in section
[9.3](#93-two-plan-correction-records-for-the-plan-owner). The BOM-sensitive form returns **9**, so it
accounts for neither figure; what accounts for the plan's 10 is a **single file omitted from its list**,
and section [9.3](#93-two-plan-correction-records-for-the-plan-owner) item 1 names it with both
commands' output. That record is a **plan-correction record notifying the plan owner** rather than a
question awaiting an answer.

Per-directive counts, BOM-tolerant, counted as **files containing the directive**:

| Directive | Files |
| --- | --- |
| `using System.Web.Mvc;` | 11 |
| `using System.Web;` | 11 |
| `using Microsoft.Owin*` | 4 |
| `using Microsoft.AspNet.Identity*` | 4 |
| `using System.Data.Entity;` | 3 |
| `using Owin;` | 3 |
| `using System.Web.Routing;` | 2 |
| `using System.Web.Optimization;` | 2 |
| `using System.Configuration;` | 1 |

Two observations from that table rather than from the total. **`using System.Web.Mvc;` reaches the
model layer** — [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/Order.cs:4] and
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/ShoppingCart.cs:5] — so the port is not confined to `Controllers/`. And
**`using System.Configuration;`** appears exactly once, at
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.App.cs:7], which is the file whose reads at [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.App.cs:23-24] are the
reason the options pattern is required (section
[3.1](#31-configuration-webconfig-becomes-appsettingsjson-read-through-iconfiguration)).

### 9.2 The four groups

Every file's disposition is set by its **role**, not by its imports, and the 27 files fall into four
groups that need four different kinds of work. The four groups are a **partition**: each of the 27
paths appears in exactly one group, each group's stated count equals the number of paths listed under
it, and `8 + 6 + 5 + 8 = 27`. The command that produces the 27 paths is in
[Appendix A](#appendix-a--reproducibility), so the partition is checkable against the checkout rather
than taken on trust.

**Group A — eight files that are deleted, so no import in them is ever rewritten.** Their `Owin`,
`Microsoft.Owin.*`, `System.Web`, `System.Web.Mvc`, `System.Web.Routing`, `System.Web.Optimization`
and `System.Configuration` directives **simply cease to exist**. A substitution table applied to this
group produces eight rewritten files that should not exist.

| File | Where its responsibility goes |
| --- | --- |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Global.asax.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Global.asax.cs:11-21] | Split across `Program.cs` and middleware, registration by registration — section [2.2](#22-the-five-application_start-registrations-do-not-share-one-fate) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Startup.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Startup.cs:4-14] | `Program.cs`; `IAppBuilder` has no successor type — section [2.3](#23-owin-startup-the-abstraction-goes-the-responsibilities-do-not) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/RouteConfig.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/RouteConfig.cs:16-20] | The endpoint registration in `Program.cs` — section [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:10] | Exception-handling middleware plus the global anti-forgery filter — sections [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order) and [7.1](#71-the-policy) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.App.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.App.cs:14-45] | Its provisioning half becomes `tools/provision-admin` (section [10](#10-administrator-provisioning-becomes-an-operator-command)); its initializer call becomes migrations (section [5](#5-schema-lifecycle-and-the-two-data-migrations)) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs:11-20] | `AddAuthentication().AddCookie()` in `Program.cs`, under the explicit policy of section [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:11-28] | **Nowhere — the responsibility ends.** There is no bundler in the target (section [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler)) |
| `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:8-13] | **Absorbed by MSBuild properties** in the SDK-style project — [04 §5.3](04-dotnet8-migration-strategy.md) |

Seven of the eight carry at least one legacy directive; `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` carries none and
is in this group because it is deleted, not because of what it imports.

**Group B — six files whose disposition is a change of identity: the file becomes a different file,
becomes two files, or sheds a responsibility into a file that does not exist yet.** The substitution
rules below do occur inside these six, but they are a detail of a larger rewrite rather than the work
itself.

- **`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs` is not import-rewritten — it is
  rewritten wholesale**, `using Microsoft.Owin.Security;`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:10] included, because `ChallengeResult`
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:394] and its `ExecuteResult` override
  [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/AccountController.cs:411] have no direct target and because its
  entire Identity surface changes shape. Section
  [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types) records the decision that **retains the
  external-login surface in dormant form** — every action and view ported, no provider registered — and
  moves the `RemoveAccountList` child action into a view component. This is the
  file [08 §4.2](08-technical-debt-register.md) sizes at 382 non-blank lines — roughly 18 percent of
  the migration source by the sizing metric — and the one part of the port with no line-for-line
  successor.

**Group C — five files where a substitution table is broadly right.** The five controllers other than
`AccountController`: `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/CheckoutController.cs`,
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/HomeController.cs`,
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/ShoppingCartController.cs`,
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreController.cs` and
`src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs`. Namespace substitution, plus the

[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs:76],
[src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs:108], eager loading, the `Dispose`

files of twenty-seven.

```text
FROM: using System.Web.Mvc;                 TO: the target's MVC namespace
FROM: using System.Data.Entity;             TO: the target's EF Core namespace
FROM: using Microsoft.AspNet.Identity[.*];  TO: the target's Identity namespaces
FROM: using System.Web;                     TO: (removed; HttpContextBase becomes the framework's context type)
FROM: using System.Web.Optimization;        TO: (no successor; the file is deleted)
FROM: using Owin; / Microsoft.Owin.*;       TO: (no successor; the file is deleted or rewritten)
Applies in full to Group C's five files only. The same substitutions occur inside Group B, but there
they are a detail of a rewrite that changes the file's identity. Groups A and D are governed by
their role, not their imports.
```

**Group D — eight files where the work is explicit mapping or annotation rather than substitution.**
This is the group a substitution table declares finished, and **seven of the eight are not**. Seven of
them carry no legacy directive at all; the exception is `Models/Artist.cs`, whose lone

here and not in Group C.

| File | Reality |
| --- | --- |

Without them the cart page breaks silently, and this file carries not one legacy import |

**So of the twenty-seven files: eight are deleted, six change identity, five take namespace
substitution plus per-site work, seven need explicit mapping or annotation, and exactly one ports
unchanged.** `8 + 6 + 5 + 7 + 1 = 27`, with no file counted twice — the last two figures are Group D's
eight split into the seven that need work and the one that does not. The import census cross-checks
the same way: the 19 files carrying at least one legacy directive are 7 of Group A's 8
(`Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` carries none), all 6 of Group B, all 5 of Group C and 1 of Group D
(`Models/Artist.cs`), and `7 + 6 + 5 + 1 = 19`. The census is how you find the files, not what you do
to them.

### 9.3 Two plan-correction records for the plan owner

Both items below are places where **this document's measurement of the checkout does not match the
frozen plan it is written against**. **Neither leaves an authority question open, because the plan
itself settles authority: its §0.11.3 states "Where a deliverable and the repository disagree, the
repository wins."** So the repository's measurement governs — inside this document and as the figure a
later reader should trust — and each item below is a **record notifying the plan owner** so the plan's
own text can be corrected at its next revision, not a question this document is waiting on. The plan
is frozen and **nothing here edits it**; its figure stands unaltered in the plan until its owner
changes it. Each item states the measured value, the plan's value, the delta, the cause, and the
disposition that follows from the rule.

**Item 1 — the authoritative `using System.Web;` file count is 11; the plan's value of 10 omits one
file.**

| Aspect | Statement |
| --- | --- |
| **Authoritative count, measured in this checkout** | **11** files — the value this document uses everywhere, reproducing command immediately below |
| **Plan value (§0.4.2 import census)** | 10 files, recorded here so the difference is on the record rather than in circulation |
| **Delta** | **Exactly one file: `src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs`** [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Models/SampleData.cs:4]. The plan's list is otherwise the measured set item for item, so the plan's 10 **is** the measured 11 minus that one entry |
| **Cause** | **A single-file omission from the plan's list, and not a method artifact.** The plan's list *includes* both files whose directive sits on line 1, [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:1] and [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:1], so it was not produced by a BOM-sensitive match: that form **misses exactly those two** and returns **9**, with a different set as well as a different total. No method that yields 10 on this checkout is known, and the difference is therefore an omission in the plan's enumeration rather than a disagreement about the source or an artifact of how it was counted. (BOM sensitivity is real and load-bearing elsewhere — it is what separates 17 from 19 in section [9.1](#91-the-census-and-how-to-count-it) — which is precisely why it should not be borrowed as the explanation here) |
| **Governing rule** | The plan's **§0.11.3**: "Where a deliverable and the repository disagree, the repository wins." The rule is the plan's own, so applying it is not a deviation from the plan — it is the plan's instruction for exactly this case |
| **Disposition** | **Settled, not pending.** 11 governs; the plan's 10 is superseded and is left untouched in the frozen plan, whose owner may fold the correction — the count and the addition of `Models/SampleData.cs` to the list — into its next revision. This entry is the notification that lets them do so. Nothing in this document's own arithmetic turns on it either way: the 19-of-27 census, the four-group partition of section [9.2](#92-the-four-groups) and the per-file dispositions are unaffected, because `Models/SampleData.cs` is in Group B on the strength of its `DropCreateDatabaseIfModelChanges` base class, not its imports |

The reproducing command is **not** `^`-anchored, because the anchor is what loses the two line-1
directives. `git grep` matches anywhere on the line, so the BOM is irrelevant to it, and the `grep -v`
filter excludes the `System.Web.*` directives that a substring match would otherwise pull in. Both
forms are printed, because the pair is the evidence that the anchored method is not the plan's:

```bash
git grep -n 'using System.Web;' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs' | grep -v 'System\.Web\.'
# -> 11 lines, one per file:
#    App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:1              Controllers/StoreManagerController.cs:6
#    App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:1              Global.asax.cs:4
#    App_Start/RouteConfig.cs:4               Models/Artist.cs:4
#    Controllers/AccountController.cs:6       Models/SampleData.cs:4
#    Controllers/HomeController.cs:3          Models/ShoppingCart.cs:4
#    Controllers/StoreController.cs:5

# The BOM-sensitive form, for contrast: 9 lines, not 10 and not 11. It drops
# App_Start/BundleConfig.cs:1 and App_Start/FilterConfig.cs:1 -- the two the plan's
# own list contains -- and it keeps Models/SampleData.cs:4, the one the plan omits.
# So its set is not the plan's set in either direction.
git grep -nE '^using System\.Web;' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs' | wc -l   # -> 9
git grep -nE '^using System\.Web;' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs' | grep -cE 'SampleData'
# -> 1   (present in the anchored 9; absent from the plan's 10)
```
