| **The page and the script, statically**, row 28 — in **both** authentication states, `28a` signed out and `28b` signed in | That the page renders **exactly one `#cart-antiforgery` carrier holding exactly one anti-forgery token** — scoped to that carrier rather than counted over the document, which carries the layout's sign-out token too whenever the caller is signed in [src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/Views/Shared/_LoginPartial.cshtml:4-6] — one removal control per cart row carrying that row's `RecordId` and the exact target path, no inline `<script>` block, and exactly one same-origin `script[src]`; and that the fetched script's text carries the exact header name `RequestVerificationToken`, the exact **scoped** token selector, and the exact element identifiers the page renders | That the script, **executed**, honours what it is spelled to do. A selector matching nothing, a handler bound before its element exists, a dependency load order leaving the library undefined, and a Content Security Policy refusal — which fails **silently to the server** ([06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)) — all satisfy row 28 and are invisible to it |

**Two mitigations are recorded, and neither is called coverage.** They are what makes accepting the limit
defensible rather than what makes it disappear:

- **The externalization the policy forces is itself asserted.** Row 28 requires **no inline `<script>`**
  and exactly one same-origin `script[src]`, which is the single change most likely to break the flow
  silently under the target's policy, and it is asserted statically on every run.
- **One functional confirmation is added to the manual review, in the same signed-off artifact.** Section
  [12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual)'s manifest carries the cart page in
  its surface list already; the reviewer additionally confirms, once per review, that removing a cart line
  updates the page and that the browser console reports no error while doing it. That is a **manual
  confirmation recorded against a named surface**, not an automated case: it is not counted in any figure
  section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) publishes, it does not run per commit, and it is stated here so
  that nobody reads it as closing entry 8.

#### The remaining limits, each with what would close it

**Two limits this table previously carried are closed, and they are recorded here rather than silently
dropped.** Entry 2 above is one, and it is the one worth reading twice: it was closed not by
acquiring a capability but by noticing that the assertion did not need one — a limit whose stated closure
mechanism is wrong stays open forever, because the thing it asks for never arrives. The other was the
same defect on two headers: an assertion can only be as tight as the value its
owner publishes, and [06 §10.2](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md) published `Strict-Transport-Security`
and `Permissions-Policy` as *descriptions*. It now publishes both as **literals** — the max-age in seconds
with `includeSubDomains` and no `preload` token, and the four `Permissions-Policy` directives in a fixed
order — so section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) row 47 and row 45 assert **byte equality** against them
instead of a directive-presence check, and neither header's value is stated twice anywhere in the corpus.
The closure is worth a sentence because it is the mechanism this section exists for: a limit recorded with
what would close it is a limit somebody can close, and this is the case where somebody did.

**Nothing else in section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) is partial, and that sentence is now true because
entries 9 to 18 exist — but the rule it closes has *three* destinations rather than two, and an earlier
form of this paragraph named only two.** The earlier form read: every behaviour, security delta, approved
delta, failure path and migration gate named anywhere in this document has a case in that matrix **or an
entry above**. It was false twice over. It was false in **fact**, because eleven live deltas had neither.
And it was **unfalsifiable in principle**, because rendered appearance is asserted by nothing in section
[12.4](#124-required-coverage) by design (entry 6 above) and is verified by the manual review of section
[12.5](#125-rendered-appearance-comparison-is-separate-and-manual) instead — so a delta whose whole content
is rendered appearance was never going to have a case *or* an entry, and a two-destination rule had no true
reading for it. **The third destination is therefore named rather than implied: a case, an entry above, or a
verification this document assigns elsewhere and identifies by owner.**

**The factual half is closed as follows.** Of the eleven live deltas that had nothing, ten are entries 9 to
18; the eleventh, `D-41`, is closed by a case rather than by an entry, on row 20 `20b`, whose anonymous cart
read after sign-out is a split oracle classified against it. Two more that were asserted by nothing
*probative* rather than by nothing at all were closed the same way rather than listed here: `D-18` on row 20
`20g`, whose second request establishes the widening a refusal alone could not, and `D-40`'s same-account
shape on row 36 `36b` — its replacement shape is entry 22.

**The principled half is closed by publishing the partition**, so the three-destination rule can be checked
from either end instead of taken. Section [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas)'s **47** live approved
deltas divide thus:

| Destination | Count | Which |

| An entry 15 to 24 above, as an open scope-change request | **10** | `D-19`, `D-20`, `D-21`, `D-29`, `D-30`, `D-38`, `D-39`, `D-40`, `D-46`, `D-48` |

in the first direction is what the `Traces to` column carries row by row; in the second it is the delta id
each entry above names; and in the third it is the owner named in the cell.

## 13. Resolution register — all 23 blockers of deliverable 12

This deliverable's acceptance criterion is that **every no-successor construct and every
differing-default item in deliverable 12 has a named resolution rather than a description.** This
section is the audit trail — the criterion is recorded in the requirement map at
[README](README.md). It
walks [12](12-migration-blockers.md)'s two groups in order. A row's *Resolution* column names the
decision; the *Where* column points at the section that specifies it.

### 13.1 Group one — no successor, or the API itself is gone (compile-time)

**Fourteen entries**, which is [12](12-migration-blockers.md)'s own compile-time count. F-12-01 is
group two's, for the reason section
[13.2](#132-group-two--what-compiling-does-not-find-nine-eight-silent-one-loud) states.

| ID | Blocker | Resolution | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F-12-02 | `System.Web.Optimization` bundling, `{version}` and glob tokens | **No bundler.** Assets move to `wwwroot`, served by static-file middleware, cache-busted by the version-appending tag helper; no JavaScript toolchain is introduced; all 11 helper call sites are rewritten; the `site.css` casing is corrected in the move | [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler) |
| F-12-03 | The Katana `IAppBuilder` abstraction and the OWIN startup attribute | **The abstraction is deleted; the responsibilities are re-registered explicitly in `Program.cs`.** Cookie authentication becomes a framework handler with **every policy value stated** rather than inherited. The external sign-in cookie's *registration call* goes with `IAppBuilder` and **nothing replaces it**: `AddIdentity` registers `IdentityConstants.ExternalScheme` regardless, but the external-login **challenge** surface that would write and read such a cookie is removed (section [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types)), so the scheme exists with no flow behind it and no cookie is ever issued under it | [2.3](#23-owin-startup-the-abstraction-goes-the-responsibilities-do-not), [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order), [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled) |
| F-12-04 | `System.Web.HttpApplication` and the `Global.asax` markup | **Disposition per responsibility, not per file.** The markup file and the base type end with no counterpart; the five registrations get five separate resolutions — deleted, replaced, moved, deleted outright, replaced | [2.1](#21-disposition-of-every-current-startup-and-configuration-file--twelve-files-four-fates), [2.2](#22-the-five-application_start-registrations-do-not-share-one-fate) |
| F-12-05 | `HandleErrorAttribute` — the entire error-handling policy | **Exception-handling middleware — not a filter — preserving the live remote behaviour and stating the rest.** No edition declares `<customErrors>`, so the effective mode is the default `RemoteOnly` and a remote unhandled exception **already** renders the generic error view; that is preserved, while the status code, the trace identifier, the logging and the environment split are stated rather than inherited. **The developer exception page is registered only when the environment is Development**, so Staging is handled like Production. The vacated global-filter slot is taken by the anti-forgery filter, and the target therefore has **one** global filter and **two** error-handling middleware stages — 2 and 3 of the pipeline | [2.4](#24-what-programcs-contains-in-order), [8.3](#83-the-five-views-that-name-legacy-types), [7.1](#71-the-policy) |

### 13.2 Group two — what compiling does not find (nine: eight silent, one loud)

Group two is defined by **what the compiler cannot catch**, not by silence: eight of its nine entries
compile and then behave differently, and **F-12-01 compiles and then stops loudly at first data access**.
[12 §4](12-migration-blockers.md) owns that taxonomy and the reason F-12-01 sits here rather than in group
one: the SQL Server Compact provider is a `providerName` string in configuration with no project
`<Reference>` anywhere, so nothing in the source binds to it and nothing reaches the compiler.

| ID | Blocker | Resolution | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F-12-01 | SQL Server Compact 4.0 as MVC 3's catalog provider — **the one loud entry in this group** | **Out of this port's scope by triage, and recorded as such rather than left blank.** MVC 3 is not the migration source; it is retained read-only. No provider is selected for it and no port of its data layer is specified — [03](03-modernization-roadmap.md) owns the triage, [10](10-build-and-deployment-requirements.md) the topology | — |
| F-12-15 | Lazy loading — **nine sites, three categories** | **Explicit eager loading or projection at each site; no proxy package.** Category (a), six sites: a1 and a2 replace `Find` with a query carrying typed `Include`s; a3 and a4 **project** instead of loading; a5 takes an `Include`; **a6 computes the order total from the album the loop already loads**. Category (b), one site: **verify the translation and add no `Include`.** Category (c), two sites: verify translation, rewrite as a grouped projection if it fails, inspect the generated SQL once. The string `Include("Albums")` stays valid | [4.6](#46-lazy-loading--a-resolution-per-site-not-a-policy) |
| F-12-16 | JSON property naming flips to camelCase | **DECIDED: annotate that ONE response model with explicit JSON property names.** The application-wide serializer policy is **not** changed; the JavaScript is **not** changed. Newtonsoft.Json's removal is an unused-dependency removal, not a serializer replacement. The coverage assertion requires on property names, not on the status code | [8.7](#87-the-json-contract--annotate-one-model-not-the-policy) |
| F-12-17 | Filesystem path casing | **Every asset reference is emitted against the actual filename during the move to `wwwroot`, and the coverage assertion requires asset availability case-sensitively.** The repository-wide audit that gates the hosting recommendation is [06](06-azure-hosting-recommendations.md)'s; [11 §3.7](11-cloud-readiness-assessment.md) is the finding of record | [8.1](#81-bundling-and-static-assets--no-bundler), [12.4](#124-required-coverage) |
| F-12-18 | The 4.8-versus-4.5 quirks-mode mismatch | **The concept ends — there is no quirks mode in the target — so the resolution is procedural and belongs to the baseline: the capture records that the source ran in 4.5 quirks mode, and any difference traceable to it is classified before it is filed as a regression.** Both misreadings are named so neither is available by default | [3.1](#31-configuration-webconfig-becomes-appsettingsjson-read-through-iconfiguration), [12.3](#123-three-problems-that-must-be-handled-explicitly) |
| F-12-19 | Connection-string resolution by convention, two conventions | **DECIDED: both contexts get an explicit `DbContextOptions` constructor and an explicit scoped registration; the two contexts REMAIN SEPARATE on ONE database, with separate migrations folders and distinct history tables.** `MusicStoreEntities` also gains an `OnModelCreating`, because the class-name convention was not its only implicit behaviour. The one-database reason is **convention, not a foreign key**, and the trade is tabulated | [4.5](#45-two-contexts-two-migration-sets-two-history-tables), [4.3](#43-the-cross-store-consistency-model) |

### 13.3 The favourable findings, and where they are used

[12 §6](12-migration-blockers.md)'s four portability findings are consumed rather than restated:
`HttpContext.Current` appearing nowhere is why the service extraction of section
[4.8](#48-the-service-layer-and-the-two-patterns-deliberately-not-adopted) is a signature change rather
than an excavation; the dead `Controller` overload being provably unreferenced is why it is deleted
there with zero call-site impact; the absence of raw SQL anywhere is why section
[4.6](#46-lazy-loading--a-resolution-per-site-not-a-policy) needs no SQL-dialect review; and the async
posture — no `.Result` and no `.Wait()` in any edition — is why the `TryUpdateModelAsync` conversion of
section [8.8](#88-the-checkout-input-model--ten-properties-not-nine) has no sync-over-async debt behind
it.

### 13.4 The three transformations no tool infers

Called out separately because each is a **required step** rather than an observation, and none of them
is produced by any automated upgrade tool:

1. **The ten-versus-nine property fact of the checkout input model.** A tool reading the `[Bind]`
   attribute produces nine. Nine compiles, binds, persists, and silently disables the promo code —
   section [8.8](#88-the-checkout-input-model--ten-properties-not-nine).
2. **The per-site lazy-loading decisions, including the one site that must *not* get an `Include`.** No
   tool can distinguish a client-side dereference from a navigation read inside a translated expression
   — section [4.6](#46-lazy-loading--a-resolution-per-site-not-a-policy).
3. **The PascalCase JSON contract between one endpoint and one script.** No tool reads a JavaScript
   property access and infers a serializer constraint on a C# model — section
   [8.7](#87-the-json-contract--annotate-one-model-not-the-policy).

A fourth is worth the same status even though it is not a code transformation: **the authoritative
schema extraction gate** (sections [5.1](#51-domain-data-migration-starts-with-schema-extraction) and
[5.5](#55-the-identity-transition--a-schema-decision-plus-a-data-migration)). Every tool will happily
generate an initial migration; none will tell you it does not match the database your data is in.

### 13.5 The 28 findings of deliverable 09 this document closes

[09 §8.3](09-security-assessment.md) states that its register's *Consumers* column "means nothing unless a
reader can check it from either end", and it assigns **28** of its findings to this document. This section
is that other end: one row per assigned finding, naming the control here that discharges it and the
evidence a reviewer reads to confirm it. **It introduces no control.** Every row points at a section this
document already specifies, and a finding whose discharge is a scope boundary rather than a control says so
in those words.

**The assignment is reproduced rather than transcribed**, because a hand-copied set is the one thing this
section cannot afford to get wrong. The *Consumers* value is the last populated cell of each register row,
and a `W`-prefixed token in it — `W7`, `W10`, `W12` — names a **workstream of
[03](03-modernization-roadmap.md)**, not a deliverable, so the match is on the deliverable number alone and
never on a substring:

```bash
# The set 09 assigns to this document, from 09's own register.
awk -F'|' '/^\| F-09-/ { c=$(NF-1); if (c ~ /(^|[^0-9])05([^0-9]|$)/) n++ } END { print n }' \
  docs/modernization/09-security-assessment.md
# 28

# The set this document carries, from this end.
grep -o 'F-09-[0-9][0-9]' docs/modernization/05-aspnet-core-migration-approach.md | sort -u | wc -l
# 28 - the two sets are equal, which is the property 09 §8.3 asks for
```

**Ten of the 28 already carried a named discharge in the body**, cited at the point the control is
specified: F-09-02, F-09-03, F-09-05, F-09-08, F-09-10, F-09-25, F-09-26, F-09-27, F-09-28 and F-09-37.
The other eighteen were discharged by a control that named no finding — the control existed and the trail
did not, which is precisely the state a one-directional index hides. The table carries all 28 so the check
is one lookup rather than a search.

**Two rows are closed by a scope boundary together with a target control, and neither implies a port.**
F-09-11 and F-09-17 are findings against MVC 4 and MVC 3, and neither edition is a migration source
(section [13.1](#131-group-one--no-successor-or-the-api-itself-is-gone-compile-time), F-12-01). What this
document owes them is not a repair of the older editions but a target that cannot reproduce the defect,
plus a statement of which deliverable owns the older edition's own disposition.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| F-09-02 | The whole authentication policy is inherited from framework defaults and stated nowhere | **A twenty-five-row policy table with every row labelled** *preserved*, *deliberate hardening* or *deliberate change*, and the framework default named in the row wherever the target differs from it | [6.1](#61-the-policy-table-every-row-labelled); [11.5](#115-the-full-set-of-approved-deltas) approved delta `D-10`; coverage rows 48-52, 70, 71 |

| F-09-17 | Every account the edition registers is created with the same two hard-coded password-recovery literals | **Scope boundary plus control.** The target has no knowledge-based recovery anywhere to hold such a literal: the account surface is a closed action map with no recovery action, and the Identity migration's **column-origin table enumerates every target column** and contains neither a question nor an answer. Nor can such columns be carried silently — a non-empty discovered source table has exactly two permitted dispositions, a target mapping or an owner-approved retirement, and until one is recorded the load is blocked. MVC 3's own store is not an extraction source, and [10](10-build-and-deployment-requirements.md) owns its host verification | [6.4](#64-the-account-surface--authorization-map-redirect-safety-and-error-paths), [5.5](#55-the-identity-transition--a-schema-decision-plus-a-data-migration)'s column-origin and table-disposition rules; coverage row 57 |

Coverage row 38 asserts that a caller cannot read or mutate another cart's record; **five of the provenance behaviours are asserted by no row, and section [12.11](#1211-coverage-limits-and-the-scope-change-requests) entry 13 records that with what closing it would cost** rather than letting row 19 be read as covering them |

One generic message answers every credential failure | [4.3](#43-the-cross-store-consistency-model), [6.4](#64-the-account-surface--authorization-map-redirect-safety-and-error-paths). Coverage row 18 case `18c` asserts the **content** half byte-for-byte, for a wrong password and for a user name held by no account. **The timing half is specified in [4.3](#43-the-cross-store-consistency-model) — per-sample account provisioning and the fixture's rate-limit widening — and section [12.4](#124-required-coverage) carries no numbered row that measures it**, which is stated here rather than left for a reader to discover from the absence |

**What this table is not.** It is not a second register: [09](09-security-assessment.md) owns every one of
these findings, its severities and its current-state evidence, and a row here that disagreed with it would
be a defect in this document rather than a second opinion. And it is not a completeness claim about
[12.4](#124-required-coverage) — the *Evidence* column names the rows that exist, and where a control is
specified without a numbered row measuring it, the row above says so in place of citing one.

## 14. Roll-up

### 14.1 The approach in eleven statements

1. **One composition root.** Twelve startup and configuration files collapse into `Program.cs` plus
   Razor and MSBuild conventions, with four different fates and no file's fate inferred from its
   imports.
2. **Nothing is applied at startup that changes a schema.** Migrations, seeding and administrator
   provisioning all leave the web application.
3. **Two contexts, one database, separate migration sets and history tables in one project.** The
   stores are coupled by convention, not by a foreign key; the consistency model is an explicit
   five-step ordering whose residual window is **not claimed closed** — the cart key is derived from
   the authenticated principal so no unauthenticated request can resolve it, and the next successful
   sign-in absorbs the reassignment idempotently. **And the cart itself is one concurrency domain, not
   four independent writers**: a change-detection witness compared in every predicate; **every mutation a single token-conditional statement
   whose affected-row count is asserted to be exactly one**, with the decrement-versus-delete decision
   re-taken on a fresh value rather than tested and then acted on; **the quantity bound inside that same
   statement, with a `CHECK` constraint behind it**; **a durable operation ledger** so a lost
   acknowledgement cannot double-apply; a checkout delete keyed on the rows it actually read; and a
   **discoverable, destination-indexed handoff** for the retired anonymous id — because a unique index
   constrains a pair and serializes nothing, and both of those columns have to be given a bounded length
   before any index over them can exist at all.
4. **Every silent-failure site is named individually.** Nine lazy-loading sites in three categories,
   one JSON contract, two `Dispose` overrides, one connection convention — resolved per site, not by
   policy.
5. **Query shape is a decision, not an afterthought.** Both unbounded list endpoints get a total
   ordering, a projection, a stated page size and a paging mechanism; the two — and only two —
   every-page components get a fixed query budget; the order write reads every price once; **the one
   browse predicate that is not a key gets a contract with two extraction-selected branches, neither of
   which loses a genre row**; and the provider carries an explicit retry, timeout, cancellation and async
   policy that the file-attached source never needed — **per command *and* per unit of work**, because
   the two differ by a product and only the second bounds a request.
6. **Data migration begins with a complete extraction and a schema diff that must pass**, and is
   performed by a named executor with defined idempotence, checkpointing and exit codes — **a run
   identity that is a parent row plus one independently fingerprinted row per store, and a durable
   lineage table the reconciling and sealing processes read rather than re-derive**, because they are
   separate processes from the load. An initial
   migration creates tables; it does not move rows and it cannot be trusted to match. **Acceptance is
   keyed sets and digests, not counts** — over a projection declared per class, so a target-only column
   is asserted against a named origin instead of quietly dropped from the comparison.
7. **The Identity transition preserves usernames as an invariant**, treats id preservation as an
   explicit convenience, aborts on normalized **username** and **role-name** collisions before writing,
   dispositions every table rather than only the users, verifies rather than assumes the
   password-hash format, and **configures the normalized columns' collation rather than inheriting one** —
   verified by target-side introspection, because those columns do not exist in the source for an
   extraction to report on.
8. **Policy is stated, not inherited.** Every authentication, cookie, password and lockout value is set
   explicitly and labelled preserved or hardening — including the two places this document deliberately
   declines to harden.
9. **Anti-forgery is global by default**, one state-changing `GET` becomes a `POST`, and the one
   form-less AJAX post gets a named header contract with three token tests.
10. **A single cutover, with two accepted costs and a rollback plan that states them in both
    directions.**
11. **Tests precede the port**, HTTP-level and semantic, against a two-database legacy baseline and a
    disposable SQL Server for the target — with rendered-appearance review scoped separately and
    manually.

### 14.2 What this document creates: nothing, and what the assessment nonetheless wrote

No **tracked** repository file was created, modified or deleted in producing it, other than this file,
and every target artifact named above is a specification for a separately approved implementation
phase. The qualifier is load-bearing: the assessment's restores and builds ran against this checkout
and left **eight ignored trees** in it — the `bin` and `obj` pairs of the three edition projects plus a
restored `packages` tree under `src/MVC4` and another under `src/MVC5` — which were removed, and whose
absence was then verified rather than assumed. Section
[1.4](#14-the-no-modification-constraint-and-the-boundary-that-makes-this-document-possible) carries
that account with the figures, and [10 §1.4](10-build-and-deployment-requirements.md) owns it.

So the closing check is the four-command one of section
[1.4](#14-the-no-modification-constraint-and-the-boundary-that-makes-this-document-possible), and it is
four rather than one because all eight trees were ignored on this checkout — `obj` by `[Oo]bj/`
[.gitignore:1], `bin` by `[Bb]in/` [.gitignore:2], and the two nested `packages` trees by `Packages/`
[.gitignore:33] rather than by the root-anchored `packages/*` [.gitignore:15], as section
[1.4](#14-the-no-modification-constraint-and-the-boundary-that-makes-this-document-possible) records
with its case dependency — and neither a bare status nor a tracked diff can see an ignored path:
`git diff --name-status ea2552d..HEAD` returns exactly thirteen `A`
rows, all under `docs/modernization/`, with no `M` or `D` row and no path outside it; and on a clean
checkout of that commit `git status --porcelain` is **empty**,
`git status --porcelain --ignored` is **empty** with no `!!` row, and `git clean -ndX` **lists
nothing**.

## Appendix A — Reproducibility

Every repository-wide claim in this document was produced by one of the commands below, run against
this checkout. They are collected here so each is re-runnable rather than merely cited.

```bash
# --- Section 1.3  The citation contract, checked mechanically -----------------
# ONE form, and exactly one: the full form [<path>:<locator>], carried at every
# occurrence. This check is nevertheless written to DETECT the locator-only
# form [:<locator>] - which would inherit the path of the nearest preceding
# full citation INSIDE THE SAME BLOCK, one table cell, one list item or one
# paragraph - because a check that cannot see the defect cannot prove its
# absence. It segments the document into those blocks, resolves any such
# citation against its block antecedent, and reports the count of them, any
# citation with no antecedent, any locator outside the cited file, and any
# path-only citation. The document is compliant when the continuation and
# path-only counts are both 0. chr(96)*3 is the code-fence marker, spelled
# that way so this block can live inside a fence itself.
python - <<'PY'
import re, os
doc   = "docs/modernization/05-aspnet-core-migration-approach.md"
FENCE = chr(96) * 3
full  = re.compile(r"\[([^\]\s]+):((?:\d+(?:-\d+)?)(?:\s*,\s*\d+(?:-\d+)?)*|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*(?:\s*,\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)*)\](?!\()")
pathonly = re.compile(r"\[((?:src|docs|tools)/[^\]\s]+?\.[A-Za-z0-9]+)\](?!\()")
short = re.compile(r"\[:\s*(\d+(?:-\d+)?(?:\s*,\s*:?\s*\d+(?:-\d+)?)*)\]")
lens  = {}
def flen(p):
    if p not in lens:
        lens[p] = len(open(p, "rb").read().splitlines()) if os.path.exists(p) else -1
    return lens[p]
def locok(loc, n):
    for part in loc.split(","):
        q = part.strip().lstrip(":").strip()
        if not q[:1].isdigit():
            continue                      # object locator: existence is the check
        a, _, b = q.partition("-")
        a, b = int(a), int(b or a)
        if not (1 <= a <= b <= n):
            return False
    return True
blocks, cur, infence = [], None, 0
for ln in open(doc, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines():
    t = ln.lstrip()
    if t.startswith(FENCE):
        cur = None; infence ^= 1; continue
    if infence: continue
    if t == "" or re.match(r"#{1,6}\s", t):
        cur = None; continue
    if t.startswith("|"):
        cur = None
        for cell in re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", ln):
            if cell.strip(): blocks.append(cell)
        continue
    if re.match(r"([-*+]\s|\d+\.\s)", t):
        cur = [ln]; blocks.append(cur); continue
    if cur is None:
        cur = [ln]; blocks.append(cur)
    else:
        cur.append(ln)
nfull = nshort = npath = lead = badinh = badfull = 0
paths = set()
for b in blocks:
    txt = b if isinstance(b, str) else " ".join(b)
    ev = ([(m.start(), "f", m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(0)) for m in full.finditer(txt)]
        + [(m.start(), "p", m.group(1), None,      m.group(0)) for m in pathonly.finditer(txt)]
        + [(m.start(), "s", None,       m.group(1), m.group(0)) for m in short.finditer(txt)])
    anchor = None
    for _, k, p, loc, raw in sorted(ev):
        if k == "f":
            nfull += 1; anchor = p; paths.add(p)
            if not locok(loc, flen(p)): badfull += 1; print("BADFULL", raw)
        elif k == "p":
            npath += 1; anchor = p; paths.add(p); print("PATHONLY", raw)
        else:
            nshort += 1
            if anchor is None: lead += 1; print("NO-ANTECEDENT", raw)
            elif not locok(loc, flen(anchor)): badinh += 1; print("OUT-OF-RANGE", raw, "->", anchor)
missing = sorted(p for p in paths if flen(p) < 0)
print("blocks=%d full=%d continuation=%d path-only=%d no-antecedent=%d "
      "continuation-out-of-range=%d full-bad-locator=%d cited-paths=%d unresolved-paths=%d"
      % (len(blocks), nfull, nshort, npath, lead, badinh, badfull, len(paths), len(missing)))
PY
# -> full=1737 shorthand=0 path-only=0 bare-filename=0 unresolved=0

# --- Section 2.2  There is no Areas folder, so RegisterAllAreas() is dead ------
git ls-files | grep -c 'Areas/'                                   # -> 0

# --- Section 3.2  The XDT transforms: 15 occurrences, 3 of them live ----------
# A plain grep counts commented template text too, which is 12 of the 15.
# Strip XML comments first, then count what remains, per file.
python - <<'PY'
import subprocess, re
files = subprocess.run(['git','ls-files','*Web.Debug.config','*Web.Release.config'],
                       capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
tot = live = 0
for f in files:
    s = open(f, encoding='utf-8-sig').read()
    stripped = re.sub(r'<!--.*?-->', '', s, flags=re.S)
    n, m = len(re.findall(r'xdt:Transform', s)), len(re.findall(r'xdt:Transform', stripped))
    tot += n; live += m
    print('%-58s total=%d live=%d' % (f, n, m))
print('TOTAL=%d LIVE=%d' % (tot, live))
PY

#    every Web.Debug.config      total=2 live=0
#    every Web.Release.config    total=3 live=1   (the compilation transform, line 18)

done

# --- Section 8.3  No live <customErrors> element in any tracked configuration --
# The taxonomy matters, because a single "occurrences" number invites the wrong
# reading. All of it sits in the six XDT files; the other nine tracked .config
# files mention customErrors nowhere.
python - <<'PY'
import subprocess, re
files = [f for f in subprocess.run(['git','ls-files','*.config'],
         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split() if '/packages/' not in f]
word = pre = close = live = 0
for f in files:
    s = open(f, encoding='utf-8-sig').read()
    stripped = re.sub(r'<!--.*?-->', '', s, flags=re.S)
    word  += len(re.findall(r'customErrors', s))
    pre   += len(re.findall(r'<customErrors', s))
    close += len(re.findall(r'</customErrors', s))
    live  += len(re.findall(r'<customErrors', stripped))
print('files=%d word=%d "<customErrors"=%d "</customErrors>"=%d live=%d'
      % (len(files), word, pre, close, live))
PY

# --- Section 9.1  The legacy-directive census: 19 of 27, not 17 ---------------
python - <<'PY'
import subprocess, re
files = subprocess.run(['git','ls-files','src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs'],
                       capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
LEG = re.compile(r'^\s*using\s+(System\.Web|System\.Data\.Entity|System\.Configuration'
                 r'|Owin|Microsoft\.Owin|Microsoft\.AspNet\.Identity)\b')
naive = tol = boms = 0; without = []
for f in files:
    raw = open(f, 'rb').read()
    boms += raw[:3] == b'\xef\xbb\xbf'
    n = any(LEG.match(l) for l in raw.decode('utf-8').splitlines())        # BOM breaks line 1
    t = any(LEG.match(l) for l in raw.decode('utf-8-sig').splitlines())    # BOM stripped
    naive += n; tol += t
    if not t: without.append(f.split('MvcMusicStore/')[-1])
print('files=%d  utf8-BOM=%d  naive=%d  bom_tolerant=%d' % (len(files), boms, naive, tol))
print('the 8 with no legacy directive:'); [print('  ', w) for w in without]
PY

# Per-directive file counts, same BOM-tolerant method:

#    System.Data.Entity 3 | Owin 3 | System.Web.Routing 2 | System.Web.Optimization 2

# 11 less the two files whose directive is line 1, where ^ cannot match past a UTF-8 BOM.
git grep -n 'using System.Web;' -- 'src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/*.cs' | grep -v 'System\.Web\.'

# --- Sections 1.4 / 14.2  The constraint this work was held to ----------------
# Four commands, not one, and they only mean anything together. Restores and
# builds ran against this checkout during the assessment and left eight ignored
# trees in it (527 files, 114,310,394 bytes); all eight were removed. All eight
# were ignored here, so the two commands a repository-state claim is usually
# rested on -- bare porcelain and the tracked diff -- reported a clean tree for
# the whole period those trees existed, and the two ignore-aware lines below are
# the ones that carry the claim. Which rule matched which path, per path:
git check-ignore --no-index -v src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/obj/x \
                               src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/bin/x src/MVC5/packages/x
# -> .gitignore:1:[Oo]bj/     src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/obj/x
#    .gitignore:2:[Bb]in/     src/MVC5/MvcMusicStore/bin/x
#    .gitignore:33:Packages/  src/MVC5/packages/x
# --no-index makes the answer independent of tracking state. The three paths above
# are untracked, so the plain form reports the same rules; a TRACKED path is the
# case that differs -- plain check-ignore exits 1 for it with no output, because
# tracked files are not ignored, which is a different question from whether a rule
# matches. Verified both ways on a tracked path inside one of those trees:
git check-ignore -v src/MVC4/MvcMusicStore/packages/repositories.config
# -> no output, exit 1  (tracked: suppressed, and no rule reported)
git check-ignore --no-index -v src/MVC4/MvcMusicStore/packages/repositories.config
# -> .gitignore:33:Packages/  src/MVC4/MvcMusicStore/packages/repositories.config
# The nested packages trees are matched by Packages/ (.gitignore:33), which has no
# interior separator and so matches at any depth, and NOT by packages/*
# (.gitignore:15), which has one and is therefore anchored to the repository root.
# The match is also case-dependent: it holds because core.ignorecase is true here.
git config core.ignorecase                                    # -> true
git -c core.ignorecase=false check-ignore --no-index -v src/MVC4/packages/x
# -> no output, exit 1: on a case-sensitive filesystem no rule ignores that tree
```
